podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2k, $20k, and $200k using her proven formula.

Hello, hello, hello. Hi everybody. Thanks for being with me here today, those of you that joined. My name is Stacey Boehman.

This will be a weird live if you’re just joining me for the first time, if you just found me and don’t know who I am. This will be a weird live. But I help life coaches make money in my 2k for 2k, 200k Mastermind, and 2 Million Dollar Group programs that I have been running for the last eight years. I’ve been in business for 10 years, but I was a general life coach before that. And actually, last year was my 10th year in business, and so I’ve been celebrating a lot of the wisdom that I’ve learned over the last 10 years.

I’m going to talk about a lot of tools at my disposal that helped with my, the recent obstacle I have faced in this live stream. And I’m going to put this on my Make Money as a Life Coach podcast because I really think this is a message everyone needs to hear, and I love being able to come to you all live and deliver this message kind of off the cuff.

And if you listened to this on the podcast and you’re loving the podcast, leave me a review. I would love to hear your thoughts. Okay, are y’all ready?

So after 10 years of business and eight years selling the same three offers essentially, I, on Monday, launched a brand new offer that I have been conceptualizing in my head for two years and that I spent the last two months working very hard on for with my entire team. Like all of our resources, other than managing our other programs going into this new offer. It was much anticipated. I had I have nurtured it very well. I have prepared people for it coming.

I’ve been super clear in my communications. This is one thing I excel at, just rolling things out and being very clear and letting people know what’s happening in my business when something new comes. Everything was prepared and ready to go, and I have been so proud of everything that I have created. I think my sales page is fire. And I love my offer. I am very sold on the Entrepreneur Coach Membership. And we launched it on Monday with a live stream, to which we had over 250 people on the entire time. So it was probably more because people go in and out, and it was a huge success.

Everyone was commenting. I told them to comment EC. You can do the same if you want the link to sign up or for more information on it, and people were commenting like crazy. People were trying to buy immediately. They said this was the thing they hoped that I was doing and that they’ve been waiting for me to do, and the excitement and the energy was literally more than I could have imagined and anticipated. And the entire time I was like, oh my god, this is exactly what it feels like to fulfill a dream. It is happening.

I want you to imagine, not all of you sell on webinars, but I want you to imagine that you bust your ass to create a webinar that you are so proud of. You put so much time and energy into it. You have hundreds of people on that webinar. You are nailing your sales pitch. You are sold on your offer. Your people are so excited. They are telling you they can’t wait to buy. That they’re running to buy right now. And then they start telling you that they’re trying to buy and can’t.

And you’re like, that’s weird. And then some people are like, oh, I think I can buy it. And you’re like, and someone’s like, it worked for me. And then people are like, it’s not working for me, it’s not working for me, it’s not working for me. And honestly, in business, I’ve been in business for 10 years, especially if you have a team, things happen, things don’t work. I’ve had things been that we tested the night before and then suddenly they don’t work the next morning.

Sometimes we can explain it, and we’re like, oh, it’s because this one little thing happened that was out of the sequence of things, and we didn’t realize it was going to create this chain of events.

And sometimes it’s like this was completely out of our control. So I got off my live stream because enough people were saying it wasn’t working that I was like, something’s wrong. And so I immediately slacked my team and I’m like, what’s going on, guys? Everyone was saying it wasn’t working. They weren’t getting theManychat link. They weren’t able to pull up the sales page. If they were able to pull up the sales page, they weren’t able to buy. What’s happening?

And at first my team had a theory, and then that ended up not being the thing, but ultimately what ended up happening, my team sent me the verbage and now I they texted it to me. I don’t have it on here. But essentially, our customer, like our email provider, we use Ontraport. It’s a CRM where all of our customer information is housed and it is linked to everything that we deliver. So when you sign up for the Entrepreneur Coach Membership and you receive a confirmation email, that happens because of Ontraport.

When you click the monthly option for the membership and you pay money, and then you get the confirmation email through Ontraport. Everything access to the member portal, through Ontraport. Everything is through Ontraport. They had what I if I can remember correctly, a DDoS attack on their external systems, and it was not just me that went down. It was hundreds of businesses. I have a colleague who also operates on Ontraport, and she was in the last two days of her launch, and suddenly people could not buy in when urgency is the highest and everyone’s trying to get in so they don’t miss out.

So the two points in your launch where things would be at an all-time high for purchases are the beginning and the end. No one could sign up. And like other tech outages that have happened over the 10 years in my business, this one was not resolved quickly or smoothly. So there have been things that weren’t working with Ontraport, like it’s had latency issues where it just delivers late. And those things have been resolved in a few hours.

This took days. And we are just now getting a confirmation that everything is working again and fully functional from Ontraport. But yesterday, we were also told that things were working and fully functional, and we emailed out our customers that things were working, and they were working, and then 15 minutes later they were not working.

And I put myself as a CEO, whenever we have a sales sequence, I put myself or my team puts me and my emails into the customer sequence. So I receive everything the customer receives from the marketing perspective, and then once they’ve purchased from the delivery perspective.

It was a disaster in my inbox. I went live at 10:00 a.m. to announce my offer, and I got the reminder for that live stream at 6:00 p.m. that day. Eight hours after the live was over. Emails came in and then came in again. Emails came that said things were working and then things weren’t working and then, oh, things are working again and oh, things aren’t working again. Disaster.

For someone who, even though this was completely out of our control, and there was nothing that we could do as far as, like, any of those things. For someone whose value is well planned and highly executed, this was not fun for me. That’s all I can say. This was not fun for me. I had to hold a lot of anxiety and a lot of frustration and a lot of things, a lot of uncomfortable emotions, like humiliation, embarrassment, like all the things.

So I want to walk you through because I think this could be, I have a belief in my business. I have a one-sentence that I have a couple of sentences. I’ve developed them over the years that I say to myself in good times and bad times. So one of them is this is just the beginning. And I say this to myself for everything. I make it fit for everything. I challenge myself to make the sentence fit for everything.

So I always tell my people they do webinars and they exhaust themselves doing the webinars and they tell themselves it’s the end of the selling and I tell them, no, it’s the beginning. So one of the things I’ve told myself is this is just the beginning.

It calms me down, it gears me up, it gets me grounded to do the work. Another sentence I have as an entrepreneur that is really powerful for me is I go first. I go often. I go with purpose. Which means I ask of myself to do things a hundred times prior to asking my client to do it once. I ask myself to do it a hundred times bigger than I’ll ask my clients to do it. So I lead the way. I act and show up empowering myself as a leader often and I do it with the purpose of knowing I will lead my people through it. And so that’s really powerful for me.

So the moment this happened, I knew this was always supposed to happen because the thing that I’m selling is a membership on entrepreneurial mindset and stamina and capacity and strength to do hard things because that’s what entrepreneurship is. And to do it aligned with coaching values and our whys and our mission as coaches, and to combine those two things. So I knew right away, I must lead on this. I have to go first here in this moment. That one day, I just imagined when this happened, I closed my eyes, and I breathed in, and I imagined that one day this is going to happen to one of my 2 Million Dollar Group students.

They’re going to have a multi-million dollar launch on the line, and something like this is going to happen. And if you have ever had millions of dollars on the line, or even for you thousands of dollars on the line, that is holding a level of pressure and uncertainty that most people are not willing to hold, and the mistakes can be very pricey. I remember my team actually made an error. We had a miscommunication last year, and it cost my company $200,000. And I remember at the time not feeling happy.

That is all I will say. Not feeling happy. But I had this thought, I go first, I go often, I go with purpose. And I really believe there is no way to grow into the millions and multi-millions of dollars of revenue without making hundreds of thousands of dollars of mistakes. That’s just the way it is. You’re going to lose money along the way, and that is part of the risk of entrepreneurship, and it’s part of entrepreneurship in general. Like you have to learn as you go. There’s no way to do it perfectly.

So you have to be willing to risk work and energy and time and emotional investment and time investment, financial investment, resource investment. You have to be willing to risk that, and you will risk it. That is part of entrepreneurship. There’s no shortcut. No matter how many mentors you have and how much you invest, you can’t pay your way out of failure and learning so that you gather wisdom. And one of the things as you ascend in wealth that you have like you can’t put money in the stock market if you’re not willing to lose it, for example.

One of the things when I started heavily investing in the stock market that our portfolio advisor, financial advisor said is like, we need to set up your portfolio based on your level of risk that you’re willing to take. And he said, so if you put this money in and tomorrow you were to lose half of it, would you be able to handle the emotional reaction to that? And would you be able to keep your money in and not panic and fight or flight and pull it out?

The same is true for entrepreneurship. Can you recognize that you just lost hundreds of thousands of dollars and instead of folding and closing up and dying of humiliation and disappointment and reducing yourself to a puddle of tears, can you pick yourself up, tell yourself this is just the beginning and keep going?

That is what is required. It’s such a big ask. It is managing an emotional, a nervous system response. It’s managing, it’s pulling up resilience, it’s expanding capacity to hold problems and things that happen that can cost you hundreds of thousands or even millions of dollars. I have also made million-dollar mistakes in my business. I’ve sold $45 million of coaching. I made a mistake three years ago that cost me $800,000. So I have developed, now keep in mind, over 10 years, I’ve grown my net worth by millions of dollars.

So it’s not that entrepreneurship is so risky that it will financially devastate you for life if you are investing and have a really good mindset and you’re developing your mindset along the way, but it is that you will make mistakes. You will make tax mistakes, you will make investment mistakes. That is part of going first, especially as a coach, but as an entrepreneur, going first, going often, and going with purpose, and not always having a direct road map, and not always being able to see the things in front of you or control them. And in this case, this was out of my control.

I thought it was perfect that this happened to me because I am literally going to build up my students when they join me in this membership, I’m going to build their capacity for failure, their capacity for risk, their mindset as an entrepreneur to handle these big moments, their stamina, their work ethic, their empowerment for everything that comes their way and their balance to be able to do it all and love their business and love their life. That is the goal. I do love my business. I do love my life. I just got off a call with some colleagues and a coach that I just hired and she was like, you are a completely different person than a few years ago. Like you look amazing.

And I’m like, yeah, I feel amazing. I’m enjoying my business. I love my business. I love my life. Even when really hard things happen and we lose lots of money. And I don’t know, people are telling me, oh, you’ll, you know, people are still going to sign up, but did we lose hundreds of people’s enthusiasm and the height of them getting their credit cards out of their purses and thinking about it and making that and signing up right then and there? Yeah, we lost that.

So instead of having the, you know, the wind at our back, we’ve got it in our face a little bit. That’s how you would feel, too, if you did a webinar and 250 people wanted to buy from you and then couldn’t for two days. You would also feel like the wind is in your face. It’s okay to feel that way. That’s a natural, normal human response. But here’s what I did about it. The very first thing, when this happened, I got on a team meeting right away. It was already scheduled, so I got on. My team’s informing me of what happened, and I took a deep breath.

In fact, I joked with them. I was like, you know how, like, you breathe into a paper bag? I was like, well, also if you just like put your, I put both hands on my face, and I’m like, if you, like you can do that with your hands. Like you can breathe through a paper bag in your hands. I also joked with them that I use the F word a lot to let the emotion out of my body. And so I need to say fuck a lot of times before the emotion leaves my body. That is true for me. My husband does not love that about me, but I express emotion. I’m an emotional authority in the human design, and I express my emotions through my thoughts.

But after that little moment to like have my reaction, I found an empowering thought and that is what you must do. It doesn’t have to be a good thought, it has to be an empowering one. And I taught this in an entrepreneur series course last year, that I asked my students, how empowering thoughts feel? I said, what’s the like, think about what emotions specifically empowers you? Like, what’s the emotion that gets you into empowerment, and how does that feel?

And so many people told me these amazing emotions that feel really great, and I said, no, that’s how you feel after you’ve empowered yourself. You’ve skipped an emotion. So, for example, they would tell me pride, and I’m like, no, pride happens after you empower yourself. You’re proud of how you handled it. The actual emotion that gets you into empowerment doesn’t always feel good. Right? Sometimes it’s courage. I can handle this. For me, one of them was determination. I will fight hard for this. I was prepared to do it. I’m always prepared to do it. I’m not above it. I’m not entitled to not doing it.

This is part of entrepreneurship. Let’s fucking go. I will fight for this. I know that about myself. I am resilient. But that takes like that, like, knowing you’re about to have to produce a fight when you expected to be celebrating and toasting champagne, that doesn’t feel the best. And it’s still true. It’s empowering, but it doesn’t always feel like rainbows and daisies and butterflies. So that was one thought that I found, is I’m going to fight for this. I know that about myself. I’m willing to do it. I’m not entitled to not do it.

I also believe truly that the people who were going to sign up for this membership cannot, like their signing up and doing this work for me, cannot be dependent on a two-day delay. Otherwise, they were not as invested as they thought. The people who are truly invested will fight to pay. I just had the same thing. I couldn’t pay my new coach, and I spent like days trying to figure out how to get her the money so that we could coach. I put a lot of energy as the client into making sure that happened, and I got in, and I was able to have my first call today.

So I believe that my ideal best clients for this room, who are excited about this room, will get in this room regardless of whether there was a two-day delay. I think about it like Taylor Swift concert tickets. If it sold out when she did like her in, you know, when you, I think there was like maybe a lottery or something. I wasn’t super a fan when she, like I didn’t really follow her when she was doing her Eras Tour, but I know they were really hard to get, and then you had to get them on the aftermarket. But the people that were her true fans that really wanted to be at that concert, paid triple the amount of money that they would have had to pay on the aftermarket to make sure they were in that room. They figured it out. My sister was one of them who took her daughter, and totally worth it.

So that was a thought I chose, is we I can’t lose the people that were meant to be in this room over a two-day lag. If they’re meant to be in this room, they’re going to get themselves in this room. That allowed me to breathe and be like, nothing has gone wrong. It’s okay. I mean, things have gone wrong, but in the scheme of things, right? Nothing is unfixable. Nothing has been broken that can’t be put back together.

Like that energy, I needed that energy. Then, me and my team really went to assess the problem, like the scope of the problem. One of the things I asked my team is, tell me every point of the customer’s journey, every point that is impacted from the moment I told them to comment EC, and that the Manychat would send them a link to sign up. Tell me every moment that is impacted by this Ontraport outage. I want to know how deep it is, and I want to know why it’s impacted.

So I want to know the scope of it so I can explain it to other people. So I understand what we could do to try to fix it. I could find workarounds. I have to understand the problem. So we had to find the root of the problem. Then we had to look at all the possible solutions and find which ones could be the simplest and most effective to implement immediately. So one of the problems was that emails weren’t going out or they were going out with dramatic lags and made no sense in the order that they were landing in inboxes.

So one of the things I said is if we don’t get this fixed quickly, I’m going to create a broadcast channel because I have to have a way to communicate with people effectively. That has to happen. So we can’t get emails up and going, like that’s got to be our thing that we do for emails. They ended up having that mostly fixed by yesterday afternoon, so a day and a half.

One of the other things I thought about is if they can’t get the pay form up, I was like, there’s got to be a way for us to like do an invoice payment and then, you know, get the person signed up, get them into the member portal, and then when the payment actually comes up, we can actually set them up on the membership, like when it works out.

But like we could get that first payment manually if we had to, if we get up to the date of, you know, like depending on how long this takes, if we’re getting close to the date of the first call, which is January 20th, then we might have to implement something like that and it could take us days and days and all manpower, but that might be what we have to do is we’re like, we’re not pushing back because I have content planned for the whole 12 months and we’ve got to figure this out. We’re not leaving people behind. And I’ve done like old school invoices before, so I’m like, this is surely we can do this.

So my team started researching different ways that we could take payment that weren’t attached to Ontraport and then ways that we could manually add people into the system to make sure they got into the member portal and everything that they needed. And so that we started creating plans. The entire time my brain is human and it wanted to fight this. It wanted to like melt into a puddle and cry. It wanted to be exasperated. It wanted to pity myself. It wanted to have a victim mindset and be like, this only happens to me, and of course, it happened to me and why me?

And every time my brain said, why me? I made myself answer it. Why me? Because you go first, you go often, you go with purpose. Why me? Because this is the point of what you want to teach people in the membership. Why me? So that you have the answer the next time this happens to anyone. Why me? So that you prove, like I really believe this, every time I make a goal to radically jump in wealth or revenue or, you know, do something big, I always believe that the universe sends me obstacles, my own personalized obstacle course so that I can develop the muscles I need to develop to become the person who’s capable of achieving the goal that I want to achieve.

And I have a big three-year plan. And so I was like, oh, I’m supposed to be the version of me who handles this really well with a lot of grace and a lot of power because I am proving that the goal that I want, I am the person capable of creating it. This is the first test. The universe is sending it to me and it’s pass or fail. Winning or learning. And so I decided every time why me, why me, here’s the answer, here’s the answer, here’s the answer. I came up with like 30 answers for “why me?”

Yeah, I’m going to extract value. I’m going to become more valuable because of this. We will now know that this is a possibility in the future. We’re now going to have backup plans in the future. Maybe we need to decide to not be on Ontraport anymore. Is this common? Like, let’s investigate this. What would it take to change? Like, why me? Why me? Why me? Here are the answers to why me that are empowering. Then I am human. So I also took time to process disappointment and anger and frustration. To say my fucks.

Yesterday, I had worked for six hours and my husband could tell that I was like, this is not like… emotionally exhausting maybe isn’t the right word, but it is requiring like this work requires a lot of emotional output, like a lot of emotional output. And my husband could see that I was, I needed a break and he offered me such a beautiful thing. He said, why don’t you go pick up Jackson from school and go take him to the zoo. It’s 57 degrees outside and tomorrow it’s going to snow and be freezing.

Why don’t you guys go to the zoo for a few hours, just you and him? And it was a little cold. It was a cold 57, but I decided to do it, and we only, we got there at three, and it closed at four. I called it Express Zoo. We ended up staying 30 minutes over there in closing time, but we were not the only ones, but we visited every single animal in the zoo. We ate lunch, and we played on the playground in our Express Zoo time. And I completely let go of everything in my business. I was so present with my kid, and at one point, I remembered, oh my god, this is the point. This matters. The other stuff doesn’t matter. This matters. This is the point of all of it. This is why I do what I do. Like this little guy, like this matters.

And also because it was like a spring-like day, made me think like there’s this concept of wintering, and I tend to get a little bit like, not seasonal depression, but I definitely have more energy when it’s warm outside. And it just made me think spring is coming, and with spring, there will be energy, there will be renewal, there will be vitality. And I just came home, and I was like, so grateful to my husband. And I told him, thank you so much. I was like, how did you see that? How did you see that I needed that bad?

We had so much fun. Like we just ran through the zoo. We had the best time. Jackson came home. I he’s never done this ever. He talked to Neil the entire dinner, recounting every single thing that we did. It was precious.

So that was amazing and really just got me into a completely different head space and this morning I woke up and I’m like, I am renewed. I am resilient. I found my resilient. I am ready to go again. I have ideas. Like I felt so clear. I came up with an entire like 20 point list of new marketing ideas that I had not come up with before, things I wanted to do to bring the energy back up for the launch. And I felt like energetically excited to do it and like this was going to be like the biggest triumph story there ever was.

So I got myself to the same energy as before. And I was thinking as we were driving home that I think many of my students would not allow themselves when the wind is in their face and the sales aren’t coming in and everything is broken, they would not allow themselves to go to the zoo for a couple of hours. They would punish themselves and say, you have to sit here and figure it out, you have to work harder. They would sit and spin because there was nothing we could do. There was nothing I could do except trust that it was going to get figured out.

But they would sit and spin in this like punishment, I’m not allowed to go let this down for a second. I’ve got to be doing something productive. I’ve got to be whatever it is, like the energy is, they would not let themselves go take two hours to go to the zoo and take the rest of the evening to just be with their family and get a good night’s sleep. I have a PEMF mat. So I did my PEMF mat, and I just let myself down-regulate from the emotional energy that was expended in all of it.

I remember when I first started doing this work, I sold a retreat out. Like, I launched a retreat, and I sold it out, and it had like 12 spots based on the sleeping arrangements. And then I had a ton of one-on-one clients that didn’t get to sign up before it sold out. And they all said, can you do another weekend? And if you do, I’ll sign up. So I booked another weekend, a non-refundable deposit. And I went to those clients, and every single one of them came up with an excuse as to why they couldn’t do it. 

Actually, well, just kidding. And I’m like, wait, what? Like I put a deposit down like on your word that you were doing this. And for it took me two weeks, two weeks of swimming in disappointment and frustration and fear and uncertainty of not getting that deposit back because and it was like the rest of the money would be do as well. And that year I think I was only at like $150,000 or no, I think that was the year I made $325,000. So it was like a lot of money at the time in my business. And I it took me two weeks to process the disappointment and pick myself up and do this thing that I just did in two days.

So two weeks to two days. That’s the point of why this work matters, and doing it over and over year after year and being getting better at it and honing it and deepening it and letting it be more of you is that the recovery time is so much faster with way bigger amounts of money on the line. And I found that to be really powerful. Like I found that to be impressive, like a very, and by the way, after two weeks though, I did relaunch my retreat, and I sold eight of the 12 spots. And I was so proud of myself. I couldn’t even believe it.

And so I always believe in the power of relaunching. I always believe in the power of being able to pick energy back up and be able to commit and see the outcome all the way through for my students who have ever, if you’ve ever done a Revenue Challenge with me, whether my 200k Mastermind or when I sell it publicly, this is the energy I’m talking about. You could be halfway or a three-fourths of the way through your Challenge and not even close to your goal and how you recover from that and get yourself back up in your energy is directly impacts the result that you create and whether you achieve your challenge or not even when everything points to the fact that you’re not going to.

And so that’s the place I’m at, is regardless of how we started, how do I reconnect with this goal that I have of how many founders I want to begin this journey with is done. And I have to have that same enthusiasm and belief, no matter how we started and no matter how many days people couldn’t buy. So that’s where I’m at today.

So here’s what I’m doing moving forward. So part of my plan was today, I went live in my program, 2k for 2k, which has 6,000 people in it and kind of broke down the number one question that I knew people would ask, which is what’s the difference between 2k and the Entrepreneur Coach Membership. And I gave them an hour inside scoop of this is exactly, you know, what’s different. And then I’m doing this live stream here, and I came up with my list of at least 10 ideas to that were never going to, like, we already have marketing in place, but here’s 10 more ideas of things that we’re going to do. And so that’s what I’m going to do.

We start the first calls for the month of January in the Entrepreneur Coach Membership, that we’re starting with the Identity Series, and that starts on January 20th. So the people who have signed up by January 20th are my founders, and they will come with me on the Identity Series. And then the next month’s topic will be released the last week of January. I’ll start marketing that.

So in my mindset, I have already started to work, like, just align with the belief because I already believe it, which is if this launch had not even happened, I could still do the numbers I had wanted to do and get my founding members with just that launch because people are going to freak out when they find out what it is.

Like that’s my thought. And so I’m prepared to generate instead of, you know, I gave myself two launches because I wanted to be able to explain the membership and the concept and what you’re going to learn for an entire year in one week. Then I wanted to kind of decompress from that and listen to what people had said and how I might need to say things differently for them to understand the value. And then I’m going to go again with the next month’s course topic and release that.

And so I wanted to give myself two launches in the month of January to sell to my founding members and get my foot in the like language and the communication of this offer because I believe no matter how talented you are at selling and how experienced you are and how much money you make, you are still selling a new offer and you still have to develop that language and figure out how people need you to say it versus how you want to say it.

And so I’m in that process, and I wanted to give myself two solid weeks to do that. So I’m still going to be doing that. And that’s it. I can’t believe that I recovered in just two days after such a massive, like, I’m impressed with myself. I’m proud of myself.

And it has really made me double down on why this work is so important. My clients and the coaches I’m speaking to on a daily basis are not recovering this fast and this powerfully. They’re not using their obstacles and their setbacks to their advantage to create more value and help their students at a higher level. And it’s everything because it keeps you in such integrity as a coach. It makes you a product of your product, and it magnetizes clients to you when you are living and breathing the work that you ask other people to do. It’s so important.

Like we are supposed to be failing. We’re supposed to be going first, going often, and going with the purpose of helping others. We’re supposed to be risking more than we ask our clients to risk. We are supposed to be learning at a faster pace than they’re learning. Entrepreneurship is literally running off in a direction, and you’re not sure if it’s the right direction. It’s putting something together without having directions to put it together. That’s what it is. And there is great reward when you get really good at doing that.

So that is my lesson for you all today. I wanted to walk you through my process and reinvite you to the Entrepreneur Coach Membership. Yes, Tracea, such a masterclass on how to recover and recover well. Maybe that should be the title of this. I’m going to release it on the podcast. I might like that better than the one that I titled it. How to recover and how to recover well.

So join me in the Entrepreneur Coach Membership. All you have to do is comment EC and we’re going to change that mini chat comment, I think soon because apparently it sends you the link even if you have EC in a word that you type, which is so weird and who knew, but I learned something new for Manychat as well.

Or you can go to
 
Staceyboehman.com/ec-membership/
 and you will also have the link there.

You have till the 20th to sign up for the Identity Series in January. We’re going to be covering entrepreneur identity, coach identity, and leadership identity and I’ve never taught the things I’m going to be teaching. Some of the things, like there will be very few things that are crossover from things I’ve taught before, but most of these things are going to be new ways to look and think of yourself as each of these three identities that you are if you are a coach and an entrepreneur. And I’m going to be diving deep into the through lines to make them all work together instead of kind of pitted against each other and in conflict and having you in dissonance.

And it’s going to really set us up for the year of work that we’re going to do together to add onto those identities in a really powerful way. And then you can sign up until February 2nd for the February’s lessons, and then we’re going to close down for two months.

So if you want to be a founder and get in before April, you’re going to need to join by February 2nd to be in on the magic and the fun. And there are special founding bonuses that you get. You’re getting the, you’re getting, if you are a founder and you do the entire year with me, you’re getting some surprise bonuses that I’m not telling people, but they’re going to be incredible, and everyone will be jealous about. You’ll get those after you complete the year with me as a celebration.

If you’re a founder, you’re also getting access to a Mastermind I ran twice called the 25k group, focused on taking my students from 2k to 25k in revenue, which is like the second hardest part of entrepreneurship. And I one of the inspirations of this membership because I all of my containers, 2k, 200k, 2 Million Dollar Group, are very revenue focused. And I created this 25k group and I found myself at that income range, specifically, I found myself coaching on all the things I’m going to teach in the membership.

So because of that, I wanted to include that as a founding bonus. So if you join by February 2nd, you get 50, I believe it’s around 50 calls from two rounds of my 25k group and what I was teaching in there. Although this is an all-level course, we have multimillionaires signing up for this. So whether you’ve made $0 or you’re a multimillionaire, this, it’s all, like I’ve done this work at every single level in my business over the last 10 years. It’s just the better I get at it. I go from two weeks of recovery to two days of recovery.

And my next goal will be two hours of recovery. Like, boom, let’s just go. And then two, maybe two minutes of recovery, right? Like that’s how you make more money is your time is just used better and better and better. So you’re getting that.

And everyone that joins also immediately has in their member portal, Return On Investment, ROI, the Entrepreneur Series course that I ran last year to teach people how to think like an investor, how to create a return on investment plan for the membership and to make sure you get what you came for, how to extract value and how to think like an investor instead of a consumer and a student. And that will automatically be in your portal.

So if you did not take that course, you can take it for the first time. And if you’ve already done that course, this will be you getting to go again, and you will be able to extract things that you missed the first time. You will take the work deeper than you did the first time. You will be ahead of the game for everyone else because this will be your second look at it. I often sign up for things more than once so that I can take myself as a new version of me into that work again and get more out of it because I’ve become a new version of me.

So you will have that as whether you’ve done it before or you will be doing it for the first time. You’ll have access to that, and it will remain in your member portal as long as you are a student. And then you can join me in the Identity Series, and then you can join me in the next month’s content, which I will announce at the last week of January. So fun.

All right, I hope this was a really, like, I knew that this would be a masterclass. I hope you receive it that way, and “recovering well,” I love that language. Have an amazing rest of your week, and I hope to see you inside the new membership. All right, let me know if you guys have questions.

You can comment on this live stream if you do have questions, or you can reach out to my team at support@staceyboehman.com. All right, talk to you all later. Bye.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2k for 2k program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2kfor2k. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #370: Lessons from 10 Years in Business: Listening to the Whisper
transcript:
W
elcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2k, $20k, and $200k using her proven formula.

Hi coaches. Welcome to episode 370. Today, I am announcing a big change in my business, a directional, it feels like a seismic shift, a directional shift in where, how things have been going, where things have been going, and I want to give you all of my perspective and my thoughts.

Because one of the things I’ve noticed over the years is that I had my amazing production manager, videographer, all the things, Matt Care, once said to me that when people don’t know the full story, our brains are designed to fill in gaps. And because of the way our brains work, often those gaps get filled negatively.

And I have seen that happen in the last 10 years of my business, and I’ve watched people think that they know how I’m thinking and decide that they know what my intentions are or how I make my decisions or why I’m doing this or why I didn’t do that or all the things. And I have found in the last like few years what I started doing, if you’ve been following me for a long time, this might not be like the best intro episode to me if you’ve just found me, but if you’ve been following me a long time, you have seen me do this.

When I did my 200k Mastermind unbundle, I really walked people through that decision. When I launched the Entrepreneur Series, I really walked people through that decision. And so today I want to do my best to capture all of my thinking and help you, help walk you through this next decision and this change that is happening starting today.

And I titled this episode

And I love that for her. I love that for all of the women that are like, yeah, like I got to this place where I don’t have to work, and I don’t, I want to live my life. Like I think that’s, I’m like, yeah, as a coach, like that might have been why we got into it.

And in fact, I will say I used this against myself for a little bit when I was feeling very sorry for myself about being a new mom and having to be away from my kids and, you know, comparing myself to stay-at-home moms, not in a healthy way. I used to be thinking like, I should be doing that too. I have littles, that’s the right thing to do. And like, well, if they get to do it, why shouldn’t I get to do it? I had a lot of very unhelpful thoughts for a while about working and being a mom of littles.

But when I think about these stats and when I think about being the first in my lineage to create generational wealth and bring dreams of entrepreneurship alive, when I think of the percent of women making $10 million a year and having babies and running a company and doing it all, like when I think about that, I feel so compelled to go in the complete opposite direction.

And I am very surprised by this. And you might be too. I am very surprised by my desire, instead of my desire to step away, my desire to double down. And I haven’t decided this lightly. There have, I mean, it’s been three years. So there’s been so much deliberate coaching and exploration and investigation and it really, like I was thinking about the phases I’ve gone through in the last three years. It took me going from I’m not growing right now, I’m being with my kids, to I’m growing slow and steady, to maybe I want to grow big. And what are all my reasons?

And I feel like if you’ve been listening to the podcast for a while, you might even be able to see those thoughts in my communications when it comes to like what’s happening with my business. I think you could see each of those stages. And now I’m firmly in, I want to grow, and I really want that growth to be on my terms and my way. And I do feel like that I have earned deeply after $45 million in sales and 10 years in business, like I for myself, like not from an entitled place, but for myself, I have earned deeply doing it my way from this moment on, even if it breaks my own rules of, you know, because I would go follow my own rules to grow again in a heartbeat.

Like if I was starting from zero, I would do everything I taught in 2k for 2k. If I was trying to get to 200k, I would do everything I taught in 200k. If I was trying to get to 2 Million Dollar Group or to $2 million, I would do everything I teach in 2 Million Dollar Group.

I would not deviate from that at all. That is my 100% truth. And now that I’m not in any of those places, I’m like, okay, what’s this next thing? Maybe one day I’m going to have a program that’s like after 10 million where you like have so much money that you don’t have to work and also you want to work and now you have to figure out like what is my motivation and my desire and how do I want to run a business with that level of like with those circumstances, which is different than I want to run a business with the circumstances of I need to create generational wealth, right?

And so you’ve seen me make some of those changes to my existing businesses. The wanting to be on, you know, the terms on my way. Again, I don’t offer guarantees anymore. I’m just more selective in general with the people I work with. And this year coming up, I’m going to be even more selective of who I let in my Mastermind spaces.

That feels like a really big deal to me, is I’m going to have a lot more qualifiers and a lot more education on what it means to be in a Mastermind space with me, not in like a high-control way, but like, hey, here are my terms and I want to make sure you agree to them. Like, I want to make sure we’re all on the same page of what feels important to me as far as how we engage together in this space. And I’m just going to be more clear. Like, I’m just going to lead on that. I’m going to be more clear and I’m going to, you’ll see. I don’t want to go too much into it, but you are going to see me be more selective and how I do that. Like, if you watch me, you’ll see it.

And I’m also, moving forward, going to worry less about other people’s feelings in regards to the decisions I make in order to make sure that I am happy in my spaces and that I desire to be there. Like, my boundaries are going to be at an all-time high, and I’m working very hard to be okay with people not being okay with some of my boundaries.

And like, some of, and let me give you an example of that, because sometimes I think you guys can make stuff up that’s not helpful. Like sometimes people will say, I want the transcripts, and they’ll have lots of reasons, including that they learn better by reading the transcripts, but I don’t give out my transcripts. That’s my intellectual property that I might want to turn into a book one day. I don’t know, but I just don’t want people owning that. Like having that for a lifetime access, like here’s a transcript of what every word that was said and all of Stacey’s intellectual property. That’s a no for me.

People seem unhappy when we, when they want them, and we say no. And I’m just going to honor that. The clients who work with me have got to be okay with that. I don’t want to give you the transcripts of my intellectual property. From love, I don’t want to do that. So I’ve got to work with people that are okay with that.

So, like that’s like an example of that, where normally I would have lots of thoughts about displeasing people in that way or like telling someone no and then them being mad at me, like I would be mortified. So I’m working with owning this is my boundary to make me happy, or like not letting people sell in my spaces and giving them warnings like, hey, if you do this again, we’re going to kick you out. Like, you can’t be selling in my spaces. I don’t like that.

So those things, again, even though things you would think are super easy, they’re challenging for me. So I’ve been my boundaries, I’m working on them being high because the more happy and desire I have to be in a space, the more I create and the better I feel. So that is like me getting to do this in my way.

But the other thing that’s happening, and I’ve told I’ve been pretty like upfront about this, but I wanted to really like paint the picture of why this is happening. I am adding a new permanent offer. As part of my doubling down, as part of my going in the opposite direction, as part of my choice and my desire, as part of what makes me eternally happy and doing it my way, I am launching a new offer today. It is going to be the next big body of work that I do. Possibly the next decade of my work.

What I know now is that it has felt scary. It’s now it feels a lot less scary because I’ve moved forward so much on it. But there has been this whisper for at least the last two years. Like a really small one amidst my brain telling me to step back, there’s also been a whisper to step forward and in a direction I haven’t done before.

In fact, in a direction that I’ve sort of stayed away from. And again, I think we’re just not listening to our whispers enough. And I’ve been telling my clients to listen to those whispers and to investigate them, to explore them, and maybe possibly honor them. And I’ve been telling them they can do so without permanence.

So, although I am saying it’s a new permanent offer, I am also allowing that at any time I can change that. It’s the only way I’ve found that I can let myself go all in without abandon is that I’ve got to be willing to say, this is what I would do if I were all in, and I’m going to do that with all of my heart until I’m not. And maybe that will never come. I know I’m in fully for a year. I’m probably in for at least two to three years because I am already planning 2027 in my head. I’m like just feel like a content teaching machine right now, and so I have at least all the way through mid 2027 planned out, and I just know once I get in that more is coming.

And so if I love it as much as I imagine I’m going to and as much as I have loved it, I can see this being the wisdom that I dissect 10 years from now talking about this offer. Like, I’ll go back and be like, oh my god, remember episode 370, 10 years ag,o when I launched this offer? L,ike here’s what we’ve done in the next 10 years.

So, I’m getting started. Actually, I already got started. I wanted to test my joy and my purpose with this new offer in a very strategic way. So, I launched the Entrepreneur Series. And what this was, if you’ve not heard me talk about the Entrepreneur Series, but even if you have, I’m going to tell you kind of a different angle about it.

When I launched it was because I’d brought on someone from outside the coaching world that was in the tech world. And after watching me teach on stage at 200k live multiple times, he said, you know, I know you’re teaching sales, but really I feel like you’re teaching entrepreneurship to coaches. Like, it feels much bigger than even selling. He’s like, the selling is like amazing, but what you’re really doing is teaching sales and entrepreneurship to coaches. And I started saying that to people. Like when they say, what do you do? I teach sales and entrepreneurship to coaches. And I started really thinking about what would it be like if I claimed that? How would I do that?

And when I started thinking about, well, what is it that’s like the sales pieces, obviously are my 2k process, 200k process, 2 Million Dollar Group process, but then what’s this thing that he’s picking up on of the entrepreneurship side that I’m teaching? And if I could say what is it that entrepreneurs coaches need to learn as entrepreneurs, it’s mindset. It’s the mindset game, it’s the emotional game, and it’s a decision game.

Like having a steely mindset that can rise above and think higher than any challenge, even if it’s a challenge no one else has ever faced. Having resilience and the ability to expand capacity and energy when you think there’s none. It’s learning how to make decisions as an entrepreneur that still honors why you became a coach in every single decision. It’s creating balance in the agenda of an entrepreneur whose job is to bring in revenue, and then also balancing that with the agenda of a coach who wants to serve and transform.

So revenue, serve, and transform. And balancing those out, and also balancing out living life and having and maybe having family and other priorities, health priorities, while also running a profitable, growing business, and how to deal with the imbalance of all that can come from that.

Now here’s what’s really crazy. When I first created 2k for 2k, my coach and I discussed if I was going to add a lot of mindset work into the process of 2k. And it is there. Like when it comes to selling, it’s there everywhere you look. It’s woven into the process. I’ve always said, when it comes to selling, I teach what to do, why to do it, how it impacts the client, and how you need to think and feel to do it really well.

But we kind of stayed away from deep dives into mindset and emotional work because at the time, coaches were kind of getting lost in this like endless self-improvement. And we wanted to bypass that and just go straight to listen, you are improved, go make an offer, do the thing, you’re ready. And it worked like crazy. Thousands and thousands of coaches got off the ground and started making money.

And that is still true and in this moment, in the industry, at this moment in time, at this time in the world, every coach that I’m having conversations with, when they’re being honest, they are telling me the biggest things holding them back are mindset, capacity, energy, resilience, aliveness, courage, work ethic, identity. It’s like development of them as people, as entrepreneurs, as coaches, as leaders.

So it feels like it’s time, like full circle to develop coaches to be the highest level entrepreneurs they can be, to be able to withstand entrepreneurship and do it well, to be able to handle the risk and tolerate that, to tolerate the journey of entrepreneurship, to honor that a coach who is also an entrepreneur needs very specific training on how to balance those two, to honor those two at the same time.

That being an entrepreneur coach is not the same as being a contract coach and being hired by a company to coach for them. And it’s also not the same as being a standard mainstream entrepreneur. We’re not going to respond well to if you want to be successful in business, you got to miss the ballet lessons and you’ve got to sacrifice and you have to work 100 hours a week and you’ve got to bleed and you’ve got to, you know, leave everything on the like we’re not going to respond to that because we got into entrepreneurship to have control.

Like, this Forbes article was saying that the reason women are outpacing men in business right now is because they want to be their own boss. They want to make the rules. They want to be able to manage their home life with and also bring money in.

And so for all those reasons, especially if you are a woman coach entrepreneur, the rules, the way you have to learn entrepreneurship, it has to be different. It has to factor in the reasons you got into business and who you are and the cognitive load that you carry, potentially as, not always, but potentially as a mom or a wife or the matriarch of the family or the doer and organizer of the family, and maybe the leader, the breadwinner, and the visionary of the family. It has to honor all of those things.

I think it’s why a lot of business programs don’t resonate with coaches. Like it’s what I, this new offer is going to be what I did with selling, is I made it resonate for coaches. I’m like, hey, here’s what you’ve probably heard in selling, and this is why it doesn’t resonate for you. It doesn’t come from service. This is why get energy sends you so far away from signing clients. So we’ve got to make entrepreneurship resonate for coaches, of we have to make being a CEO, being the boss, being a leader resonate for coaches, and what that entails.

Like, there’s such a huge cognitive load that comes from being the one who has to make all the decisions, all of them. The one who has to decide when you don’t know what the right answer is. The one who goes first. And I want to help develop that next generation of coaches in this industry to be great at that, to handle the load of going first and going often and going with the purpose of leading your people to do the same, to be powerful instead of powerless.

And to bring it full circle again, because honestly, I can’t even keep track of in the last week or two how many full circle moments this offer has created. But when my coach, when I first started my business, I heard my coach say, I’m not scared of losing it all. I would just rebuild it with all the knowledge that I own in my brain. And if I was being honest, I used to think, oh my god, I hope I never have to do that. And then I had to.

And now having rebuilt it, having taken my business from literally struggling in customer service, struggling in operations, struggling in team management, struggling with profitability, struggling with reputation to killing it in customer service, clean, clear, lean operations, efficiently managed, lean teams, 60% profitability, a million dollars of revenue growth, all in the same year, and a strong reputation with clear leadership, like no one can ever take that away from me.

And I want this for you. I want you to never let anyone take it from you, including yourself. I feel really passionate about this. One of the other things I read, I believe in this Forbes article, is that 47% of women who quit their businesses do so for personal reasons. They cite personal reasons as the reason.

And one of the things that it said is that women actually, the reason we’re outpacing men in starting entrepreneurship is that we actually have more tolerance for risk. Like we’re willing to take financial risk, we’re willing to take risk, but we also take the financial losses and the criticisms the hardest because we’re taught that being nice and caring for others above ourselves is the mark of being a good woman.

So we do that. We pay employees more than average to be good. We keep them long after it’s stopped working to be caring. We refund even when it’s against our policies and financially harms us, so that just to not be seen as uncaring and to be seen as abundant.

I cannot tell you the amount of conversations in 2k and 200k that I have seen with that, it’s that in and of itself, I’m going to take out credit card debt that financially harms me just so I don’t look uncaring and because I’ve been taught that’s the abundant thing to do. I’m going to financially harm the business and go against good, savvy business sense and put myself in harm and possibly put myself out of business. And I’ve done it too. I remember when people were attacking me, I refunded $1.5 million of my own personal net worth, took that from my family, because I didn’t want to be seen as uncaring, and I wanted to be seen as abundant.

That’s what we do because of the messaging that we’re given. We say yes when we mean no. We fear being talked about. We fear leaving our spouses behind. We take care of everything and everyone but the business. And when we can’t fucking keep up anymore, when we are in despair, we let go of the business.

But it doesn’t have to be this way. Like, this offer feels like my rally cry for women, for coaches, for entrepreneurs. Like, there is a different way. I have created it. I now live it. But it does require evolution. It requires thinking in a revolutionary way as a woman, as an entrepreneur, as a leader, as a coach, it requires something different, something that works because what is happening now for a lot of people isn’t working. And I’m going to teach it.

I started teaching it in the Entrepreneur Series. And I will tell you, each course that I launched of this of the Entrepreneur Series, I, every time it ended, I was left feeling sad that we could not take this work further. And at the same time lit up because there was so much more I wanted to share, and I saw the work changing my clients. Like, we got so overwhelmed with testimonials that I couldn’t even keep pace with sharing them all.

So I know that this work is needed, even if it’s not like the most apparent thing on your mind, even if you think that what’s on your mind is like what’s the next offer and what’s the stats, and how do I get people more converting? It’s like the honest answer for so many people along with that, along with the strategy of entrepreneurship is the mindset work, is the emotional work, is the decision-making work of the entrepreneur coach.

And this is my new membership. Oh my god, I almost started crying. I’m so excited. I’m launching a membership for the first time ever, which also feels like a big deal. It’s the only thing I haven’t sold, really. And I’m so excited to do it. You can come with me by signing up annually and just be all in for the entire, the whole year is planned out, every single month and into the next year. Or you can come with me month to month. That’s the this is the first time ever that you’re going to be able to do that. So you can join if you’re like, oh, I’m really curious about what this is, you can join for one month and decide if you want to continue or not. And each month, I’m going to teach you how to be a stronger entrepreneur coach.

And I will say although I am totally fine to have men in my space and I have men in all of my spaces, I will take you all day long, but this is, there are going to be moments where this is very focused on being a woman entrepreneur coach because we just have that added extra layer of societal expectations that really makes us make bad decisions in business that harm us and sometimes have us closing the doors at 47% because we can’t manage the life and all of the things.

Like, I feel so compelled by that. When I read that, I just burst into tears because I know I’ve been there. I’ve been through the dark of the night with my business. I have been through the deepest depths of despair with my business. I get it. I know the challenges of running, having a family, being the mama, and also dealing with the deep business problems. Like I or even just growth and not being able to figure out how to get there. Like, I know all of it. So I wept from knowing for these women that closed their doors. And you may not even fear that now, but I want to make sure it never even comes up in your brain.

So each month, we’re going to focus on you being stronger so that you don’t need the path to be easy, so that you don’t need life to be easy, so that you can meet any challenge with a bigger version of you than you ever thought possible. Like I could not imagine the me that I am now, even two years ago, even a year ago.

We’re going to study the identity that you need to develop as a coach, as an entrepreneur, as a leader, as an investor, as a breadwinner, as a woman. I’m going to help you build capacity and capability every single day, one day at a time, because it’s created in the little moments, not the big things. It’s the everyday tiny moments. I’m going to teach you how to ignite a liveliness in you with your business and your life, no matter how hard times are, and then expand it during good times.

And one of the things that people have been asking about like crazy, I’m going to teach you how to operate from desire instead of willpower. I’m going to teach you how I create new belief alongside protecting revenue and all the other entrepreneur responsibilities. That’s something else people have been asking about like crazy in my behind-the-scenes, is like how do you have time to create all these new beliefs for yourself, but you’re also running this business. I’m going to teach you that.

I’m also going to help redefine standing out online as an entrepreneur and a coach because this current social landscape has like scrambled a bunch of people’s brains. And I’m going to help you build the muscle of visibility and how to withstand haters and cancel culture, how to think about that, how to be so rock solid in your core. I’ve coached so many people through that recently.

Like all of these things are labeled personal issues, right? When I’m talking to my people, why I took a step back because of this personal reason. I took a step back because of this health reason. I took a step back because of a family member’s health issue. I’ve taken a step back. Like I’ve had so many people and then I’ve also helped so many people step forward that wanted to. Not from should. I don’t want to be another should, but if you want to take a step forward, I want to make sure that step is concrete.

I’m going to help you challenge your work ethic in the best way, not just like hyper productivity and burnout, like the best way to challenge your work ethic to where you never have to worry about burnout again. We’re going to really create true balance one day at a time. This is everything that you need to be in business for the rest of your life if you want it, and everything that you need to enjoy the hell out of your life and your business while you’re in it.

And if you’ve ever just thought, I want what she has, just know each month we’re going to break down the thinking and the emotional expansion that I had to do to create it. Like this is the entrepreneurship on steroids, but in the best way.

So, come join me in the Entrepreneur Coach Membership. We start this January right now with the three identities: the coach, the entrepreneur, the leader. If you heard my podcast where I taught that for an hour in a free course, I’m going to teach that for an entire month inside the membership. We’re going to dive deep, we’re going to take lots of examples in coaches businesses, like real coach examples, and I’m going to teach far deeper than I taught on that episode

But the identities that we have to embody, we have to start with that, and then we’re going to layer on all the skills, all the emotional capacities, all of the beliefs needed to be the highest level, to execute at the highest level as a coach and entrepreneur and a leader.

So, I am not taking a step back. I am not pairing down. I, like a rubber band pulled back just so I can slingshot forward. Come join me at 
staceyboehman.com
 forward…. I’m going to cry… forward slash ec dash membership. So let me say it again, and we’ll link it in the show notes,
 
staceyboehman.com/ec-membership
. I hope to see you inside.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2k for 2k program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2Kfor2K. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #369: Lessons from 10 Years in Business: Infinite Perspective
transcript:
W
elcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2k, $20k, and $200k using her proven formula.

Hi coaches, welcome to episode 369. You’re going to be listening to this on the first week of January, the first Wednesday of January, but I’m recording this on my last day of work before I head off on and my team heads off on Christmas break

I am cozy in my office with a cup of coffee and a flannel Christmas shirt that’s so cozy, and my little warm Ugg boots and just feeling so excited about the holidays. I’m actually, I’m not actually sad, but we’re a little sad over here. We had the most amazing snowy first three weeks of December ever. Like nothing but snow outside for three weeks. It felt like a white Christmas. And then it’s going away and Christmas day, it’s going to be 70 degrees. Make it make sense. This is Kentucky.

So we’re like, what happened? Like, why couldn’t that have just shifted like one week? But it’s not the case. So I hope that you all, if you celebrate any of the December holidays, Merry Christmas, Happy Hanukkah, all of the beautiful wishes that I want to send you your way. And I hope that and if you celebrate nothing, I just hope that you have cozy time with your family, and that you have, is it hygge? Is that what they call it? Just be so cozy and comfy.

And I hope that you have some time to reflect about this year, the past year, and that, well, I’m saying it now, but you’re going to listen to it after the fact. So that’s a little weird. But I hope you had time to sit and reflect and then think about the new year. And if you’re just now doing, that’s great too. Hello.

At the time of recording, I’m going to be delivering a three-year plan event for my students in my 200k Mastermind and 2 Million Dollar groups. So I think this is the perfect episode of, this was always going to be one of my top 10 lessons from 10 years in business. And it’s so perfect that it fell the exact week of the three-year plan event. I don’t know how that happened because it wasn’t intentional. It wasn’t like massive forethought. I think sometimes when you’re just in the current, things align. And so that’s what’s happening here.

So today I want to talk about infinite perspective or infinite thinking. And I want to say, before I dive in, that I first learned of this concept and this idea from Simon is it Simon Sinek or Simon Sinek? I always feel like I mispronounce his last name. But he has a book called 
The Infinite Game
. It’s brilliant. I highly recommend that all of you read it. I have it, I have like a collection of maybe 12 or so books of like my all-time favorite books in business on my shelf in my office. This book is one of them.

I actually used to require, not require, but like request of my 200k Mastermind students for the first several rounds. When they came in before they started, I would tell them to read three books, 
Essentialism
 by Greg McKeown, I think is how I’m pronouncing his name right. Then I would have them read
 Originals
 by Adam Grant, and then 
The Infinite Game
 by Simon Sinek.

Three profound books that really shaped a lot of the ways that I think in my business now and the things that I teach in the 200k Mastermind. And I would say this episode, if you read the book, may be like a far deviation from the way he describes it and how he talks about it because I read it so many years ago, and then I’ve been using it in my own brain for so many years that I’m sure they don’t align, like line up exactly anymore. And this episode really isn’t a recap of his book. So if you want to read that, I think you will hear brand new things, a brand new take, and maybe it will also solidify some things that I do say here, but I don’t think it’s going to be a copy in any way. So I highly recommend that book. It’s very brilliant.

So here’s what I want to share with you all today. A couple of things. So the way that I use the idea of infinite thinking or infinite perspective is that I filter all of my decisions through this perspective. And you can also think of it as just big picture thinking. Like I’m always thinking of the big picture, the infinite perspective. So I think further ahead and wider than just now. I solve problems thinking of the bigger picture.

But what’s challenging is that we live in the small picture, right? Like we live in the smaller picture problems. And our brain tells us that those are the most important. And they’re the most painful because they’re in the moment. The pain now. But if you always solve for the most painful things of the moment, you are always in the moment, like we live every moment in the moment, right? So if you’re always solving for the pain points of the moment, then you just always end up being in the pain.

Like, let me solve this pain right now in this moment, and then let me solve this pain right now in this moment. And it’s just always small picture things that you end up solving. In scaling, a lot of times, I talk about this, and I’ve heard this explained, it’s like the energy of always putting out fires.

If you are someone who’s constantly putting out this fire and this fire and this fire, and it feels kind of hustly, like as soon as I put out one, there’s another one that comes, it’s because you’re solving in a very narrow, small, current thinking versus when you scale, you have to think in three years, how do I want to solve this problem? If there were 10,000 students instead of 1,000, how would I solve this problem? How do I solve this problem forever, not just for today? Because you can solve things for today to get out of the pain very quickly, but those solutions don’t typically work long-term because they’re very hustly, get out of the pain very quickly decisions.

So for example, if you needed, if you were full-time in your business and you needed to come up with money really quick and you threw out an offer that you were never planning on offering again, and it didn’t really fit into anything for the future of your business, you might spend a lot of energy, make a little money, but you didn’t actually solve the chronic thing of why is there not money coming into your business with the offers that you want to be selling, how you want to be selling it. That’s the difference.

And it is kind of, I think you can small decision, current pain point solution your way to 100k, to 200k, to 300k, but the more money you start making, the harder it becomes because those little decisions really start to add up and it just really does become those fires all over the place. And you just never get out of, like we always think, oh, when I finally make $200k, then I’ll be out of the pain.

But I always say, like when you want to, this is something I actually say in the three-year plan, is if you want to double your revenue, think of the top three pain points you have right now in your business, and imagine those being doubled. Like, we think I’m going to double the money, and the pain points go away. No, you’re going to double the money if you don’t solve the pain point first before you double the money, you just double the problems too.

If I want to have an amazing reputation in the industry, what does that look like? I just ask myself these bigger picture questions.

And then again, the same with my investments. I think I don’t make the small investments, of like how can I solve this problem and make it go away now? Even with my employees, I’m looking for like not who can fill the gap now, but who will forever be able to fill the gap? What investment can I make next that will infinitely serve me in the future? Like all of my questions are like that. It always comes back to the big picture for me.

So that is one of my lessons. I’m having so much fun with these. I will have another one for you next week as well. But I hope you enjoyed the infinite perspective, infinite thinking. And I really, even if your infinite thinking is not the same as my infinite thinking, I want to offer and highly suggest that you try this on.

All right. Happy New Year, my friends. I hope you have lots and lots of big goals, and if I can help you with any of them this year, let’s go. All right, I’ll talk to you next week

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2k for 2k program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2kfor2k. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #368: Lessons from 10 Years in Business: Mindset and Emotional Expansion
transcript:
W
elcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2k, $20k, and $200k using her proven formula.

Hey coaches, welcome to episode 368. Are you loving these episodes? Because what I’m hearing is you are, which makes me very happy because I’m loving doing them. I was actually just telling a client in my—we just had a 200k Mastermind call, and she was telling herself that she didn’t know what to say to her people and that she didn’t—she didn’t basically didn’t think that what she had to say was life changing. And so, I gave her homework at the end of our session.

We coached on a bunch of things, but at the end, I said, “Sit down and make a list of what you believe to be true about coaching for your clients, about your work. What’s your philosophy? What are the things that you think are true?”

Make an exhaustive list and then choose some of the top ones that you think, “I really believe this. I think that if people knew this, they would 100% have their lives changed. This would serve them. This would help them. This would be so much—if they really got it, this would be so valuable.” And then go out and say those things. Say those things to other people. Create content, create webinars, create emails, create podcasts, create things.

I was like, “That’s all I did when I decided I want to release my top 10 lessons from 10 years in business, wisdom from 10 years in business. What are the things that I believe after 10 years? What are the things I believe to be the most true? What are the things that—what are the pillars or philosophies that I have that have really made me successful and made my client successful?”

And I created a pretty exhaustive list, so there’s the ones that I think are the top 10, and then there’s ones that I’m like, “Oh my God, we also have to talk about this. We also have to talk about this.” And so now I have a list a mile long, I feel like, of episodes that I can’t wait to produce from that space.

So, I just want to offer that to y’all. You guys can do the same thing. Do it on your podcast, do it as webinars, do like—now I have 10 webinar topics, right? Whatever it is that you want to do, get your work out into the world. I just have a deep belief that each of these episodes is going to be so valuable and really change people’s perspectives and engage them in their businesses, engage them in thinking differently about their businesses and that actual deep change will happen because I recorded them.

And because of that, think about the energy to which other people receive these episodes. People are posting like crazy in my different communities about, “Have you listened to this episode? So good.” But that comes from me believing this work is so important and this conversation is so important every single week, and that these things I’m sharing are hugely valuable.

But from being willing to just sit down and say, “What do I believe? What’s my philosophy? What are the things that have mattered to me along the journey?” And then I believe that other people want to hear those things. 

Okay. And this week is no exception. We also had this conversation about things being enough to sell, and I was talking about, I remember the first time my coach, Brooke, sold feeling better. And I remember thinking, “Oh my God.” Her thoughts must be, “This is so important. Someone would invest money to feel better.” And that changed my life because I think sometimes we complicate things up.

And so this episode today, for this week’s episode, this is also a very simple idea that I think we all adopt and also, we all believe and also, we don’t always act on. So today we’re talking about mindset and emotional expansion, emotional capacity.

And what I have learned in 10 years in business is the people who double or triple down with this belief and this work and put it at the forefront as the first response to solving problems, the first response to creating things—it’s like this is their front line. When you do this, you will create higher profits. You will be able to work less, and you will have a leaner business. When you go to mindset and emotional capacity first, before changing circumstances or solving with strategy, before the actions.

Now, I want to say this first: I know not everyone comes into the industry studying and believing the same things. I coached 6,000 coaches in my 2k for 2k, and not everyone comes in as a coach learning that their thoughts create their results. So, this is also why I believe it deserves a firm spot on the list.

But as a bigger thought that I have, I believe that we believe in mindset in theory, and it doesn’t always show up in application. And that is the work, is always remembering, “Oh, it’s our thoughts. Oh, this thought is the reason I’m not creating the result that I want.”

And so I just see on a regular basis and know deeply that many coaches struggle to see how their thoughts actually create their results, especially in the beginning, and how they create their business results. They also struggle to believe new things, like actually create new beliefs. And coaches also tend to struggle with stopping believing in unhelpful things.
