So, for this episode, I want to offer you this thought, this belief, is that the degree to which you manage your mind actively, with purpose, and the degree to which you expand your emotional range to feel things that you don’t want to feel and to feel things that you want to feel, there will be a direct result on the simplicity of the way your business runs and the more profitable that your business is. That will become the result. If you are looking for a simple, lean, highly profitable business, you will create it through your thinking and through what you are willing to feel.

So, I learned very early on that if there was nothing I was unwilling to feel, there would be nothing I would be unwilling to do. So, I remember I was actually in a Meijer grocery store when I heard this idea, and I had just had a show where I felt completely humiliated. Live audience, you never knew what was going to happen. Some shows are amazing, some shows you felt humiliated. And I remember thinking, Okay, let’s go. If this is true, I want to have a very big willingness to feel very big things. I want to be 100% willing to feel the hardest emotions: humiliation, shame, frustration, disappointment, inadequacy. Let’s go.

And I remember doing this show thinking, Okay, I went up, and I did the next show with, What if I was just willing to feel humiliated? And every show after was completely different in that store. And even from that store after store after store, from that moment on, my willingness to feel humiliated changed—I mean, I could talk about that for an entire episode—changed me. And since then, I’ve been, “Okay, here’s the emotion I don’t want to feel. I’ve got to move towards that. I’ve got to be willing to feel that.” And the heavier emotions I’m willing to lift, the stronger I’m going to be.

And then at every level over the last 10 years, it truly—I can see it—it has been my thoughts and that emotional expansion that has been the leap for me in my business growth every time. So, I want to give you a few examples so that you can tangibly see what I’m saying.

I remember a time when I was selling one-on-one coaching, when I believed that as I grew 2k for 2k—like right as I was creating 2k for 2k—I really had a very strong, I don’t know how to describe it, but I was just very stuck. I was very stuck in my willingness to even want to scale my business and grow. Like I wanted to scale my money, but scaling it through a scalable offer like 2k for 2k, I had a ton of resistance.

I believed that the more people that were in there, the less attention each individual person would get and the less results people would get. I thought that going beyond one-on-one was for greedy people, for people who didn’t care about their client results. Not in a way where I was judging other people; it just felt—I was feeling very righteous in my high-touch experience, if that makes sense. Like, “Oh, I care about my clients. I have a very high-touch experience.”

And so in order for me to be able to create a program like 2k and scale, my thoughts had to change. And I remember trying on the idea, “What if it were true that more people in a program could equal better, faster results?”

I don’t even know that anyone ever offered me that. I just remember thinking, “Well, I believe it’s the opposite, so let’s just try on the opposite, right? If I believe that high-touch one-on-one is the way to get better, faster results, let me try on the idea that it could actually be the opposite and then try to prove that to myself. Like, open my mind and try to prove that to myself.”

And I have a few podcasts on this idea and this topic so you could scroll through and find them. I talk about the scaling equation, and I talk about it on a couple of ones: 100% results. I talk about it in several. You could scroll through and find them, so I won’t dive into it here. But ultimately, what I will say is I did prove that. To this day, students are getting profoundly faster, better results than when I was coaching one-on-one.

And the short version of why that’s true is the 2k process has just been stress tested by 6,000 coaches over eight years. There are things that I used to teach in there that I no longer teach in there. For example, that you have, in order to sell one-on-one coaching, you have to have hired a one-on-one coach yourself, and you have to be in an integrity of what you’re selling. And I stopped saying that because people started proving me wrong.

People came into 2k and were selling one-on-one coaching and they had never had a one-on-one coach. They just came straight into 2k, and their clients were getting results. And I was like, “Oh, I can’t say that anymore. It’s not true.” I love it. I love to be proved wrong. If I’m going to be proved wrong, let’s do it, because that was a limiting belief I had that I was passing on to clients at the time. Now, it doesn’t harm them. Can’t possibly harm yourself getting a one-on-one coach, but it just wasn’t true anymore, so I stopped saying it.

And I proved this thought untrue to myself, that the only way to get better results is by doing one-on-one coaching. I proved that wrong, so I stopped saying that anymore. And now I know more people can actually equal better, faster results. And then it went on to be true for my 200k Mastermind and my 2 Million Dollar Group.

So my thought changed, and then my results dramatically shifted. I went from someone who could only make $300,000 a year coaching 20 hours a week to someone who could make $10 million a year coaching 3 hours a week. So that in and of itself proves my theory for this episode true, if we just stopped there.

When you’re willing to challenge—I mean, this was a deep thought. I believed this as if I was reporting the news. There was a lot of emotional resistance to the idea of putting thousands of people in a program at the same time. A lot. You may not know that now because now this is who I am, but there was a version of me who did not believe that this could be true.

So because I changed my mindset and expanded emotionally—and I’m going to talk about this in a second—to where I could hold 1,000 people in my room, 2,000 people, 5,000 people, 6,000 people, I now have a business that was able to be created—$45 million of revenue in three days a week because of what I—the change I decided to make and what I did in the middle, right? It’s not just like, Oh, I decided to think something different, and suddenly this is the business I had.

No, I started behaving differently. The problems that I started to solve, right? So I went from not having—the problem is I can’t scale because I can only coach so many people one-on-one, and that’s the best way to get results—to the problem I’m solving is, How do I get 1,000 people better, faster results? And asking myself that question every single day, or, How do I know that it’s true the more people are in this program that they will get better, faster results?

Answering those questions made me the person I am today. So that’s the middle, right? It’s not just like, Oh, I just start thinking something different. No, the middle and how I behaved in the middle, what I chose to solve, the problems I put my brain to solve, that’s what created the $45 million in three days a week.

And I remember when I got my first 1,000 people into 2k for 2k, the feeling—I coach this a lot in my 2 Million Dollar Group—the feeling of pressure and heaviness of holding 1,000 people’s results, feeling like I needed to be checking in all the time. I needed to answer every single question to give value and to over-deliver because I actually couldn’t answer 1,000 people’s questions, right? I couldn’t be there in that way for that many people, and I believed that was required.

And it was very uncomfortable. I would go to bed at night and be thinking all of the time about, Are my students getting results? Are they going to be okay? Are they going to be happy with me? Are they going to tell me that this didn’t work? I would be holding that in a way that did not feel good.

And so for this, I had to expand my emotional capacity to hold a big group of students and not know if they were going to get the results and not know what they were doing in that specific moment. Are they out there making offers? Are they telling people they’re a life coach? Are they offering to help them? Have they signed a client? Have they made money? I didn’t know any of those answers because not everybody reports into your Facebook community, if you even have one. You don’t always get—the more people you get, you’re not getting direct feedback from them

I just coached someone in my 200k. We just completed a revenue challenge, and I coached her at the very beginning of November when the revenue challenge started.

And I’m trying to remember now, I think her goal was $20k in 30 days, something close to that. And then I didn’t see her on a call again or talk to her again the rest of the revenue challenge. And then she came back today, and she was like, “I made $38,000 in 45 days. I’m freaking out. I didn’t do it with hustle. My entire life has changed. I now see the standard to which I have to operate my business from here on out.” I was crying on the call with her. It was the most incredible thing.

But before I expanded my emotional capacity to be able to hold not talking to her every single week about her goal, I would have been a wreck. But I expanded that ability to be able to let her go out and do her own thing and come back and get coaching when she needed or report back when it was right for her.

I actually teach this in my 2 Million Dollar Group. The ability to scale is directly correlated with your emotional capacity to hold this: the fact that people will not be giving you direct feedback all the time anymore, and you still have to believe in them. I have to believe that they’re going to be resourceful. My clients are going to extract what they need, they’re going to show up for themselves. I had to believe in them deeper. I had to believe in myself more strongly that I’m going to give them something, and it’s going to be valuable enough to see them through for an entire month.

I had to hold the uncertainty of people not having gotten results yet, and working on those results actively. I had to be able to hold the uncertainty of them being actively in failing, failing, failing, and not having broken through yet.

I had another client in the 2 Million Dollar Group this year who was failing, failing, failing, failing, failing. And they actually wrote me an email and said, “Should I quit or am I going to break through? Tell me something to help me break through,” because the failure was so hard. And I had to believe breakthrough is possible, breakthrough is happening. I’ve got this. You’ve got this. We’re going. We’re moving forward. That is an emotional capacity. That’s an emotional strength to walk with someone through their failure and in the uncertainty of them not having achieved the result until they achieve the result, no matter how long it takes.

But the coach that I showed up as when I believed in my students’ capabilities and held their beliefs and the uncertainty of it all without having to act on it or overwork or the way I think about it is manhandling the results for them, like forcing them to be a good student and to show up and to ask questions and to check on them, right, so that I feel better because I haven’t built that emotional capacity. Right? Instead of doing that, I had to hold all of it. And that coach, that version of me, started getting client results predictably and on a larger scale.

And again, because of the middle, the in between what I did. So for example, with my 2k for 2k, when I started noticing, Oh my God, I feel like I need to be in there, one of the things that we do in 2k is that you evaluate. So you do a consult, and then there’s a specific evaluation process where you break down what happened and what you could do differently to sign the client the next time or to make that sale easier or whatever it is. And in the beginning, I would go in, and I would coach. If there was 100 people, it was very easy for me to go in and coach everybody’s consultations. And then there got to be a point where there was 1,000 people, and it was much harder for me to get to all of the consultations.

And so when I thought about, Okay, I want to believe that it’s possible more people equals better, faster results, and I’m not able to get everybody, and I do want to expand my emotional capacity to hold the fact that I won’t be doing all of them, but also, how do I not need to do all of them? How do I teach what I’m doing at scale to the amount of people that are in the room?

And that’s when 
The Consultation Code
 was created, which if you’re in 2k for 2k, it is the one thing people tell me over and over and over it’s worth the entire cost of the program. They would pay $2,000 just for what’s in that book.

What I did is I spent 64 hours—I clocked it. That’s why it’s so specific—64 hours coaching people in 2k on their consultations. They would post an evaluation, I would read their evaluation, I would tell them what went wrong, why it went wrong, and what they need to do differently, what they need to think, what they need to say, where I would have taken it, how the client responded the way that they responded. And then I put those in 
The Consultation Code
.

So people will say, “If I read through that through a weekend, it’s like I’ve just studied a master course in selling.” And then I added to the beginning of the book the five-step close that I teach in 2k, and then how I transition conversationally in between each step so that they could have it out when they’re on a consult and just follow along.

It’s such a valuable resource, and it took me from needing to coach everybody every single time to speeding up that process and even my clients not having to do so much of that consult failure because they’ve learned so quickly through the program and the book.

But I would have never gotten there if I hadn’t been willing to think it’s possible that more people will actually equal better, faster results. The more, 64 hours of coaching people on consults made me an expert on coaching on consults.

And now I can do it so fast on our weekly calls, it’s insane. I can get to the point of the problem so fast. So I got better as a coach, too, because I was willing to change my thinking on that. And now I sometimes think one-on-one can be the slowest way to grow. There are other advantages to it, but the way I think about it now is there’s no way—it’s not always the fastest route.

Another one of my favorite examples with this idea that mindset and emotional expansion create less work, leaner businesses, and higher profits is when I decided, after I had my son, to end live events. I felt very complete with them.

I’d done so many of them that I just felt complete, but also I didn’t want my family to have to travel. We were traveling for eight days at a time to do a three-day live event, plus my 2 Million Dollar Group live—I was doing live events for them too. So it was like four days of live event, two days of travel, and then days in between because we had to be there a day early to plan, and then usually a day after to decompress. And so it was a huge amount of travel multiple times a year, and so I just decided I didn’t want to do it anymore.

And I wanted to become 100% virtual. And then because of that, I wanted to scale down the amount of people I had to manage. I also wanted to have my business be simpler and leaner. I wanted to have less things happening in the business so that I could personally oversee them.

And people have asked me a lot of questions about this in my business. I’ve had colleagues ask me, “How did you turn things around, and how did you de-scale so quickly? How did you get so lean? How did you get your revenue up so much? How did you get your profit up so much?” And really, it isn’t what I did as much as the brain I did it with.

And truly, when I look back to that time, I’m literally postpartum with a new baby, trying to get pregnant for another baby, dropping $6 million of business expenses. I think I cut 12 team members, dropped operations significantly, took back over everything, quality-controlled everything, went 100% virtual, all in 18 months.

And I did it with one thought: I am capable. It’s a simple thought, but I want you to imagine all the times you think you’re not capable of something and you don’t go for it because you think you’re not capable, versus if you decided in that moment to tell yourself you were.

And I actually had leaders on my team—I prepped my team, the leadership team that I did let go, I prepped them of that. They had time to transition out. And I had some of them on their way out the door, offering me that they were very worried about me. And, “This is a lot, and I’m afraid you’re going to be very overwhelmed, and things are not going to go well.” And I would tell them, “Don’t tell me that. It’s going to be simple. I’ve got this.”

And it was simple, but not because it was actually simple, but because I decided it so. People have asked me in my behind the—I’m doing a behind the scenes experience, and they’re like, “How do you stay so organized?” I’m like, “Because I approach things from an organized mind.” “How do you keep things so simple?” “Because I approach it from a simple mindset. I decide something’s going to be simple. I decide I know how to organize this. And then I go do it.” So I went in, and I simplified every business operation. And every time my brain offered, “It’s too much,”—I literally, I remember asking people, these weren’t even jobs I knew how to do. 

I remember sitting down with one of my operations people, and I was like, “Okay, walk me through how you do this thing that’s very complex and very difficult and so time-consuming.” And, “I don’t even know how to do this job, but I know that I think the highest in the room. And so you’re going to walk me through how you do it, and then I’m going to simplify it.” And I did that for two days straight with every business operation in the company.

And I’m like, “Well, that doesn’t make sense. What if we could do it this way?” And they’re like, “Well, I don’t know if I could do it this way.” I’m like, “Well, let’s figure it out. Let’s see if we can do it this way, because it seems like it would be a lot simpler if we did it this way. What if we cut this out and cut this out? And what if you just did this right here?”

One of the examples is they were telling me that it takes weeks to upload all of the email notifications, for example, for 200k to say, “Hey, our weekly call is upcoming,” the call reminders, that takes a really long time. And I was like, Okay, could we not just set up an automation and have it, like we schedule it one time before the Mastermind starts, and then the automation just sends it out. And then if you need to make a change, you go in and change that automation, and you just change one email at a time, but the automation continues and it’s always there.

It was things like that where I just thought about, There’s got to be a simpler way, versus my team members were coming to me with, It’s so complicated and it takes so long and there’s no other way to do it. The thought is what drives the result.

I know that we know this, and yet I see this every single day in these little things here and there where we’re just not practicing what we preach. So every time my brain offered me, It’s too much. I’m overwhelmed. Like, from this experience, I learned that “I’m overwhelmed” is just the feeling of overwhelm is just the thought, “I can’t handle it. I’m not capable. It’s too much.”

So when I felt overwhelmed, I told myself, “I am capable. I have the capacity. It’s not too much. I’ve got this.” And that is how I have the result that I have now. My business grew by a million dollars in revenue. My profit went from 7% to 60% over 18 months. My operations are now very lean. We have a very clean, simple business that’s very doable for me to manage and a business that’s very doable for my team to execute on.

And in fact, now we make all of our decisions—does this allow us to stay lean? Does this allow us to—because people think, “Oh, you’re just being…” I’ve seen comments that it’s like, “Oh, you’re just trying to be cheap, and you’re just trying to make a bunch of money.” No, no, no. Lean business operations have to do with not making tons of mistakes. The more complex your operations, the more opportunity there are for lots of mistakes and then for those to become customer-facing mistakes.

So the leaner your business—and I know for some of you if you’re selling one-on-one, this is the nitty gritty of a bigger complex business, but it applies to one-on-one. If you don’t believe you can go from a 60-minute coaching call to a 30-minute coaching call, if you don’t believe that you can take your prices from $5k to $10k, it’s the same thing. There’s a thought that you’re not capable for whatever area it is in your business.

But as you learn this work, it really is very profound to challenge these complex business things with very simple thoughts and ideas. And anyone that’s been in my business from that time to now, I know would say, “I can see a difference in the client experience, customer service, the way things operate. Everything’s much smoother. There are a lot fewer errors.”

But because I’ve grown this to be so simple and lean, knowing we’ve got—it doesn’t matter how much money we make and how many team members—I was just telling my team, I was like, “Listen, we’re going to make this new offer and we’re going to grow our business by a lot of millions of dollars and by thousands and thousands of clients potentially, and we’re not going to just pile on 10 more team members.” I was like, “It doesn’t always make it simpler. It actually, in fact, makes it a lot more complicated the more people that are involved in a project.”

I was like, “So we want to, every decision we make, we want to filter it through, does this allow us to stay lean?” I’m trying to think of the example we were talking about on our team call this week, but there was something that had to do with, “Can we solve this with technology?” And if we can’t, then we can’t offer it because doing it manually would be too much of a stressor with the volume of people.

And even if we added—we could add three more team members, and still it would be the room and potential for error to do it manually would be greater than the benefit of offering this service. And so if they can’t find a way for technology to solve the problem and the only option is manual, then we won’t offer this one specific thing, which isn’t that big of a deal, but it was like, if we could do it, I think it would be a great thing to offer people.

And so that’s the way we think: if we can’t do it lean, if we can’t do it simple, then we can’t do it because if it’s super complex, there’s got to be a great value in it because the chance for complications and errors just increases. And I’ve learned that the hard way through experience. So my brain now filters everything through simple and lean. And because of that, a million dollars in revenue, 60% profit, a very functioning, well-oiled machine with my team.

So, notice that these thoughts weren’t complex: “I am capable. More people equals better, faster results. I have the capacity. It’s going to be simple. I am organized.” These thoughts aren’t complex. The beliefs that grow you usually aren’t. We’re always looking for the complex one, the very specific thought that is very detailed. No, it doesn’t need to be complex. It needs to be simple. The beliefs that grow you are simple. Those are the ones that often feel the truest when they’re negative and have the biggest impact when they’re positive, the simple ones.

So here’s why this matters: after 10 years in business, I have watched coaches who believe this, most of them inherently, try to solve their business problems with strategy and changing the circumstance. I’ve watched them lower their prices to try to avoid objections. I’ve watched them change their offers because they can’t handle the feeling of when their current offer isn’t selling, or if it was selling, the feeling of having to revive an offer back to life. I’ve watched them hire more people because they tell themselves they’re overextended. I’ve seen them try to pay their way out of having to be more capable. “I’m going to hire contractors. I’m going to hire this. I’m going to hire that,” telling themselves, “I can’t do it, so someone else has to.”

I’ve seen them change their messaging 100 times before they change their belief in their offer and their attitude when they’re selling it. I recently coached a client in my 2 Million Dollar Group that had a huge million-dollar launch and enrolled, I don’t know, maybe 100 people in her offer. And she was telling me how she was going to launch it again, and she thought, “Oh yeah, I think 30 or 40 people will sign up.” And I pointed out to her, “But what if instead of thinking that these 100 people were the biggest part of your demand?” Right? That’s the only reason she would be thinking only 30 or 40 people would be available to sell the next time. And I said, “What if instead you simply thought, ‘I’m just getting started?’ What if the next launch could be bigger? What if you’re building momentum? What if you’re climbing up the mountain, not down it?”

This is everything. Another 20 people dramatically could change the profit of her entire year. And then five to 10 thoughts like that in a year when you’re launching could be the difference of hundreds of thousands of dollars or even the difference of another million doing the exact same work and effort, just having that one thought, “I’m just getting started. This could be just the beginning. I’m building momentum. I’m climbing up the mountain, not down it.” It could be the difference of a million dollars in revenue at that level. Not at maybe at your level if you’re at $200k, but it could be the difference of a couple hundred thousand. It could be the difference between $200k and $400k when you’re selling with those simple thoughts.

I believe your thinking and your willingness to do hard things, your emotional capacity, is directly creating your P&L, your profit and loss statement at the end of the year that your tax person creates for you or that you turn into your tax person to pay your taxes, right, if you are creating a profit and loss statement.

If you’re not, don’t freak out. I’m just saying as the business gets bigger, you will have a profit and loss that you create and that your company pays attention to as far as finances. And it’s your thoughts and emotional capacity that creates the bottom line. Let’s just say that, to create less drama, the bottom line. Every single line item, though, in a profit and loss statement is a product of your thinking.

When I believed I couldn’t lead operations and manage people, I paid someone $360,000 in salary and benefits to do it for me. When I decided I was capable, I got that money back, and my business runs smoother and is more me. It has greater quality control because I’m the one running it.

When I believed my 200k Mastermind was already worth $25,000—this was years and years ago when I increased the price from $10k to $25k—I didn’t go add a bunch of hustly things to create the value to make it more valuable. I started with, I’m going from $10k to $25k. How is it already worth 25k? And my students have just been getting it for a steal.

I thought, How would I show up now if they’d already paid $25k? What would be different about my thinking? How would I show up? What would be the intangible parts of the program if I just believed it was already worth $25k, or people had already paid me $25k?

And then for six months straight, I exercised those thoughts, the messy middle. I exercised those thoughts and walked myself straight from $10k to $25k and then made $25 million with that offer. That’s when things really started skyrocketing for 200k. Not because I just simply raised the price. No, I started scaling that, and people started buying like crazy because the program was so good. And I have the data results to prove that. You can go listen to that episode about the 200k data study.

Students started growing at hypergrowth because I started running 200k differently. I started coaching harder and faster and taking the program a lot more seriously. I started showing up a lot more seriously. I started creating assets for the program. I just saw I had such a bigger vision for it because I changed and became someone bigger because I decided to raise my prices.

And now, after 10 years of that, my emotional capacity has never been higher. My thinking and problem solving has never been higher. My self-confidence has never been higher, and I’m coaching better than ever because my brain keeps evolving and getting stronger. I’m more resilient. I have more energy. I get more done. My ideas are better. They’re more creative. I’m in the current more often. I’m in higher value cycles the majority of the time. I manage my money better. I get higher returns on the investments I make into coaching for myself.

There isn’t a way that thought work and emotional management hasn’t rippled out into positivity in my life. But this isn’t the thing I do on the side or after the fact. It’s not when it’s convenient. It’s not the thing I push off. It’s not the thing I do if I have time. It’s the thing I start with. It’s the thing I challenge the most. It’s the thing I invest in the most.

I only hire business coaches that do high-level mindset and emotional work. I do not hire business coaches that just do strategy, for me, because I just believe so deeply that you have to start with the thinking. The thinking has to drive the strategy, otherwise you will have a heavier business that requires more operations, is more complex, requires more hours to work it, and doesn’t make as much money.

Right now, I have two employees and seven contractors that run my multi-million dollar business. And that’s including my podcast editor and my production manager, my video, my people who do my videos, and my bookkeeper. Those aren’t even people that you would normally consider as contractors. They work for lots of other people, and I run a multi-million dollar company.

We just run things very lean. We’re very smart about how we do our business operations. And our quality control has never been higher. I work three days a week. I manage it all. I organize it all because of the quality of my thinking. I’ve become stronger, smarter, and more capable. So I create more money and a leaner business year after year. That’s the power of doing this work. It’s not the afterthought.

People ask me, “When do you have time to self-coach while you’re doing all these things?” I’m like, “No, no, that’s the first thing I do.” Just like I might plan my week for an hour before I actually get into my week, I plan my brain before I do the things. I spend more time doing that, not give it the leftover time I have. It’s not something, it’s everything.

All right. I hope you enjoyed this episode. I can’t wait for next week’s lesson. Every one just is so exciting and feels so good. I hope you’re loving this as much as I’m loving doing it. I will talk to you next week.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2k for 2k program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2kfor2k. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #367: The Best Business Christmas Ever
transcript:
W
elcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2K, $20K, and $200K using her proven formula.

Hi coaches. Welcome to episode 367. Merry Christmas Eve. Merry Christmas. Or happy holidays, especially if you’re listening to this after the fact.

My podcast producers were telling me that this week is not a highly listened to week on any podcast because people are enjoying Christmas, and I’m feeling that. I’m not going to be necessarily listening to podcasts and studying and doing all the things on Christmas Eve and Christmas. But even though I will be off for two weeks for the holidays, I will be doing some working and doing some thinking, and I will be listening to some podcasts. So I wanted to record one for you.

So I wanted to record one that would be different and fun in case you’re taking the full two weeks off and you’re not thinking, you know, if you’re taking off from basically Christmas Eve through New Year’s and you’re not thinking about work at all, but you want something fun and sweet and inspirational to listen to, I think this could be the episode. I’ve never done an episode like this before.

So, what I want to do with this episode, no matter where you are in your listenership for this week, I want to tell you about the best business Christmas I ever had. So it’s storytelling time. I’m not even sure what the lessons are going to be. There’s going to be a few in there. But I want to just put possibility in your head.

A lot of times, coaches tell me that nobody’s buying during the holidays. I think sometimes we have that thought if we are not buying during the holidays. If you are not thinking of any investments that you would make in your life or your business, if you are checked out of goals and things you want to create in your life by the end of the year or the beginning of next year, you might experience the belief that people aren’t buying. But I’m always like the week of Thanksgiving, I actually was considering two different business investments. And in fact, I was texting with one coach about it, and I forgot it was the day before Thanksgiving.

And so I think if you are actively looking to make a big change for yourself, you are thinking other people are buying because you’re buying. And the same at the beginning of the year. So that could be one thing, but you may also just not have any amazing stories of people buying during the holidays. And so I want to share this one with you.

So this story starts the winter, the, I guess, actually it would be considered fall, but the December of my first full year of business. The year that I made $150,000, which would have been 2016. So this story starts in 2016.

I had at this point, at the end of the year, a full coaching practice, and I had started, I had started a group that, if you bought my 1-on-1 coaching, you got to do the group. So all my 1-on-1 clients would come together every week, and we would coach as a group. And it was super fun because at that point, they were all creating something major in their life. They all didn’t have businesses. Some of them did, but some of them were creating just big things. Like I had a professional athlete in there and some network marketers and a coach or two. Like I had people doing big things. And so we all would come together and work on that. And I had one person who was just deeply working to change her life. So it was a lot of mindset work.

So it’s important to know those two things were happening at the same time. I had a full 1-on-1 coaching practice and a group. And my group, I don’t remember the exact details around it, but my group started talking amongst themselves, I’m guessing in the Facebook group, about wanting to get together and see each other in person.

And it started coming up so often that I had this thought, I’m going to have to create a retreat, or they’re going to do one without me. It felt like the demand was so high. Like they were literally talking about when they could get together with each other. And I thought, I mean, they could do it on their own, that’s fine, but I could also offer them an experience.

And so I created my very first retreat. And I did not have, at the time, or I mean, I really don’t have that thought at any time, but I really didn’t have the thought at the time that no one would buy because the holidays were coming up. In fact, my thought was, I love the holidays. What if we created, I created a holiday retreat? That would be, in my brain, that was like the most exciting thing that you could do.

And the first two years of my business, I think this could be the first lesson you can take from this episode, the first two years of my business, I did a lot of what felt fun and exciting and a dream come true for me. If it lit me up, I did it.

Even if like all of my offers, my second retreat, this really is a story about my first retreat, but my second retreat, I called a Midnight in Paris in Michigan. I love to tell this story because it was just such an outrageous concept. I loved the movie Midnight in Paris, and I had this like before and after triumph story that really happened in Michigan where I got my heart really broken and very publicly humiliated and then kind of staged a comeback where I made $100,000 and then my last ever store, what we called store run for my pitching job was in Michigan, in the same city where I had been humiliated and had been just heartbroken. Muskegon, Michigan.

And so I wanted that retreat to represent this like triumphant journey, this deep dive into a woman’s soul, into her heart, into her mind, into her expansion. And I wanted it to have this like dreamlike vibe. And we did, we did like, what do you call them? The like kind of erotic photo shoots. I can’t think of what they’re… boudoir photo shoots. That’s what it was. We did yoga on the beach. We had this insane catering company come in and do like a carnival masquerade night.

And I drove, literally drove 9 hours to the French Quarter in New Orleans to have custom masquerade masks made for my retreat attendees. And we stayed in this insane French-inspired, which is so crazy, right? Midnight in Paris is I was into that movie. And then I find a French-themed house in Michigan. I mean it was the wildest thing.

But I look back, and I’m like, I can’t believe people bought this. I can’t believe this sold, but it was my heart and soul that was actually selling. And it ended up being one of the most incredible experiences. I did two retreats back-to-back. So that was my second retreat.

But I just have this belief that anything can sell, especially if your heart and soul is into it, especially if you don’t have negative thoughts around it. If you’re not having limiting thoughts around it. And so my thought was, I love Christmas. I cannot wait to throw a Christmas retreat for my people. And so I rented this beautiful log cabin in the Smoky Mountains. And which is like a few, you know, maybe a 6-hour drive for me.

I bought a Christmas tree and put it up in this house for a three-day retreat. We did champagne cocktails with cranberry, like cranberry mimosas. We did hot cocoa. I mean, it was like the most I made, had custom ornaments made with all the retreat, like the participants’ names on them. We had these this beautiful sign. We called it the Diva Christmas retreat, I think. This was when I was selling something called Diva Business School at the time.

And it was just like the, I had someone else make a homemade, one of those like picture frames that you can hold, and then someone takes a photo of you, so you’re like holding a fake frame with your head in it, and they take a photo. And then I bought all these like Christmas face, I am at a loss for all the words today. But you know, when you put something in front of your face and it’s like a mask and there’s a stick on it? Why can’t I think of what that’s called? Like photo props. We had a ton of Christmas photo props, like the googly glasses and reindeer ears and things like that.

And then everyone dressed up like crazy. Like women were wearing gowns for one of our like fancy dinners and I remember I was wearing the cutest Kate Spade dress. It was bright, like satin red with black bows on the back. It was like mostly backless, but it had black bows on the back. It was so gorgeous. The whole thing was just like a Christmas vibe. I mean, it was like a winter wonderland.

And I sold a VIP experience with it. So I had a couple of girls come early, and I took them to the Grand Old Opry, and we had morning like hot coffee overlooking the beautiful Smoky Mountains, and just had like the most intense conversations about what we wanted in our life and what they were creating. And I coached them. And it was just absolutely stunning.

I had I think 20 girls come. Like 20 women took time out of their lives to come to a Christmas retreat in the month of December for an entire weekend. We coached, we did gift, like Secret Santas. It was stunning. It was truly the most magical experience ever.

And I walked away with the belief that if you create an incredible experience, people will come. If you create a vibe, like something that feels like I have to experience this. I have to be there. I can’t miss this energy. I can’t miss this these memories. I can’t miss this experience, this luxury thing for me to fill my soul. Like I can’t miss this. I think if you have that, whether it’s an online offer or an offline offer, people will come.

It 100% has to do with you selling the offer, making that offer right. You can literally sell something, a Christmas retreat in the Smoky Mountains, the Diva retreat, and you can sell something called a Midnight in Paris in Michigan if your heart and soul is connected to it. 

But then as I’m selling this retreat, I have a client. I would call her a VIP client because she didn’t want anyone to know who she was, that she was coaching with me. She had coached with a really big name in the network marketing industry and had told people about it because she was so excited about it. And then everyone wanted to coach with this coach, and she felt like now it wasn’t this like private personal experience that she’d been hoping to have.

And so when she hired me, she was like, listen, I have a huge audience, but I really don’t want you to tag me in things and post about me because I want this experience to be my own. I actually remember at the time thinking, that’s so strange. But I actually feel that now. I mean, I honored it 100%, but I remember thinking, okay.

And now I’m in a program where I feel a little bit like that. Like, I don’t talk about who I’m coaching with because I’m having an experience where I get to fully be the client, and I’m loving it. And I don’t want a bunch of my clients in the group. Like I want to have the experience for myself, at least for now. So I really get that now.

And so she wanted to do this retreat, but she just didn’t want to be seen at the retreat. She didn’t, I don’t think she wanted me to have to edit her out of photos or like stand out of photos. Like, it just wasn’t the vibe she was looking for. And it sold out so easily. We only had so many rooms and so many beds and so many places to be. So it sold out so fast that it was like only sign up if this is the perfect offer for you.

And so I started thinking about it, and I said, so, you know, I know you’re wanting something that’s like very intimately private. What about a VIP weekend where I can come and for four days straight, I can coach you morning, afternoon, evening, day and night, 24/7, doing the most luxurious things anywhere in the country that you want to go?

And she was like, I’ve always wanted to be a snow bunny and go to Aspen at Christmas. She was like, I don’t want to take my kids. I don’t want to bring my family. Like I want to one day, but like I want something for me. And I want to do something that’s this luxury experience for me.

And so I sold her a $20,000 VIP four-day event the week before Christmas in Aspen, Colorado. And I went all out. Private helicopter rides over the Aspen Mountains, landing on private property that you can only land on or get access to through via helicopter. L’Oreal had shot a commercial the week before there. Like, champagne toast on this private property in the middle of the mountains with helicopter-only access.

We did, we stayed at the St. Regis in Aspen, which is where I love to stay when I go to Aspen. Spa days, going, we didn’t ski. I didn’t ski at the time. She didn’t ski, but we went up the to the mountain and had hot cocoa. It was just walked around town. Like, it was the most incredible, luxurious, like high vibe experience.

We did the most insane dinners out. Aspen has like the best food scene. And we really got to the root of one of her like deep issues that she came to coaching for and worked through it over an extended period of time. And it was just incredible.

And I remember feeling that year like anything was possible. It was just the most fun I ever had. I was gone for so long in the month of December that I did not put my Christmas tree up until December 24th. But I was so full of magic and dreams and just heart and soul and holiday magic that when I did get home, I was like, who cares? I’m staying up all night and putting my Christmas tree up. And then the next day, I left for my family’s house to go celebrate in a different city.

So I didn’t even, like I put it up just to come home after Christmas to my Christmas tree. That’s how full of Christmas spirit I was after a three-day retreat in the Smoky Mountains and a four-day VIP in Aspen, Colorado.

Like, I don’t know if you guys have been to Aspen in the winter, and especially at Christmas time, it literally to me feels like if you’ve seen A Nightmare Before Christmas, when Jack Skellington goes into Christmas time, when he opens the door, and he enters the land of Christmas time, to me, this is Aspen at Christmas. It has the same exact vibe. It feels a little bit like Whoville. I love it so so much.

So I put my Christmas tree up and then went to celebrate Christmas with my family, and came home and kept my Christmas tree up and the magic in my heart alive until I think April of that year.

In fact, if you’re in 2k for 2k and you take my Interrupt training that is in the bonus section, people say to this day they love that training so much, but they laugh because I filmed that in March or April, and I filmed it in front of my Christmas tree that was still up and like it was no big deal. Like that wasn’t abnormal in any way, shape, or form because I just felt so good about it.

It was the best business Christmas ever. It blew my mind for what’s possible. It made me think that coaching could literally be magic, that having a business could be 100% on your terms.

Like, I think why I feel so passionately now and what’s been coming out in my Entrepreneur Series is this overarching lesson that you just can’t take the typical, you know, entrepreneur business rules and apply it to coaches because if you do, coaching will start to feel really dry. It will start to feel like your corporate job, like another heavy thing you have to do every day, like another hard thing.

It won’t feel like this magical, beautiful expression of my own ideas and creativity and my heart and my soul and what lights me up and you won’t then find clients who match that same energy where your best idea that feels like magic to you, that feels like everything you would ever want, like just radiating outside of you, this is my greatest expression of love. Like, there are people in the world that will connect with that and be like, mine too.

People loved my students loved my Midnight in Michigan retreat. The photos were insane. Like, lives were changed from that event. At least two of the people that were there are still my clients to this day and have $100,000 coaching businesses themselves now. Like real transformation happened there. It wasn’t just like selling random stuff and having a good time and, you know, raking in money and not caring. It was like deep transformation was happening.

And so I think about that often with coaches, like, does your coaching business feel like a dream? Does it feel like something that is your greatest expression of your creativity? Does it feel like love? Does it light you up? Does it blow your mind? Are you having the absolute time of your life? If you’re not, you might be doing it wrong. And I know there’s a solution.

100% it can feel this way, especially when you don’t have a business that’s like really bogged down with funnels and ads and like I just feel so passionately about building your business one 1-on-1 client at a time until you can’t sell 1-on-1 anymore and you have to go to group and then building it one group at a time until you can’t sell group anymore and you have to go to a program or a course because selling 1-on-1, doing retreats, like not having like a business that has like it’s not having an operational-heavy business is so much fun. So much fun.

Now, I am having so much fun in my business right now, but I will tell you, I haven’t had this much fun in my business in many years because it has been so operationally heavy for a long time. And I think I needed to go through that to get here and to extract wisdom from having both because I do coach people who have operationally heavy businesses as well. And if I ever want to go to 20 or 30 million, it will also be operationally heavy.

But I always tell people, your first 100k, 200k, 300k, 400k, you have got to enjoy the crap out of it because it really is a time where you could throw things at the wall and see what sticks. It really is a time where you could be like, this would be fun, let’s go do that. It’s really a time where you can say, deep in my soul, I’ve always wanted to do this, let’s do that.

I also remember a couple of years later, actually the year that I was going to start scaling my business, I sold a retreat in Cabo, San Lucas, to maybe like 10 or 12 women. We stayed in this insane house that is, if you’ve ever stayed at it’s the Waldorf Astoria in Cabo, San Lucas, now, but it used to be called Resort Pedregal. And if I pronounce that right. And it’s like right above the resort. You can see this insanely beautiful mansion on a cliff, and it was that house.

And that retreat was like if you could just say, what would be the most fun and life-giving experience I could ever have is take all of my favorite people to my favorite place in the entire world. Be in the sun. We went on a yacht and saw actual whales jumping out of the water. Like what dreams are made of with like imagine your best clients watching whales jump out of the water with you in like beautiful 80-degree weather in your birthday month. Like those types of things. And that is the retreat where I created the three-year plan. Like I, the very first iteration of the three-year plan was offered at that retreat.

Like, I just think when you’re in such connection and alignment, and you’re just feeling the vibes, and you’re doing your like heart’s work, the best ideas come out of you. Your coaching business, especially in the beginning, it should feel this way. It should feel like you’re having the time of your life. It should feel like all of the things.

I know I’ve said that a lot in this episode, it should feel like it should just be magic. It should be pure magic coming from your heart and soul. It should be your biggest transformations, offering it to other people, bringing in the best people that light you up, that you’re so proud and honored to coach. It should be breaking all the barriers of what you think is possible for business, the greatest expression of your personality, and what you care about. I mean, it really should feel like art.

I want that for you so much. This was my best business Christmas ever. The Diva Business School, Christmas Retreat for my Divas, the Aspen VIP Experience. And then my Christmas tree up until March. Carrying the magic of the holiday season with me the entire way through.

And y’all, let me just tell you one last story because this is so crazy. These experiences are not without friction. Like I’m in the middle of doing a behind-the-scenes experience of making a new offer for my business. And one of the things I want, because I think sometimes when I tell these stories, like people imagine it a little bit like Instagram.

I was watching a reel the other day on Instagram of this woman, who I don’t know if she’s a trad wife. I don’t and I have nothing against that. PS. I think everyone should do them. But like her whole thing is like how beautifully kept her house is, and how she like perfectly cleans it for her children and her husband while they’re away, and that’s from what I’ve gleaned, that’s the thing.

And I was watching it, and I remember catching my brain, and my brain was like, wait a minute. Nothing is, like cleaning a house is not. She’s making it look effortless because it’s like, you know, the sped up like little caption of it, but actually, this is hours and hours of work. We’re talking like cleaning up every ounce of mess made by their Christmas decorations, folding the laundry, making all of the beds in the household, dishes, all the vacuuming of this, like what must be a 10,000, at least 10,000 square foot house, if not bigger. Like this is like what whole cleaning teams come in to do, but in the video, she makes it look like nothing is really happening, like completely effortless. And so I know that sometimes that happens on the podcast, on social media, like you see the perfection of things, but there was friction during these experiences as well.

So I’ll tell you about two of them. When I marketed the retreat and sold it out the week before we were supposed to go, the Smoky Mountains burnt down. Like Gatlinburg, Pigeon Forge burnt down. I’m not exaggerating, you can Google it. It was wild. Every day we were like, is the cabin still standing? When I was thinking of my VIP things, like the Grand Old Opry and doing things with my clients, I’m like, what can we actually do?

When I was leaving from the retreat, I saw so much of the fire damage. Like we were heartbroken. We were so sad for all the people at Christmas that their houses burnt down, maybe their vacation properties burnt down, staples in the towns burnt down. Like we were so devastated for them and so scared for us. Like were the fires going to be contained? Were we going to be able to get to do it? Were we going to need to refund? It was wild.

And they got it contained under control and then out within days of our retreat happening, which is so wild. Like I remember just holding, if you’ve listened to my uncertainty tolerance podcast, that was one of those moments, just holding the uncertainty of the fires and then holding the dream and the vision in the other hand.

And then when we went to me and my coach at the time did the VIP retreat in Aspen. And on our way there, I think our flight was at 4 p.m., and I remember we got to the Louisville airport, and I was like, I’m a little hungry. I think I might go get a snack. And I was like, no, I’ll wait if we when we land in Denver, and we had a connector to Aspen. I’m like, Denver’s going to have so many more options. I’ll wait.

And then our flight got delayed and then delayed and then it got delayed to the point where like no announcements were made. Like, oh, the airport food is closing. Nope. They didn’t make any announcements. And suddenly, every single thing in the airport was closed, and you could not get food or even water. You could not get even water in the airport. And it wasn’t until like 8 hours into the delay that they’d offered water to people standing around being like, what is happening? You can’t keep us in this airport without food or water.

So we finally left sometime after midnight, and we’d been there since, I think 2 if our flight was at 4. Sometime after midnight, we land at like 2:30 in the morning. We’ve missed our Aspen flight, and our client is landing the next day. They’re also getting a snowstorm in Aspen. Like, I think every time I’ve gone to Aspen, we have landed right as a giant snowstorm dumps onto Aspen. We’ve gotten lucky every time and gotten there, and we’ve never gotten stranded, but it always seems like they’re like, oh, we’re about to, you know, we land and then 36 inches of snowfall.

And so it was one of those things happening, and I remember eating pizza at 2:30 in the morning from a gas station, sleeping two hours, and then having to get up and get back to the airport for a 6:00 a.m. flight to Aspen, no sleep. And then we were behind a day of execution, like prepping for this VIP weekend, and like talking to people, you know, we would just set the stage for everything. So every single place we went was like expecting our client and ready to, you know, welcome her and call her by name and treat her to an incredible experience.

And all of that we had to do on no sleep in approximately 4 hours before our client landed. And then we were afraid she wasn’t going to land because of the snow. And so we’re sweating a $20,000 experience where we’ve already booked all these things, and maybe she doesn’t even land. It was wild.

Holding uncertainty tolerance like crazy and or building that up, holding the uncertainty, building up the tolerance, and then holding the vision and the magic in the other hand. And it all ended up working out so beautifully by the time my client arrived. Like, there was no indication that any of that had happened.

That was one of the rules of a retreat and a VIP that I learned early on is that no matter what happens, the client can never know. So whatever is going on behind the scenes, like that, the client cannot hold that stress. You hold it, you figure it out, you make sure the client feels like a million dollars. I do think these experiences are why I’m so good at hosting live events and retreats, is because I have been through the fire with them.

So they were not without friction, but if you can get through the friction, if you can believe deep enough, I mean, it was the most magical experience ever.

So I just wanted to share that with you. I wanted to share that there’s always possibility during the holidays. And if you have a beautiful dream in your heart, execute it. Don’t let the holidays hold you back. Don’t let the idea that people wouldn’t buy it, that you’re the only person ever that would want it. No, decide you’re going to compel them to want it too, because you see something that they don’t see yet, and you know it’s going to be immensely life-changing and valuable. That’s what you do. That’s the work.

And if your business does not feel magical and fun and like you could create anything, you might just need to develop a mindset or some skill sets that allow you to do that. That is it. You need support, you need a bigger, more open mind. Like you just need different things. Like, we have to rewrite the ship because it really can be this fun, this magical, this level of connection, it can be this creative, it can be this mind-blowing, it can be this transformational. I want that for you.

All right. I hope I caught you at some point after the holidays, before the holidays, whenever. I really wanted, I didn’t want to do a previously done episode. I just wanted to get on here and talk to you and wish you a merry Christmas, and offer you this, these few stories to encourage you for what is possible.

All right, have an amazing rest of your week. Hug your babies, hug your parents, hug your grannies. Eat lots of amazing food. Appreciate every gift and give from your heart. I love you all so, so much. Talk to you next week.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2K for 2K program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2Kfor2K. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #366: Lessons from 10 Years in Business: Your Business is an Asset
transcript:
W
elcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2k, $20k, and $200k using her proven formula.

Hey coaches, this is lesson 5. Today, we’re going to be covering lesson 5 of my lessons from being in business for 10 years. And this one is going to save some businesses. Like for real. I think there will be before this episode and after this episode. So make sure you dig in.

So we’re going to talk today about your business being an asset, thinking of your business like an asset, and treating your business like an asset. And I’m going to explain what that means. So I used to say that your business is your baby. And if you are a parent, you will really get what I mean by that. Even if you’re a fur baby parent, okay? All the parents.

In the beginning, especially, one of the things that made me so successful so quickly is the idea that it was my job to take care of the business, not the business’s job to take care of me. That I had to feed it constantly with coaching and skillset development, and effort and time to go out and market it. I had to care for it 24/7. I would lose sleep over it, I would be exhausted with it, I would nurse it constantly as it grew into a big old business or an asset. I could never need anything from it or have high expectations of it, right? We don’t have high expectations of babies or toddlers. I couldn’t expect behavior, certain behavior, because it wasn’t mature enough yet to give me the results, the behavior that I demanded.

But if I kept nursing it and showing it how I wanted it to be, one day it would be this beautiful, handsome, well-behaved thing that I wanted to show off to the world, to everyone. One of the hardest lessons I think is that your business is not responsible for your living and lifestyle and bills when you get into business because you want it to pay for your lifestyles and bills.

That’s the absolute hardest thing. What do you mean? That’s the only reason I started this thing. I really know how that feels. And even worse, I think what makes it more painful is that we don’t realize that’s the deal that we’re making when we start. We don’t realize that we’re having a baby, and we’re about to metaphorically or physically be very sleep-deprived and financially strapped for the next few years while we grow a tiny baby business.

So then, when you’re confronted with this level of hard, the level of hard of having a newborn and a toddler, I see very, like, there are very stark similarities between the two. Right, the level of hard of having a newborn and a toddler.

Like this, and then having a business. Like, often this is when people tell themselves when they are in the hard, when they’re in the, you know, metaphorical or physical sleepless nights, when they’re in the failure, when they’re in the I don’t know how to do any of this. I don’t know how to keep this alive. I don’t know how to make money. It’s not making money. What do I do? When they’re in this, and they didn’t realize this is what they signed up for, then we tell ourselves, like, I’m not cut out for it, I can’t handle it, it’s too much, it’s not working, I quit. 

With real babies, you can’t quit. You’re forced through the hard. And you do get to the other side because you can’t quit. This is something I remind myself of often. Now, actually, you can quit. So this is also really important. You choose not to quit being a parent because you are unconditionally committed. Right? You don’t like get 4 months in and be like, this is so hard, all right. Bye baby. Some people maybe, but the majority of people, if you are listening, maybe you have not done that. Because you are unconditionally committed. You have to be unconditionally committed to your business as well. 

And I’m not saying that it comes before your kids. I’m saying I always tell my clients who have kids, I’m like, you have two kids. Okay, great. Now you have three. You have four kids, great, now you have five. When you have multiples, then I think it becomes less and less a thing, right? The 1 to 2 is stark, but it’s a big, it’s a big difference. 0 to 1 and 1 to 2 feels like a big difference. But I could see if we had a third one that would be like, all right, we know what we’re doing here. So you’re just, you’re not replacing your actual children, you’re just adding a child. It’s a baby child or a business child. It’s a baby child. It’s a business child.

But you really do have to be unconditionally committed to it so that you show up and feed it enough, and you put in enough tender care and nurturing that it can grow up and thrive. So what the feeding it and the nurturing it looks like is you growing your mindset as an entrepreneur, as a coach, and as a leader. You growing your emotional range for courage, uncertainty, tolerance, resilience, disappointment, all humiliation, shame, all of the hard things. 

Growing your capacity to handle hard things. Growing your capacity to create time where it currently feels like it doesn’t exist to make way for these growth activities and the learning and caring for the business. That’s the biggest thing, right? You’re going to probably be working full-time and parenting full-time. And you’re going to be like, how do I make time for this business?

Well, how would you make time for another baby? Maybe you would, I don’t know, take a sabbatical. Maybe you would, yeah, you’d figure it out. You’d be up in the mornings, you’d be up late at night. You’d get less sleep. You’d not have time for social stuff as much. You wouldn’t be watching as much TV, you wouldn’t be doing as much things for yourself. Like that is the truth in the beginning. It’s not always like that.

But I think we’re afraid to have this conversation because so much selling has been done, not just in the coaching industry, in network marketing industries, about like how easy it is to just start a business and make money on the side, and it really is an illusion.

It is not, there’s no such thing as passive income in the beginning. Anyone who is telling you that is it’s a little bit of a lie. Like no matter what, it takes time to educate yourself, to figure out how to create some sort of passive income stream. It doesn’t just happen. Right, so everything that you create in the beginning is a baby, and it’s going to require this level of care.

And so the only option is to grow your capacity to manage what you’re already managing so that you have more energy to manage and handle more. That’s it. And I tell my clients that is at the beginning, but that is also going to millions. I get multiple 6-figure earners or a 7-figure earner that wants a multiple 6-figure earners that want to go to 7 or a 7-figure earner that wants to go to 8. And they’re exhausted by their current business, and they don’t have extra time.

Or people will ask me, you’re launching now, and you have all this time because you’re not coaching. What do I do if I’m coaching 20 hours and I want to start selling group and I want to have time for launches and marketing? You have to grow your capacity. This is not a time issue. It’s a capacity issue.

And when you’re at your max, that will always be when it’s the hardest, but you have to figure out how to handle hard. Not find a way to bypass the hard. You will never be good at entrepreneurship if what you’re searching for are ways to bypass hard. You will become excellent at entrepreneurship if you’re always finding ways to grow your capacity to handle hard, to create more energy, and to find time where it doesn’t feel like there is, and to manage your time better and to produce more in the time that you have. That will make you a phenomenal, very rich entrepreneur. 

Feeding it also looks like growing your confidence to put yourself out there and to be visible. It looks like expanding your money beliefs to create money from your personal service. It’s a very personal thing to sell a coaching service or a program or like your content. And to believe that people will pay you and to believe that you can make way more money than generationally you’ve, anyone in your family’s ever made. It was so wild. Oh my God.

We had a 200k Mastermind call recently. We do bonus revenue coaching calls. So we have our weekly call, and then we do revenue reporting or revenue tracking. And I have, I’ve done a podcast about why we do this, but we do that every month, and we cheer people on in the Facebook group, but people also have my tracking system that they’re able to upload their revenue in and really see their growth.

And the those that participate in that, I give them an extra call every month to come on, and all we do is coach on their thoughts about their revenue and their money and the feelings around it. And so the first call of this new class, we had, I mean, it was like the greatest call that’s ever been. We cried through the whole thing, mostly.

And there was a really big transformation about that, like that it’s okay for women to cry in business spaces. But the thing that was like one of the things that was radiating through the room is that it got brought up that we are all, every single woman in the room, was the first to make the kind of money that they’re making in the generations of their family. They were the first ones to break generational money barriers. Can you, like, I can’t even explain it to you.

The profoundness of being on a call where every single person or most of them are saying, I am breaking generational income barriers. I am making more money than any person in my family that’s come before me. Like that’s wild.

Me too. And if you’re in 200k or if you’re not there yet, like that’s, it might be my new mission is to help women become the highest earners that have ever been in the generations of their family. Like, break that barrier. Yes.

And we have to work on our money beliefs to be able to do that. We have to work on interpersonal relational issues within our family to do that. We have to break out of the family dynamic a little bit to do that. There’s a lot there. I could go on about that forever, but I’ll move on.

We also have to grow, or we, you have to grow your skillset to market, sell, and deliver. Just that alone is has been my entire business offer suite for 8 years in business. I’m going to teach you how to market, sell, and deliver, and create a really profitable business. I’m going to teach you how to make money as a life coach. Like that in itself has been enough to be almost 10 years of content coaching and business delivery.

Learning how, and I call, I really teach a lot, like in my revenue challenge, learning how to create money from nothing in my 200k Mastermind. That is the skillset. Going from zero to 2k. We also start, we start that process in the 2k for 2k. Learning how to go from literally I’ve never made a dollar as an entrepreneur to my first $2,000 and then my first $4,000 and $6,000 and $10,000 and then $20,000 and then $200k. That is a skill set. That learning that is feeding the baby.

Feeding it is also growing your audience, growing the value that you give, adding to your value bank. It’s nurturing the people you meet as a coach, and then the audience that you start gathering on maybe the socials, or on an email list, or through a podcast. All of these things are how you grow the baby, how you feed the baby.

And just like those sleep-deprived nights, if you have had a newborn in your life, where it feels like it will never end, and you have entered the tunnel or the land of hopelessness. It will. But this is where the analogy starts to differ. It ends with growing your value and skillset in selling and your mind as an entrepreneur, not automatically.

So with kids, if you keep feeding them, and I guess it doesn’t really end automatically with them either. Like, you have to maybe sleep train them, you have to do things to get your children to the different stages, right? They have growth stages, but there are things parents do to foster that along. And if most humans can do that. If you do it, then they get to the point where they do maybe sleep through the night. We are not there yet, but I eventually think we will get there. They go to school.

Like I was telling my husband, our lives are going to be so dramatically different in 3 years because both of our kids will be potty trained, both of them will be out in school full-time, and we will have our days back. And then if they’re in school full-time, likely they’re going to sleep probably really well at night. And then maybe they’re going to be in sports, which is also going to help them sleep. So I was like, or extracurricular activities, whatever it is.

I’m like, our lives could be dramatically different in just a few years. And it feels a little bit more like that’s inevitable, versus your business doesn’t get out of the baby phase unless you grow your value and skillset in selling, and then you grow your mind as an entrepreneur. And that can take as long as it takes.

I have had people come to me and not grow these two things and be in business for 10 years, not making any money. And then they spend a couple years with me, and they’re making 2 million dollars a year. That example is rare, but it’s a profound example of this specific thing where it’s not automatic, it requires value and skillset in selling, and your mind is growing your mind as an entrepreneur.

So I have two big ideas around this that I want to kind of unpack. One big idea that I will drop here, and I’m not here to tell you that you’ve done anything wrong or what you should do. But the advice I will offer from love, the story I will tell you about my success, that’s what this series is about, is because in the beginning up until $100k, and now I would even say in like the current economy, I would say even maybe $200k, I treated my business like a baby and did not make it responsible for taking care of me. I worked full-time. My job paid my bills and allowed me to feed the baby.

I invested in what I felt I needed when I needed it. And that’s where my personal money went. And then when I started making money in my business, that’s where my business money went. I invested a lot of it up until my first $100k. And I have been aggressively investing ever since. And I have lots of podcasts about that.

I talk about it often because I want you all to know, like as much as the things I teach skill-wise and the lessons that I teach you here on the episode that have to do with mindset, as much of that has to contribute to my success, my willingness to invest in my business has to. I just because I’m a business coach who you could potentially invest with, I can’t hold back that message for seeming salesy. Like, I just have to tell you I’ve invested a lot in my business.

And so when I left my full-time job, I was making $8,000 a month. Like when I gave my notice. And I was living substantially below that income so that I could still invest and pay my taxes. And so that’s why I’m saying that amount might be higher now because it’s been 10 years. So it doesn’t make you a failure if you are still working your full-time job while you are growing your business. It makes you smart.

And it doesn’t make you more successful to leave your business; it might make you insufficient. It might make you scared. It might make you unbalanced, imbalanced. Created a new word there. Right, there’s not like this equals that. Leaving your job equals success, and staying at your job equals failure. That’s not the way it works. For me, I wanted to be able to invest. I wanted to feel sufficient on every call and not push a client because I needed money to pay bills.

I didn’t want that level of desperation. So every day I walked into Walmart, for those of you that think you have a hard time. I walked into Walmart and all of its glory, all the Walmarts across the country, all of them. And I would walk through the doors and say, I choose to be here so that I can pay my bills and take care of myself powerfully, invest in my business, and grow my asset, grow my business baby. Some version of that every day.

Because I used to have like there was a moment where I had a really intense coaching call with my coach and I was thinking about quitting, but it was in a creative space where I couldn’t pay for my coaching and I couldn’t pay my, I wouldn’t be able to pay my bills. And it was a really big like, I don’t know, you got to step up to the plate here. Like that’s not being a mature business owner. And it was hard, but she was right. And I was like, okay, like I’m not going to just like not pay my bills and not pay my coach when I owe my coach money. Like I’m not going to do that. I’m going to figure it out, even though it’s going to be really hard.

So every day I choose this. I choose to come here so that I can create money to pay for my bills, to take care of myself, and to pay, to invest in my business so that it can grow more.

And every day that I empowered myself in that way, I felt more and more grateful for Walmart and for being there. And I had less and less of a level of desperation that maybe other people experience when they’re trying to build their businesses. And so I was really, truly in a good place every time I got on a consult.

Now, I wasn’t in a great place. I wasn’t making tons of money. I was definitely like every week, where are my coaching payments coming from? And I got to scrap it together. I got to work a couple extra hours. I got to bring on another shift. I’ve got to vie for better stores and like really try to, you know, go across the country wherever the best store is. Like I would literally drive 8 to 10 hours just to get to a best store so I could make more money. I was committed.

So, another idea I want to drop here that I’ve already kind of mentioned, but I want to say it a little more plainly, is we get the equation wrong. We’re used to believing that time equals money. So we think if we quit our jobs, we will finally have the time to be successful. But in entrepreneurship, time doesn’t equal money. Skill equals money, value equals money. There’s no set time for how long it will take you to develop that skill.

An entitlement to that happening in a certain time frame will have you taking actions that lead to a lot of unnecessary pain, frustration, low self-confidence, and it will have you putting your business into financial distress by believing if you quit your job, you will finally have the energy to be successful. No, that’s not that may not happen. It’s not that it won’t happen, it may not happen.

I think what makes you successful is finding the energy when you think there is none. The learning curve is very steep for entrepreneurship. If it wasn’t, everyone would be doing it, and everyone would be rich. Now, just because everyone isn’t doing it doesn’t mean everyone can’t do it. Everyone can, just not everyone will. I want you to do it.

And I believe this is the power of having constant coaching and having community of other people doing the hard thing with you, normalizing that hard, normalizing that journey, seeing lots of examples of what feeding the baby and nurturing the business look like. But you’ve got to think of it that way. Everything is an investment for creating a healthy baby that turns into a healthy child that turns into a well-adjusted adult. That is what we’re doing with our businesses in the beginning.
