Except I actually think it’s harder to not go after your dreams than to go after them. I think it’s harder to have a life where you’re just living the life that you’re on the track for. I actually think it’s much harder to do that, to not confront what you most want in life.

So you’ve got to have dedication to evaluation for everything you do and everything you spend money on, or you will experience a lot of unnecessary failure and financial and emotional pain. If you evaluate, you will experience a lot less. So those are my two rules. They increase my risk tolerance, both financially and emotionally. I always get a return. I always learn from my pain.

So I want you to think of the entrepreneur identity as I have an evaluating mindset. I evaluate everything. I learn from everything. I figure out what works, what doesn’t work, what I’m going to do differently. I find the failure gold, and I tolerate risk. That’s my entrepreneur identity.

And the final piece of it is that as a first priority, as an entrepreneur, above all else, my priority is to get revenue in the door. First and foremost, when I think about my business, when I think about being an entrepreneur, and I think about the things I need to do in my spare time to build this business, to sell life coaching, it’s to get money in the door.

You do not have a business without sales. So a business isn’t an email list. It’s not perfect client messaging. It’s not a funnel. It’s not a perfect IG thread with perfect little graphics. It’s not the perfect Reel, and it’s not a website. And you want to think about how much time you spend on things that aren’t actually direct activities interacting with another human to get cash in the door, cold hard cash in the door.

What I have found for people who come to me, a lot of coaches come in and they care more about looking professional and not having anyone think of them as not professional. They care more about that than actually making money. They care more about what it looks like than it actually is. And I’ve had marketers even tell me, like big-time marketers in the industry tell me, “I didn’t have a business until I had an email list.” I had someone tell me I don’t have a business until I have a LinkedIn account. Someone told me that at a networking event years and years ago.

An email list and a LinkedIn account are not businesses. That is not the indicator of a business. I had lots of colleagues with email lists and were not making any money, coming to me asking me how I was doing it. And I had no email list, but I was being paid $150,000 a year, and I had a full client list, and I launched my first several groups, and I had sold my first retreat and my first VIP weekends.

So you tell me who had the real business? The people who figured out how to work an Active Campaign to set up an email list and spent a week in their office doing that, and then inviting people to this list, or the people who went out and got clients and started getting paid and started coaching without any of it?

And it doesn’t mean you can’t have it, but if you want to succeed the fastest and be the most essential, you want to cut all of that noise out. You don’t want to care about what it looks like. You want to care about what it is, and what’s the fastest way that I could sell another human life coaching so that I can get cash in the door. You never want to lose sight of this. You want to get a bank account with money in it. You want to have revenue streams in the door, and you never want to lose sight of this day after day.

So, something I’m going to say over and over in this training, I want you to ask yourself every day, does this activity directly engage me with real people who can pay me real money to coach them? Does this activity directly bring in cash? If it doesn’t, beware, because you can be playing business and feeling very busy and working very hard without actually making money. It becomes a very fancy and expensive hobby, and I am not interested in teaching that. So your entrepreneur identity, risk tolerance, failure, and evaluation are gold, and prioritizing cash in the door. Those three things are the biggest aspects of the entrepreneur identity that you want to grow.

The second identity that you want to grow is your leadership identity. This is the identity of I go first, I go often, and I go with purpose. The journey of entrepreneurship and learning to sell life coaching is meant to be an experience that creates mastery in your coaching tools. This is the time where you practice what you preach. This is where you find out in entrepreneurship what you really believe about coaching.

You have to take on more risk, more action, have more guts than your clients will ever have by a mile. Like that’s the way you want to think. I go first. I go often. I go first to fail. I go often at fails. I go with purpose to lead my people through failure. You have to lead. You can’t be a theory advice hotline. My friend and I used to joke we would coach each other after coach training, and then we would be like, “Okay, that’ll be $999 from the coach hotline.”

You can’t be coaching from theory. You can’t be coaching from what your certification school taught you. You can’t be coaching from what you a concept you learned in a book. You have to be coaching from I have lived this. That is how people will know you’re the real deal. That will be the differentiator. Not your certification, not how your website looks, not how many clients you’ve worked with, or what your client testimonials are, or if this person can talk to another one of your clients. It’s none of that.

They’re going to hear what you say and know whether you’ve lived your experience or not. There is an energetic difference that is palpable to other people of those who are walking the talk and those who aren’t. And I promise you, because I have coached, I mean, I have done launch audits, I have done email audits, sales page audits. I have coached people extensively on their consults, on overcoming objections, things they said, things the client said. I have gone into the nitty-gritty with my clients, and you cannot and will not ever be able to say enough of the right things or make enough of the right perfect IG or TikTok reels to ever compensate from not coming from a place of leadership where you go first with everything you teach, where you go first to fail often towards your dreams.

You go many times towards your dream. You go many times towards failure, and you go with the purpose of learning from it so you can walk someone else through it. This really matters. I can’t say it enough. The energetic piece of this cannot be faked. There’s no marketing funnel you can create that’s going to change this. You won’t be able to move people to a yes to pay you if you are not living in this leadership identity.

So don’t let entrepreneurship and risk eat you alive. You’ve got to be tough so that you can fail so that you have material for your people. I’m going to talk to you like my second mama. I have a second mama.

She is a lifelong New Yorker, and I met her doing a show, a theater show in Spain, when I was in college. I played the ingénue, and she played the mother of the ingénue. And we hit it off instantly, and we have been friends ever since, and I’ve been visiting her every time I go to New York, her whole rest of my life since 2006. And so almost 20 years.

And I went to New York once when I, before I became an entrepreneur, and I was an actor, and I went to a studio called HB Studio in the West Village, and we took acting classes together, and I lived in the city for months during the summer to take these classes. And one time, I was supposed to meet her at her apartment in midtown, right by Columbus Circle. She had an apartment that was three buildings down from the Columbus Circle, like that it used to be the Time Warner building. I don’t remember what it’s called now.

But anyways, I’m going to meet her, and I’m staying in Jersey City, New Jersey, and I’m going to meet her at her apartment in Midtown, and I get lost. And actually, I might have just been out running around visiting the city, but I get lost, and I end up somewhere in Tribeca. And my phone dies, and I don’t know the subway systems, and I’m walking around the streets of New York trying to get someone to help me get to Midtown. And people are giving me directions, and they’re talking so fast like New Yorkers, and I’m from the Midwest, and I’m so overwhelmed, and I can’t figure out like no matter how many people I ask how to find the subway to get to Midtown.

And so I’m an hour and a half late to our rehearsal for our that we were going to practice one of our scenes for. And I’m crying. I mean, it felt traumatic to be lost in the city without a cell phone and without knowing where to go. And I thought at one point, I might just have to live on the streets of Tribeca. Like, I don’t know what to do. And I show up at her door finally, I get there, and I’m crying my eyes out, and she opens the door, and I tell her, “I’m so sorry, I was lost, and it was terrible, and it was awful.”

And she looks at me like only a New Yorker could look at you, and she says, “You’ve got to dry your tears and tough up, or this city is going to eat you alive.” There was no pity. There was no like, “Let me give you a big mama hug.” Dry your tears, tough up, or this city is going to eat you alive.

And I have thought about that forever. Now, maybe it was a dose of tough love, but I really want to say it to you from maybe my Midwest mentality, which is in this industry, you have to tough it up. You have to be emotionally resilient. You have to be able to take the fails. You have to be able to hear no. You have to be able to feel rejection. You have to be able to put yourself out there and feel uncomfortable. You have to be able to feel embarrassed. You have to be able to feel humiliated. You have to feel like I just made a post and I want to delete it, or I just went live, and I want to retract it.

There’s a level of vulnerability that you are going to have to feel. You have to go first because there are people looking to change their lives in the world, and they are terrified of taking action and not getting what they want.

I really believe the number one reason people don’t reach out for consults or they don’t say yes to coaching, especially on consults, they don’t just reach out for consults because they are terrified that you might tell them that they are broken and unfixable. They are terrified if they finally go for it and take it really seriously, they’ll find out they don’t have what it takes, and they’re not capable.

They’re the most terrified of that. They’re not actually terrified of spending $1,000 with you, $5,000 with you, $10,000 with you. They are terrified it may not work. They are terrified of the learning curve, of the failure, and you have to go first. You have to know, you have to be living in that and know that you’re surviving and that you’re okay and in fact that you’re thriving. You have to become alive to the challenge, to the hard work, to the obstacles, to the friction, to the setbacks. You have to be so strong in them that when they give that to you, you’re not scared for them. You can’t be scared for them. Right?

My friend, I call her Madre. My Madre was not scared for me. She’s like, “Toughen up, girlfriend. What are you doing? You’re in New York. This little like softness is not going to, you’re not going to survive. Toughen up.”

This is what we have to do. Right? I call this type of leadership being a product of your product. And I really believe that this is why entrepreneurship and coaching are so important. I believe that getting coaching when you’re an entrepreneur is so important because it keeps your head on straight, and it helps you see every struggle as an opportunity for leadership.

So just check yourself now. Is that the way that you’re currently thinking every, every challenge is an opportunity for leadership for me? So that I can have come from a place of compassion and truly have been there and been there 1,000 times, so that when my client comes to me with this type of fear and is thinking about coaching, I can hold space for that. I know exactly what they’re thinking. I know exactly how they’re feeling. I am so strong to it that I’m not afraid for them that they may not get results. I’m not afraid for them that it might be hard. I’m not afraid for them that they might have to sacrifice something that they you know, they’re thinking they don’t want to give up

 I’m thinking of how big of a life they’re giving up if they don’t do it. I’m thinking about how big of an emotional freedom they’re giving up if they don’t do it. I’m thinking about the resilience they’re giving up if they don’t do it. I’m not thinking about the thing they have to sacrifice temporarily in the moment. So it’s so much easier for me to talk to people because of how often I go first.

So you want to strengthen yourself with I go first, I go often, I go with purpose to help myself and then others, and to be in alignment and integrity with what I teach. And I promise you, integrity and alignment will sell coaching for you. You will have people reaching out to you when this is how you’re approaching entrepreneurship, when this is how you’re approaching your dreams, when this is how you’re approaching your life.

And this is the tangible thing I want to tell you. If you are not living in your leadership identity, if you aren’t living how you would coach people through failure and hard things and obstacles and friction, you will not be able to say the right things on consults to create tangible breakthroughs that then create value that make someone want to pay you. You will not be able to overcome objections. You will hear them, you will be stuck, you won’t know what to say. You will struggle every single time.

And I teach people step-by-step how to do the perfect consult, how to overcome objections, how to transition to things, exactly what to say, but if you, with a real person, if you are not living the truth of what you teach, you will not know what to say to them. You will not say the right thing in the right energy, the right way that lands for them. 

But alternatively, if you are embodying the leadership identity, embodying the entrepreneur identity, and really going for it, you are building your risk tolerance. You are growing your emotional regulation skills. You are going out there and doing the thing. You are in the work. You don’t have to do anything perfectly, and you will have you will be selling life coaching.

People will be reaching out to you. You know exactly what to say to them on a consult when you’re selling and they will close. They will feel your authenticity. They will feel your alignment. And this is one of the most intangible things that sometimes people think, “Oh, that’s not really true,” but it is. It 100% is. So integrity and alignment with your leadership identity will sell coaching for you.

And the last identity that you want to develop is your coach identity. And it’s as simple as believing I am a life coach. And how you know you believe I am a life coach is you take yourself and your business as seriously as you would at $100,000.

Like if you were at had $100,000 business, how seriously would you take yourself as a coach and your business? You cannot wait to think of yourself as your main identity as a life coach until someone pays you. Like, “Oh, once someone pays me, then I’ll feel like a life coach. Then I’ll be able to tell people I’m a life coach.” You have to see yourself as a life coach in your main identity, and then you will make money.

And I always tell my clients this. It’s the first barrier for entry. If you’re not taking yourself seriously, no one else will either. So you can’t be a new coach or a coach in training, or notice when you do this. I’m a lawyer, and I just started a coaching practice. No, you’re a life coach who has their own coaching practice, and you’re a lawyer, and you’re a doctor, and you’re a teacher, and you’re a mom.

This identity has to be in the forefront. It can’t be a part-time. You can’t think of it as part-time. You can’t think of it as a hobby. You can’t think of it as a dream. You can’t think of it as something that one day you’re going to try to have. You can’t think of I’m trying to build a business. You just are. The coach identity has to be your predominant identity. I’m a coach. I’m a leader. I’m an entrepreneur.

And then what will happen is you will treat your business like a business, and you will do what it takes to bring in cash. And when you are doing that, people again, they feel that from you because no one, this is again, I’m going to say the hard thing that maybe no one would say on a free course or our first time meeting each other, but I’m going to say it.

No one’s hiring a hobby coach. No one’s hiring a part-time coach. You could be part-time, but if your mindset is I’m a part-time coach, they’re not hiring you. They want an expert. They want someone that guarantees them results. I also think the only reason people hire you is for results. So you have to believe I can get you results. I’m that good of a coach. I believe in the coaching tools that much. I believe in myself as a coach that much. I believe in your resourcefulness and your ability to tolerate emotional risk, and I believe in you because I believe in me so much, and I’ve watched myself do it, and I know how hard it was for me. And so if it was hard for me and I was still able to do it, you’re going to be able to do it too.

That’s what it does. When you do really hard shit that’s like unbelievable to you, you’re like, “Oh, well, if I can do it, because we always believe the least in ourselves. If I can do it, you can for sure do it.” But this is what you have, this is what you have to be carrying with you. I am a coach. I am a leader. I am an entrepreneur. Yes, Lisa.

Then you have to take, you have to embody being a life coach and take yourself everywhere you go. You can’t turn it on and off. If you go to Target today, or you go to the grocery, or you’re in an Uber, you’re not trying to sell these people life coaching, but you take yourself everywhere.

I had a client once who sells, she helps students get into the Ivy Leagues. What? She was a Stanford student at the time, so she was in Stanford building a, and she built a $300,000 business while in being a student at an Ivy League, teaching other people how to get into the Ivy Leagues. And one of the things she said for that very specific niche, she said one of the things that made me the most money in my business early on is I just took myself everywhere I went as a coach.

And I did the same thing: parties, family get-togethers, conversations with relatives. It did not matter. I took myself everywhere. And when you are taking yourself everywhere as a life coach, the world starts to notice. It’s something energetically that happens that can’t be explained. It’s completely intangible and it’s 100% the truth. So you have to take yourself everywhere. You can’t pick your moments because you won’t learn enough about yourself as a coach if you’re picking your moments, and you’ll miss the moment that actually came that was the opportunity.

And the last piece of the coach identity is you have to love your life now. I’m going to say something else that’s going to feel really hard. Are you ready? No one is hiring a life coach who hates their life, or is bummed about their life, or is regretful about their life, or their life isn’t enough. No one’s hiring that.

So if that’s how you’re feeling, you got to fix it right away. You got to step into a different perspective of your life and your journey. The people that are hiring coaches right now are hiring examples of what’s possible. That is the truth. They are hiring people who they see are alive in their lives. They are activated. They are engaged. They are connected. They are triumphing. They are overcoming.

This is a big piece of what I teach. A big piece of stepping into the journey and being all in because when I started my journey, when I became a life coach and I started going out to get clients, I had two spoons, no money, no furniture, a tiny apartment, nothing to my name but a new car and only because my 20-year-old car had almost killed me on the interstate and so I finally invested in a new car and it was the only thing I had. I didn’t have anything that said I’m so successful, I’m going to teach you about life. I didn’t have any of the tangible things.

So I always tell people, you don’t have to be positive all the time to sell life coaching, but you need to be powerful. So I made $150,000 with that set of circumstances. I had a broken heart. I’d been humiliated, and my life was sort of falling apart around me, but I chose in that moment when it would have been perfectly good to say Woe is me. Everything is terrible. Everything’s falling apart. I chose to love my life. I chose to love and accept the journey that I was on.

Even when some of my friends and peers who had started coaching businesses were doing it faster, and it was easier for them, I chose to be with myself on my journey and own it all. And to truly engage with the hard parts for me. To find gratitude every day despite all of it. Despite not, having a negative bank account, I could live my day in gratitude and still go out and give value to other people. I didn’t need my life to change to feel happy.

And I was also actively fighting every single day for the life and the future I knew was possible. And that translated everywhere I showed up for myself, on and offline. It had people inspired, influenced, and compelled to follow me, to engage with me, to show up to my things, to reach out and ask for more.

It really made an impact on people. And I rallied a group of clients very quickly who who who were watching me, and they were like, “I want that. I want to feel how she feels. I want to approach her life the way she’s approaching her life. I want to turn things around the way she’s turning things around. I want to go on that journey because it looks like she’s pretty alive. She’s pretty engaged. She’s pretty connected to herself and her life.”

That’s what people are hiring. If they wanted just like someone to sit and write in a little notebook and give them some tools and concepts, they’d go hire a therapist. People are hiring coaching because it’s a different approach and you have to be living that approach, and that includes loving the journey of growing your business.

Where most people just, they resist the journey of building their business. They resist the failure, they resist the hard part, they resist the not being where they want to be yet, they resist all the time before they sign their first client, then they resist until they sign their second client, then they resist until, you know, they get a yes, but they resist until someone pays. There’s just like constant resistance, resistance, resistance. I don’t want to be in this experience

Instead of, I want this experience. This is the first, last, and only time you might ever get to start a coaching business and be in the grind of making your dreams come true. Like, that’s the way I think about it. I look back to the beginning of my business when I was working so hard and signing my first clients.

I remember like, I look at that fondly, the same way of eating cold pizza in college and having no money and, you know, living off of chicken burritos for weeks on end, like, or ramen noodles. I look at it that way. I look at it as like, that was one of the greatest times of my life, and I’ll never get it back. Don’t let it pass you by. The way you feel about being in the process of creating anything is what either attracts or repels people to you.

So we want to step into the leadership, into the power, into the coach, into the entrepreneur, and be with it all. And no matter what, I’m going to teach you for the rest of these trainings, this is going to matter the most. This is the who before the how. It influences all of the how. It doesn’t matter how much of the how you do and how perfectly you do it, if the who is not there, it will not happen.

So before you go out and think about what do I tangibly need to do to sell life coaching, you need to know who do I need to be to sell life coaching? And I want you all to answer that today. I want you to answer, who do I need to be to sell life coaching? Who do I need to be when I think of someone buying life coaching from me, considering buying coaching from me? Who do I need to be for them? What would inspire them?

Like, I think about this when I’m in the deepest depths of challenges for myself, or I have so much friction in my day, or I have so many challenges that come my way, I think who do I need to be for them? How would they want to see me approaching this thing? What is the story they want to hear from me about this experience? Think about that today.

And then tomorrow we’re going to talk about actually going out and building your audience and building it quickly. But this part is going to influence so much of it. I want you to really think about, who am I?

Imagine what would be different about what you’re doing now if you were completely embracing the entrepreneur identity, if you were completely allowing the risk financially and emotionally, if you were failing and going into the failure and evaluating, if you were considering cash in the door as the most important priority of your business, if you were leading first and often with purpose, being a product of your product, embodying being a coach, loving the life you currently have, working with vigor towards the life you want, being all in on an entrepreneur journey, imagine how infectious your energy will be and how many people will want to listen to what you have to say. 

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2K for 2K program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2Kfor2K. We’ll see you inside.

Okay.

So, let’s talk about today’s lesson. It’s very timely, the second lesson. It was actually further down on my list, and I’m bumping it up because I know it’s going to be so useful to my Revenue Challenge students, and I’m really focused on supporting them through their challenge right now. And in the challenge, I teach something I call the Value Plan. It’s also what I use to guide me in my launches.

And I get asked one very specific question in regards to value and the value plan every time I run this challenge. And towards the end of this episode, I’m going to tell you what that question is and give you the answer. But you have to keep listening for it. It’s a little hook for you today.

So, the lesson I want to share with you today as my second lesson from 10 years in business is value is what creates money and clients. This is very important. Like when you think I need to make money, I need to get consults, I need to sign a client, any thought of I need this, the answer is, I need to create value. In 10 years of business, I have used this statement to guide everything, every single action I take, every coaching session, every move I make is about value because I believe this is true.

In fact, I would say for me, knowing the inside of my business and how I think and how I operate and what I spend my time doing, this statement is my entire strategy for success. Create value, receive clients, and therefore money. This is why I feel so passionately about teaching the idea of 100% results, like striving for 100% results. I’ve already done a podcast about that so you can search that if you would like, if you haven’t heard it. My philosophy behind it, how I use it to coach myself, what it really means, you can dive further into that. But I do think that the number one way that we can create value as coaches is simply by helping people create results. It’s the only reason people hire us. If they could do it on their own without paying, they would. And then if we’re promising to help them, we got to help them.

And although we can’t control the people who hire us, there are a lot of things that we can do to help someone get results, and I focus only on that with all of my power. It’s like I don’t give any energy to the things I can’t control, and I give 100% of me to the things I can. I love creating value for people. I’ve been thinking about this when I was thinking of this episode. I love creating free value and paid value. I love creating courses. I love creating workbooks. I love coaching. I love creating these podcasts. I seriously love taking something from my brain and getting it out into the world. I think it is the single most satisfying thing that we can do as humans when it comes to work.

So this statement, value creates money, changed my business forever. I learned this from my coach, Brooke Castillo, years and years ago. She said, she also said this, she said value creates money, but she also said the amount of money that you have made is the direct result of the value that you have created. The amount of money you’ve made is the direct result of the value that you’ve created. And sometimes that stings to hear that statement. Sometimes that feels unfair. Sometimes that feels impossibly not true, but it is. And the faster we stop taking that personally, the faster we stop thinking it’s not fair, the faster we start stop feeling entitled around that, the more value and the more money we will make.

So if you want to make $2,000 or $200,000, you have to create $2,000 or $200,000 of value. And I will take it one step further and say that you also have to find someone to give that value to. That is part of the equation, right? Imagine if you make art and you paint this beautiful picture, and it can be worth $2,000, you make $2,000 when you find someone who agrees with you and wants the painting and is willing to pay $2,000. But you can’t get paid if you leave the painting hanging on your wall and never show a soul. Right? You have to actually go out and show people this valuable thing that you made, and you have to do that way more than you think as well.

So you have to create or give the value, and you have to create and give the value, and then you have to find the people to pay you for that value. So there’s only two problems you ever have in your business. The first one’s, I’m not creating and giving value that equals how much I want to make. And how I know that to be true is I haven’t made how much I want to make. And then the second one is I’m not finding enough people to offer it to who agree. And I think we usually have both of those problems. I don’t think it’s either or. I think it’s usually both.

And so I’m just always working on both of those solutions for my business even at the level that I’m at now, right? Even at millions of dollars sold, multimillion dollar business, I’m always working that. Another thing that Brooke said to me years ago, or maybe she just taught this and it felt like she said it directly to me, is that if you want to make, you know, X dollars, you have to give X amount of value for free ahead of time. So it’s not just that you have to create an offer that’s worth $5,000 and then you deliver $5,000 worth of value. You’ve got to also give $5,000 worth of value ahead of time so that it makes sense for someone of why they would pay that. Right?

So you can’t just think my coaching package is worth 5K. You want to also think, how can I give 5K of value ahead of time? How can I demonstrate that my offer is worth 5K of value? Right, that’s my job. That’s what marketing is, demonstrating that I know what I’m talking about, demonstrating that I am worth the value that I charge. Not just saying it, demonstrating it.

So if you’re in 2K, if you’re one of my 2K for 2K students, I believe we do this in a few ways, a few simple ways. I reinforce this a lot in that program. We do it by being the coach, being all capitalized, like being the coach whose coaching is worth 5K every day and every way. Like taking ourselves with us everywhere we go as the coach who’s being paid $5,000. Like what difference would that be if you showed up to the world as if being paid 5K every day is your norm. That’s just who you are. Like being that version of yourself. Every day to every person, every encounter that you have. Not like picking and choosing, oh, I think this could be a sales opportunity, so I’ll turn it on, and then I’ll turn it off when I’m at home or I’ll turn it off when I’m with my friends or it’s not something that you’re turning on and off. It’s just who you are. That’s the first thing. It’s simple, not easy.

But the second one is by having conversations that create that amount of value. And I think we do that by being able to explain someone’s problem better than they understand it themselves and then by showing them a simple, clear, doable solution and helping them see the impact and the value of that even when there are obstacles and even when it’s hard. And that’s my 2K for 2K process in a nutshell. Like in a very simple explanation, I walk you step-by-step how to do that through that because it’s so important. If you can explain someone’s problem better than they understand it themselves, you have already given them 5K of value. Like knowing what the problem is and knowing what the solution is worth $5,000. Then believing that solution is clear and simple and doable and the person believing they could actually do it worth another $5,000. Then it becomes suddenly very easy to think paying someone $5,000 is a good idea. And we do that on consults. Like that to me is the easiest place to start doing that.

We give value ahead of time and demonstrate our value in the conversations we have, in the connection we make, in the marketing that we do, and then we really demonstrate it on the consults. I think consults are the most valuable thing ever. Like we can create $5,000 worth of value in a 1-hour consultation. And if you don’t believe that, then you’ve got to take 2K for 2K. Let me show you how a consultation could be that valuable. 

But we can also create $5,000 worth of value on a webinar, on a live stream, on social media posts, or again, the most simply by showing up and being a coach to everyone you interact with. Not coaching without permission, just being a coach where if someone didn’t know what you did for a living and they engaged with you for an hour, and then you left and they turned to someone and says, “Who was that person?” They’re like, “Oh, they’re a life coach.” And they’re like, “Oh my God, that makes sense.” That’s what I’m talking about, that you wouldn’t even tell someone you’re a life coach, but they would immediately know that it was true and it makes sense by how they engaged with you. I think your being can be transformational to people. I’ve signed so many clients just by my presence impacting people and them thinking I want what she has. Them following me on social media just being myself in the world, living my life, thinking I want what she has. I want to figure out how what she knows that I don’t know. So many clients that way.

So I told you I was going to the question I get every single challenge and I was going to tell you what that challenge was and what the answer is. And so the question that I get every challenge when we’re talking about, let’s say $25,000 in 30 days. And I tell someone you have to create $25,000 of value before you get paid $25,000 in cash. And I take it a step further and I say, the way I think about it is if I’m doing a launch where I’m doing marketing leading to a webinar and then a webinar to a sales pitch, then to sales emails to offer my whatever I’m offering. If that were my setup, the way I think about it is I want each thing I do to be worth $25,000. 

So if someone’s following along to my marketing, I want them to receive $25,000 worth of value just from my marketing. Then I want them to receive $25,000 worth of value on my webinar. Like that’s just the way I think about it. Not from a place of I have to create so much value that I’m in lack and I’m desperately trying to create value, but from a place of I love to think about that with my brain. It’s like if I want someone to pay me $25,000, then how do I demonstrate that I’m worth 25K on this webinar. I used to think about this with my 200K mastermind when it was $25,000 and I did a three-day live event ahead of a six-month mastermind. I wanted people to forget that there was ever a six-month mastermind. I wanted people to get $25,000 worth of value from the three-day live event.

So then I started thinking, if I only had three days to teach them how to make 200K and to give them $25,000 worth of value, what would I do? What would I say? How would I time things out? How would we orchestrate this three-day event? It made the events so valuable, so valuable that people would say to me without me seeding that, be like, oh, you’re going to get 25K worth of value. Like they would come and be like, I forgot there was a six-month mastermind. I can’t believe there’s still six months to go. I can’t believe this isn’t just that. Like this is worth 25K alone. People started mirroring that back to me because I decided to think about it that way, not from a place of lack but from a place of fun and desire and abundance.

So the question that I get again is how do I know what is 25K worth of value in, you know, on a webinar or in 30 days? Like how do I know what I could do to equal that value? And the answer is you don’t. I know that’s not the one that you want. But it’s the real true answer. It’s your best guess. We create a value plan with our best theory of what is 25K of value in 30 days or on a webinar or on a live stream. And with our desire, like I’m so excited to give this huge amount of value. I think of it seriously like Christmas. I feel the same way about dropping a free training or an entrepreneur series course or even this podcast, the same as I feel buying and wrapping a gift for my son. Do you feel that way about your marketing and about the value you give ahead of time? Like start there. Does it feel that way? Like Christmas, buying and wrapping gifts for your kid.

Now, coincidentally, I didn’t start this episode out and mean to be an ode to my mentor, Brooke Castillo, but I have learned so many amazing things from her. And one of the other amazing things I learned from her is that gift giving is for you and you receive the value of gift giving before you give the gift, so it doesn’t matter how someone receives it. That also changed my life because gift giving is my love language. All of my friends will tell you, everyone that knows me, that gets gifts from me knows I am obsessed with giving the perfect gift. And I will spend hours thinking about, I mean so much time shopping for the perfect things, thinking about the perfect things. It’s just how I express my love. It’s a good thing I’m rich. I was meant to be rich because I love to give gifts as my love language. It makes me feel so good to do it, and it doesn’t even matter how they receive it. It just feels so good.

And this is how I think about value. I am picking out the perfect gift for you. And listen, yes, every once in a while, you’re not going to nail the perfect gift. I don’t always nail the perfect gift, or someone doesn’t always react the way I anticipated. Sometimes it’s because they’re not good at receiving the gift, but I don’t make it about me and I learn about the person and their preferences for gifts in that moment. And I’m going to talk about that in just a second, but I actually just thought about the funniest story. Can I just take a detour real quick and tell you a quick, very funny story about gift giving?

Last year, so my mom is notorious for putting the worst, worst things on her Christmas list. By the way, I would tell her that I was telling this story. She would not be offended. But she puts the worst things on her Amazon list. the worst. And then we all talk about it. We’re like, what? We’ll take a picture and send it to my siblings and be like, this is on Mom’s Christmas list. What is happening?

So last year, I decided to gag her and order her the worst of the worst on her list and then wrap them up in like my fancy, beautiful wrapping paper. So she had, one of the so the three things I got her, she had 1,000 post-it notes on her Amazon list. Why? Why do you have 1,000 post-it notes on your list? A paper shredder and light bulbs, rechargeable light bulbs. This is what I mean by the worst things on her list. So I wrapped them up in fancy paper, and the whole family was in on it. Like we cackled every time we talked about it in anticipation of how awkward it was going to be when she opened them and then I was trying to prove a point when she would open them and it would be really awkward like, why did you get me these random a paper shredder and light bulbs and post-it notes? These are not good gifts. And I was going to be like, see, don’t put them on your Amazon list. I really thought she was going to be like, “Oh, thanks.” And then we were going to laugh. I had actually gotten her other real gifts and I’d hidden them away. But the joke was on all of us because she freaking loved it and appreciated it. She said it was the perfect gift and was so confused why we were all laughing, and then she called us assholes.

But we had to educate her on proper gift requesting etiquette. She was saying how she doesn’t put any she puts stuff on there that she doesn’t want to spend money on herself. And we were all like, “Yes, and no one else wants to spend money on that either. That’s why you don’t put it on your list.” It’s like putting like garbage bags on your list. Like no one wants to buy that either. Like don’t put that on your Christmas list. So, last year, I learned about my mom’s gift preferences. I learned that she really does like it made her day. She and then she I was texting her about it the other day, and she said, “Jokes on you. If you ever lose electricity, you’re going to know the value of having rechargeable bulbs.”

So, I think of this as when I’m giving value, I am doing my best to think of what could be the perfect gift for them. And then I’m giving it to them. And then I get to learn whether it actually was or not. Maybe the thing I would have bought her that I thought was perfect wouldn’t have been perfect. She loved her gifts. So it’s either what I like to say, winning or learning, winning or wisdom. And that’s what we’re doing with the value we give to people in the world. We’re wrapping the most beautiful Christmas gift that we can possibly think about, and we’re giving it to them, and then we’re seeing if that was their preference or not. And then if not, we’re like, okay, next time I know that they like this or they don’t like this. They don’t like it when I spend this much money on a gift or they like it when it’s more practical. They like a luxury that they wouldn’t spend for themselves. They like this, they like that. We’re giving from desire, finding out how the person receives it, and then learning how to be a better gift giver.

I love thinking of it that way. I love thinking also of value as being for me. Like even if no one buys, I become more valuable when I give the value. The more practice I have at giving value, the better my value gets, the more valuable it becomes. So I want to practice giving value as often as possible. I want to stretch my value. I won’t know ahead of time what value is needed to create whatever amount of money that I want to create, whatever amount of money you want to create, we won’t know ahead of time. If we did, we would have already created it. We would have created the value and we would have created the money. 

So I have to have this mindset of posing a theory and going out and testing it. Like I think this is an awesome marketing idea. I think this will be a really valuable training. I think people will really love this. And then we see, did they sign up for it? Did they attend? Did they purchase afterwards? Whatever it is, right? Whether it’s a consult or a webinar, and knowing that we will know that we have in fact created $25,000 of value only when we are paid $25,000. And we can’t have any entitlement or frustration or anger or resentment around that.

If you gave it your all and you put more energy and effort than you’ve ever put into it and you didn’t make 25K, guess what? You got to go again. We’re not entitled to I gave you all of me and so you should give me 25K. It’s just not the way it works. That might have been your first iteration of what you thought was all of you. So next month, let’s try to be even more. I can promise you all if you’re like, I gave everything I had, then you just aren’t scratching like you’re just not like there’s so much more in you. You haven’t scratched the surface. You’re giving yourself a self-imposed limit of what you have that’s possible. And it really is like that’s it. It’s that simple. 

And what keeps us from doing this from like I like to think of it as like giving value with reckless abandon. What keeps us from doing that is being transactional and entitled with the value. I spent time on this. This should have gotten this result. This got the result in the past and it’s not getting the result now. It shouldn’t be this hard. I shouldn’t have to give this much. I gave all of me, and I didn’t get the result. All of that, I like to think of as anti value thoughts. It’s creating a new concept here, anti value. That’s what that is, non-valuable thoughts, low value thoughts. If you’re in my 200K mastermind, we talk about low value cycles and low value thoughts. Those are all low value thoughts. And I’m not judging you for having them. You have a human brain. I have those thoughts too. I get entitled too. I just check it a lot more often than I see other people checking it.

And the more low value thoughts, anti value thoughts that you have, the less value you create. And then the more that’s going to show up and how you get paid. So it’s like if you’re wanting to make 25K in 30 days, you give yourself all of you or you give the value all that you’ve got. You give your people all that you’ve got, everything inside of you, all the energy you possibly can. You don’t make any money, worst case scenario, you make no money. The chances of you making that 25K, if you then adopt, I spent time on this, this should have gotten the result, it shouldn’t be this hard. I shouldn’t have to give this much. Any thoughts like that, you’re just going to go create zero again. I know this because I used to do 10 pitches a day selling slicers and mops and dicers and all the things. And the more entitled I felt to I did the perfect show, they should have bought, the more zeros I got. 

And yeah, there were days where I went into stores and every show I did was a zero, and I walked out of that store not being paid a dime for 8 hours, 10 hours of work. I actually think that’s what’s made me an amazing entrepreneur is that for seven years I did that and so I never like there was no entitlement. I didn’t get paid like even a two-dollar-an-hour wage. I got nothing. I was a contractor. You sold or you made nothing. And so I understood that I couldn’t stay in that cycle forever because I was just not getting paid. And other people would just quit. But for me, I was like, okay, let’s figure this out. 

I ended up becoming the person that knew how to sell in every store across the country, in every community, in every type of environment, with every type of crowd, with every type of offer because I just refused to keep having zero shows. I refused to stay in the feeling of entitlement and taking it personally. And just decided, okay, I got to learn about these people. They didn’t love that perfect pitch. If they did, they would have bought. That perfect pitch wasn’t the value that they needed. I didn’t give each of those people $40 worth of value because they did not buy the product. 

So I have to figure out how they need me to do the show to make it valuable for them. I need to figure out what demonstration I need to do, what examples I need to talk about, the speed to which I need to speak to them, the formality to which I need to do the show, how engaging I need to be, like all of the things. I have to figure out what they need to feel comfortable, excited, and desired to buy the product. That is a high value thought or what I call a high value cycle. Not taking it personally and just like I got to figure it out.  Like my job is to desire giving value like it’s Christmas, to feel positive anticipation of people receiving that value, going out in the world to offer that value, and then to keep evaluating and adjusting and improving until I make the money I want to make and to be a really good sport about it the entire time. 

Another thought my coach Brooke gave me years ago was the impact is none of your business. I remember where I was when I heard that. I was listening, I think she said it on a podcast or it could have been a coaching call, but I was in the parking lot of a juicery. I know the exact juicery I was at. I know the exact moment, like I remember it like when you hear something that changes your life so deeply that you’re like, I remember the like I’ll never forget the time and space. That’s what it was for me. The impact is none of your business. That thought helps me be a really good sport. It keeps me playing the infinite game of becoming more valuable day by day and believing that value will compound and pay out eventually and maybe in ways that I don’t expect.

So for example, I offered free coaching for six weeks to a client when I first started my business. And then I offered her paid coaching and she said like either she couldn’t afford it or her husband wouldn’t pay for it. It was something like that. She really wanted to do it and she was a stay at home mom and I don’t know what the whole scenario was, but basically husband wouldn’t pay for it. But she found it so valuable that she talked about it to her best friend all the time. And her best friend looked me up and asked me for a consult and was my first paid client. And I coached her and she paid me for years. 

That’s what I mean by like the impact can’t be your business. You can’t be transactional. I gave you six weeks of coaching for free, so you should be paying me. Maybe you were never supposed to pay me and actually, this other person that you know is it was supposed to always be my client and pay me. That’s how it felt. I was like, oh, this was never supposed to be orchestrated that way. It was all supposed to be orchestrated in a way that I could have never anticipated or imagined because I didn’t know the other person involved. I had no idea that they were even interested in life coaching and that they would be introduced to me.

And actually, fun fact, the person who said no to the coaching ended up saying yes years later, I think three years later, and paid me for quite a while as well, and then also ended up working in my company for quite a while. So that value paid out tons as well. Another time I created a free training to sell my 2K for 2K students. And I thought this was years ago. I thought it was going to hit. I was so excited about it. And then it had really low signups like to get people into the training. It converted really well. So the people who joined like such a huge number of them bought, but we struggled to get people to sign up for it. And after as I was evaluating, I had a couple colleagues look at the marketing and they were confused as to what I was offering. 

So it turns out the name, what I had called it, people were confused about what it is and the value that they would receive. The people who joined it, they had I had the chance to demonstrate the value, so they got tons of value because I don’t hold back. I didn’t hold back because it didn’t perform well and because there was only so many people that signed up. Like I make sure I give the same training that I would give if however many people I wanted to sign up signed up versus, well, now there’s only this many, so I’m not going to give the same training. No, I don’t do that stuff. I give the training I was always anticipating giving as if everybody that I had wanted signed up. And because of that, people did like it converted very, very well.

And now what’s really interesting is it’s become one of the most valuable assets in my 2K program and I send people to it all the time. I’m like, oh, have you done this training? You got to go do this. It’s become such an asset that now I even market like, oh, you have this problem, go to this bonus course here. It’s going to solve it for you. So it ended up being a better fit for paid clients than free clients, right? And I could have never anticipated that ahead of time. The value came later. I just created something for free that should have been for paid. But I let it be none of my business in real time. I didn’t get transactional. I stayed open to receiving the payout. That’s the way I like to think about it. I’m open to receiving the payout. And the only time I make the impact be my business is in my honest and fair evaluations that will create more value for myself.

So an honest and fair evaluation means not beating myself up, not victimizing myself, deciding to see what value I do have and I did give, honoring my effort, honoring my creativity, honoring my ideas, not discrediting them or myself because they didn’t produce what I thought that they would in the time frame that I thought they would. And then radically taking responsibility if I didn’t get paid without the drama. I thought I created a $25,000 value plan. I thought I gave $25,000 of value. I planned to. I didn’t because I didn’t make 25K. So my theory was wrong. What is there to learn here? Like how was my theory wrong? Where might I have fallen short? What was off? What could have been better? I ask myself 100 different thought-provoking questions to engage my brain in evaluation.

And I believe that an evaluation is also not a punishment for not creating the sales I wanted to create. It’s for me as well. If you’ve listened to my podcast about failure gold, it’s for me to extract value. It’s not punishment. It’s how I become even more valuable, how I receive even more value. Like for me, I remember I saw my first 12 consults all said no, and I was charging $5,000 at the time. So that’s $60,000 that was on the table that I did not get early on in my business. It would have been life-changing. And I decided I’m either getting paid $5,000 or I’m getting $5,000 worth of value. I’m either making 60K or I’m getting $60,000 worth of value. And what I learned from evaluating those consoles gave me every yes from then on out for an entire year straight and I made $150,000, more than double that value from what I learned in the failure of it.

So the gift of value is always actually for me first. I go first with giving value and feeling valuable, believing myself to be valuable. I go first. I give value often and freely with abundance and openness to demonstrate my value ahead of time. And I give it with the purpose to create transformation and then clients and then money. Transformation, then clients, then money. And when the money comes, that’s how I know I’ve done my job. All right. That was a good one. I’m all worked up. That’s today’s episode.

If you want that free course, How to Sell Life Coaching, it’s going to be available for a limited time. Make sure you grab it at staceyboehman.com/howtosell. And I will have another lesson for you next week, my friends. Have an amazing one. I will talk to you soon. Bye-bye.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2k for 2k program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2Kfor2K. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #362: Lessons from 10 Years in Business: There Is No Right Offer
transcript:
W
elcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2K, $20K, and $200k using her proven formula.

Hi coaches. Welcome to episode 362. It’s a lot of episodes. Hi. I am so excited to be here with you today. Happy Wednesday. All of my episodes typically come out on Wednesdays.

And this is the first episode of a very special series that I have been dying to get out into the world. This is what I anticipate being a 10-episode series; however, I’m not holding myself to that. If I decide I want to make a couple extras and I can’t narrow it down. But a 10-episode series on the top 10 lessons that I have learned in business over the last 10 years. This is my 10th year in business, and I’ve been sort of celebrating that all year.

And also been thinking a lot about what I’ve learned and the 10 years of wisdom that I have developed after selling $45 million of coaching. What? It’s crazy. So wild. And some of the wisdom that I have learned in business has been coming out through my Entrepreneur Series. And so this isn’t a compilation of this is the top 10 or only 10. It’s like, these are the 10 things I haven’t talked about yet, maybe. I haven’t done an Entrepreneur Series on them yet. I haven’t maybe had a podcast about them. I haven’t really gone in-depth with them.

And some of them are from my core offers. So today’s lesson is going to be a lesson straight out of the 200k Mastermind. And it feels really important that this is the very first one. I’m so excited to share it with you. It feels like the bedrock to which the $45 million of coaching that I have sold has been sold through. This one core belief.

And if you are in my 200k Mastermind, you know that we do this work. If you ever join me in 200k Mastermind, this is the work that we do. It’s not just the concept of it; we actually become the person who can do this work and has this thought, and creates results from this belief.

Okay, are you ready? My first top lesson after 10 years in business and $45 million of coaching sold, it’s a lot of coaching. I also think I should say this, this is important to know before we dive into this episode, that I have created at least that I can remember, five seven-figure offers. In those five seven-figure offers, and I’m about to create a sixth one. In those seven-figure offers, one of them has come very close to reaching eight figures. It will reach eight figures. One of them has done multiple eight figures, like $25 million in sales. That’s the 200k Mastermind. And one of them has done multiple seven figures.

So I just want to say that to say, this belief that I’m about to give you is a very powerful one that can make you a lot of money. It can make your offers be incredibly successful, incredibly successful.

That’s what’s on the table. Okay, are you ready? Here’s the belief. There is no right offer. Only the offer that you make right.

So this is my core belief. My core belief is everything sells. Everything can sell. There’s not a perfect offer out there. There’s no right, there’s no like, oh, this offer at this price point with this length of time to this amount of people selling this result is the right offer, and I will, you know, once I offer it, suddenly everybody will start buying.

There is only the offer that you make right by learning how to sell it and becoming who you need to be to sell it well. And the faster you learn this, you can sell anything. This is very important because if you can sell anything, what actually happens is that you will sell what you truly want.

So I want to tell you a quick story because I’ve taken some heat on this belief. Now, mostly how I used to say it, and I’ve just I have no interest in being polarizing, so I’ve stopped saying it. But this belief came to me in a mastermind, or this realization that I believe this and it’s a core belief of mine, came to me while I was in a mastermind with my colleagues at the seven-figure level.

And I had a colleague who was being coached on a group offer, and she’d been offering one-on-one coaching. And she had a really big story about why her people with what she coaches them on and who they are, that they would never buy group. They would only sell one-on-one.

And she was very stuck on this. I was not the one coaching her, but she was very stuck on this. And out of the blue, I go, “Okay, hold on, listen. Do you know what my clients buy for me?” And she goes, “No, what?” And I said, “Anything I fucking sell them.” And that moment, the whole room erupted, and they were like, “This is the most brilliant thing we’ve ever heard.”

Now, I’ve taken heat on that because people have made that say, I used to have this on mugs. We used to give mugs out in the 200k Mastermind that had that on there. “Do you know what my clients buy for me? Anything I fucking sell them.” And it used to be on the mugs and people loved it until they didn’t. And until they I got really, really successful. I crossed eight figures and then suddenly, people started saying that saying meant that I sell dumb things to dumb people.

And I have to tell you, I do not believe that. I do not believe that I sell to dumb people. In fact, my truest belief about my clients are they’re smarter than me. Many of them have high Ivy League educations. Many of them climbed the corporate ladder way farther than I could have ever done myself. Many of them are more worldly than me. I have to ask them all the time what their words mean when they’re getting coached. What’s that mean? I don’t know what that is.

So I believe they are very intelligent. I really do believe that about them. And because they’re coaches, I just believe they’re very in charge of their buying. They’re very intentional. They’re not making decisions against their will. We’re coaches, we know how to operate our brains more than the average human. So I have a lot of powerful beliefs about the power of the people I work with. So this never crossed my mind that anyone could ever believe that’s what I was saying.

For me, it was me being in my power, being fun and cheeky, which I sometimes am, and recognizing that the offer is not the thing that people are buying. They’re buying my vision and my passion. And it was also me recognizing that I am in charge of what gets sold as the salesperson. That’s my job, right? It’s not the buyer’s job to sell themselves on whatever offer I give them, it’s my job. Whatever the offer is, it’s my job to sell it.

I probably know that at my core because I used to sell infomercial products in stores. And the one thing is I could sell everything. I could sell the ShamWow, I could sell the knives, I could sell the slicers, I could sell the chopper, I could sell the Euro Clean Mop, I could sell the Mr. Sticky. And then even within those products, we had free things that we gave away at the audiences. And I could sell a $5 paring knife the same as a little couple inch square of a ShamWow. And what is someone even going to do with that?

I enjoyed it as a cloth to clean off my phone, which is how I sold it. I really love knowing that my phone is clean and it’s shiny. This is how I use it. I keep it in my purse. Whatever it was, if I loved the product, I could sell it. What I also know about myself is they used to ship me shit from China from a factory that was not the same factory that we always use. Like every once in a while, we would get a shipment that was like, it just wasn’t the same factory. And the product didn’t work as well, and I would refuse to sell it. I would say, hey, listen, I’m in the store. This product doesn’t work. I’m not selling it. Well, you’ve got to sell it. We’re in the store. Well, I’m not going to sell it. So if you want me to sell something by tomorrow, you should probably overnight me new product.

And I’m not joking with that. That’s before I found coaching. That’s before I became the sales queen. I’ve always had an aversion to selling anything I don’t love and I don’t want and I wouldn’t buy and I wouldn’t use. I feel very strongly about loving your product, and I feel very strongly that if you do, it doesn’t matter what the product is, you can sell anything, especially if you have the sales skill set, right? If you know how to sell, if you have that skill set, you could just plug it into any offer that you love, right?

So around the time where this was sort of like being used against me, as like Stacey thinks her clients are dumb and, you know, she just sells anything to anyone. And someone actually said, I’m not kidding, online, that I would bag up my dog’s dog shit and sell it to someone for $5,000 and convince myself that it’s valuable. I kind of laughed at this because I was like, clearly they don’t know Neil obviously picks up the dog poop. That is not something I do, ever. I don’t take out the trash either.

But I really thought about this. I don’t have a desire to be polarizing. I really don’t. I don’t like any sort of drama like that. It’s so embarrassing if someone would take something I said from love and power and being empowered and trying to empower someone else and use it. I don’t like that. So I remember having a call with my one-on-one coaches in my 200k Mastermind around the time where this concept and this idea started kind of taking heat online.

And I said, I want to have a conversation with this with you all about this because you’re coaching my people, and I want to make sure you understand where I’m coming from when I say this and what I meant by this and the empowerment I feel when I say it. You know what I sell, what I can sell? Anything to anyone because I’m amazing at selling.

And I was like, let’s have a conversation about this. Let’s talk about it. Like anything that you disagree with, tell me. Like anything that question you have, tell me. And one of my coaches who I love and adore, raised her hand and she said, “Stacey, you can sell anything, but you don’t.”

And that opened and like up something inside of me and created such an aliveness with this concept for me because she was right. I can sell anything. I’m that good at selling. I understand the art, and I do believe it’s an art. I understand the art and the skill set of selling anything. I am a good salesperson. I know how to communicate in a selling conversation. I know how to think about the buyer in a way that allows them to feel safe to say yes. I know how to sell. I can sell anything.

And I don’t. And that’s really powerful to know. She said, “Stacey, you’ve had the same offers for the last six at the time, for the last six years.” Now it’s been eight years that I’ve had the same offers. 2k, 200k, 2 Million Dollar Group. And I have a new series that I’ve been doing called the Entrepreneur Series that’s been like a really fun expression of mine and something that I feel really deeply called to do that doesn’t, you know, is not part of my mainstay offers, but something that brings me a lot of joy and really serves my people.

So here’s what I really believe. When you know that there’s no right offer, there’s no magical perfect offer. When you commit yourself to becoming the person that can sell any offer to anyone, what you will sell is what you desire to sell. What you will sell is what you believe is the best thing to sell. I genuinely believe that about people. Like, if I have a box of slicers that come from one factory and a box that comes from the other and one of them isn’t as good, why the F would I choose that one over the other one?

It’s like common sense to me, right? I’m going to choose the one that’s the better product because I get to feel good about when they when they leave the store with it. And if you’re in my 2k for 2k or my 200k Mastermind, you have access to my irresistible offer protocol. So in the 2k for 2k, if you’re a student, you can go into offer week, and I teach the irresistible offer protocol, the foundational ideas behind that. And if you’re in the 200k Mastermind, it is inside the five-step process. The very first step addresses that the simple offer addresses the irresistible offer protocol.

So if you’re in that, and I’m going to give you a vision of it now if you’re not in either of those programs, but what you know to be true is that I only desire to sell offers, like this is my philosophy. I only desire to sell offers that I know will get my clients results, that I know will be an over-deliver, that I am enthusiastically obsessed with and would want to buy myself, and at a price that feels easy for me to sell. Like, I have no drama about it.

I coach people this all the time. I’m like, I am the biggest proponent of choose the price that feels easy to sell, not the one that you have to convince yourself that you’re good enough to sell. It’s like such wasted drama. I’d rather just get in and coach people for a lesser price and get the experience and get the and create the momentum and the demand than try to convince myself into selling a $20,000 package that I don’t feel ready for.

So I want to sell offers that get my clients results, that overdeliver, that I’m obsessed with, that I would want to buy at prices that feel easy to sell. That’s what I want to do.

And because I have the skill set, I can do it. But when you believe there’s a right offer, meaning a correct price point at a time frame and a perfect result to offer to get people to buy, notice I said get, to get people to buy, so that you don’t get objections, then you compromise your desire and your integrity. And you try to manipulate the buyer into buying and to manipulate the results. And you don’t mean to do it. We don’t mean to do it. But when we’re thinking, what I know to be true is it’s going to take them a year to create these results, but I’m going to offer them six months because I don’t think that they’ll say yes to a year.

You’re not offering them the thing that you know is true. You’re compromising your integrity as a coach. For me, I didn’t think that I could get someone results in six weeks. I didn’t even think it was possible in six months, like life-changing, when I was a general life coach. If I was coaching people to change every aspect of their life in entirety, I believed in my coach integrity that would take a year at minimum. And that is what I sold people.

And I figured out who do I have to be to be a new coach and get on a consult and sell a $5,000 year-long coaching package because that is the right offer to make them. That’s the power. That’s the beauty of believing that there isn’t a right offer is you decide from your coach integrity, what do I want to offer? What’s the right offer for them and for me and for all of us? And then I learn to go sell that.

You can’t be more interested in a yes and not failing and not hearing no than what you think is right. If you are, you will not be as happy in your offers and you won’t make as much money. You will be imprisoned by your lack of sales skills. I want to sell this thing at 10K, but I don’t think anyone will buy it. Or I want to have this in-person version of this, I want this to be virtual and in-person, and I think it’s really important, but I don’t think that people will do in-person, so I’m just not going to offer that. That’s imprisonment by lack of sales skills.

So I want you to be able to sell anything, to believe that any offer could sell anything. You could literally any type of offer that you could ever make would be able to be sold, right? I want you to be able to sell anything so that you don’t. So that you sell the right thing for you and your clients, not the easy thing, not the popular thing, not the thing that you think you have to sell in order to get the sale, but the thing you want to deliver.

I was just telling my 200k Mastermind, I have a new offer coming out in January that will be a new mainstay offer, something I offer all the time alongside 2k, 200k, and 2 Million Dollar Group. And it’s an offer that could be composed a hundred thousand different ways. So many ways. I’ve narrowed it down to like five. But there are a lot of ways that I could offer this offer.

And I was telling my students, I’m getting very still inside of myself and very quiet. And I’m listening to my heart and I’m listening to my desires and I’m paying attention to the vision. And I’m thinking about the people who will join me in this offer, and I’m thinking about their journey. And I’m just paying attention and listening to what is it that I most want, regardless of what people say, this is the right way to offer this, and if you want to sell this, you’d better sell it this way. And you got to do this to keep people, and you got to do that to have this result, and for buyers to do this and buyers to behave this way and buyers to behave that way.

And I’m like, wait, wait, wait, hold on. I’m responsible for buyer’s behavior, right? They’re playing off of me and my certainty and my energy and my sales skills. That’s what I believe, right? It’s actually the opposite. It’s more manipulative to be like, I’m going to do this thing because if I do, then the buyer might pay me more money. The buyer might stay with me longer. The buyer might buy quicker. The buyer might do this or that. Like that is actually manipulative.

But to say this is the offer, this is what I’m excited to give you, and I’m going to go find the people who agree with me and want to join effortlessly. And then the people who need that, it’s like a little more effort for them, I’m going to take on that responsibility and figure out what I need to say to them to where they see the vision the way I do and it works. That’s my job.

But in order to get to this place, you have to try on this belief that there is no right offer. And you have to come up against your brain thinking there is all the time. There’s no right offer that suddenly gets people just saying yes. I’ve never seen that happen, and I have 6,000 coaches in my 2k for 2k program, and I’ve coached thousands of people in my 200k Mastermind, and I’ve coached many people at the 2 Million Dollar Group level. And I’ve never seen an offer, someone’s just like, Oh, I landed on the perfect offer. Everybody said yes. No objections. That doesn’t happen.

There is no right offer that magically has no objections. There’s no perfect price point that everyone can afford and will say yes to. There’s no right time frame where people won’t try and negotiate down less time for less money. Like, oh, I offered them six months and they said it was too long. It’s because the right offer was three months. No. If you offered them three months, they would have asked about six weeks because that’s not the reason they’re not buying, and it’s not the reason you’re not selling. And when you believe that, you start finding the reasons that they actually aren’t buying. You start actually doing better evaluations. Oh, it isn’t the price. If it isn’t how long it is, then why didn’t they buy?

And then the other thing you have to believe is what is true is that you actually can craft your perfect offer, and there actually is a market for it. That’s so fun. That’s where coaching gets like really fun. Is I love this offer. This is the offer I want to make at the price point I want to make it. I am not compromising my desires or my integrity in any way, shape, or form in order to sell this.

But in order to get to that place, you have to keep believing there is no right offer. There is only the offer that I make right. And then when people don’t buy, instead of blaming the offer and changing it to try to mold it into the right offer, you take responsibility for why. You pose your best theories of why they didn’t buy. You evaluate. You choose to only address the things in your power.

That’s why I believe, you know what my clients buy for me? Anything I sell them because I know I’m going to create the perfect offer for me and for them, and then I’m going to be in my power to take responsibility to sell it. And if they’re not buying, it’s not the offer, it’s me, every time. Every time I say it’s not the offer, it’s me and I don’t get down about it with myself, but I get curious about it and I start paying attention and I start deciding that I’m the thing I can change, how I’m selling it, who I’m being selling it, I’m more and more and more empowered. And I sell more and more and more.

Right? So, for example, if someone doesn’t have the money, if they tell me, Oh, I don’t have the money, more often what they actually mean is I don’t have the money to spend on this thing that I can’t see the value of or don’t believe I will create results with.

If I’m taking responsibility, then I can say, okay, I clearly did not explain the value right. I need to redo that. And I clearly didn’t show them simply and doably how they will create the result. I didn’t help them believe in themselves enough. Maybe I didn’t believe in them enough. Maybe I wasn’t believing in my offer enough. I get to be real about that and work on that. I get to be in charge of figuring that out.

And then you keep going until you figure out how to market your offer, how to find the people for it, and how to sell it, and how to address objections for it. You just keep going until you do. And the moment you do, you will realize, oh my God, Stacey was right. There is no right offer. There is just the offer I commit to selling and figuring it out.

And that is for me what 2k for 2k was. I remember thinking the name was a little silly and maybe people wouldn’t get it. I remember thinking it’s not a big enough result. I remember thinking, I don’t know if this is what coaches want. I don’t know if this is what they’re going to buy. Everybody else is selling 10 clients in a week or, you know, $100,000, six figures. Like everybody was selling really big results. I’m like, what am I doing? I’m going to sell little results?

But then I decided to be in charge of that. Yes, I am. Here’s why I love this. I think it’s more realistic. I think it sets people up for bigger success. I know it’s the hardest part. I know if they do that, they could do anything. I believe that this is where we should focus. I believe it will get them small, it will have them thinking in small, tangible steps instead of these like big, giant ones that they’re unable to do. I believe it will give them energy and motivation every day if they’re just thinking of making $2K, of selling one person.

And so that’s what I went and sold when no one else was selling anything like it. And oh, I have made over seven figures with that. I was thinking 6,000 people, or eight figures. I have made over eight figures with the offer. So I have two eight-figure offers. I’ve sold 6,000 people that offer. I’ve made $12 million from it. Cannot do math. So I’ve made $12 million off of an offer that I decided to release that was contrary to what every other business coach in the industry was offering coaches, because it was never about the offer. It’s the energy behind it. It’s my willingness to figure out how to sell it, to share that vision with people, to tell them why it’s so important, to make them believe it’s possible for them.
