So now that I know I can do that, I can do that with my next offer and my next offer and my next offer. That is a more aligned offer. Now, here’s the caveat to there is no right offer. An offer could not be right for you if you are not in alignment, integrity, congruence, whatever you want to call it. Alignment, integrity, and congruence with your offer or any offer components.

So, meaning if you are offering something that you haven’t mastered yourself. If you’re offering to help them lose 100 pounds, but you never have. If you’re offering to help them make $100K, but you never have. Now, that’s not the same as I’m going to coach, I’m a mindset coach for business owners. I don’t market results. I’m just going to help you manage your mind while you build your business. But if you’re saying, I’m going to help you make $100K and you’ve never made $100K, it’s not going to work. It’ll be very hard to work.

If you are not doing the work that you teach, if you are not using coaching to solve your problems, and you don’t actually believe your thoughts create your results, but you’re telling other people that they do, it’s never going to sell.

When you price your offer above what you’re actually willing to pay yourself and that you’ve actually invested, it’s not going to sell. If you’re selling renewals to people but you don’t ever renew yourself, you’re not going to sell it.

If you’re marketing to people above your experience level, they’re going to sniff it out every time. You can’t just decide I’m going to coach millionaires. I’m going to help them with their productivity. If you don’t have a million-dollar business, you don’t understand how to help a millionaire with their productivity. You know how to help someone with their productivity, with how much money you make. If you are great at productivity, but productivity at the million-dollar level is very different than productivity at the six-figure level, and you would only know with 100% mastery if you’ve done it, right?

But those things are not the offer; they’re the salesperson. So the reason the offer doesn’t sell is not because it isn’t sellable, right? It’s because the salesperson isn’t in alignment with the offer. So for every offer you want to make, you want to know I have to be in alignment with this. I have to be in congruence with this. This has to be a masterful offer.

And maybe my first work to sell this offer right, to make it right, is to find all the ways that I am masterful. In the beginning, coaches love to tell themselves they don’t know anything, and they’re baby coaches and they don’t have any experience, so how have they mastered anything? But they have. This is why they’ve decided to become a coach. There have got to be things you’ve mastered. You’ve got to be a few steps ahead of somebody. And you figure out who that is, and you sell to them.

But I will tell you, for every single offer you could dream up, someone else is already making it and having success. I guarantee it. But are you the person who is the right person to be offering it, and are you willing to invest the time to make that offer work, to figure out how to sell it? Are you willing to stick it out and figure it out so that you have this skill and this freedom from here on out, for the rest of your career? It is literally freedom to know that you could sell any offer to anyone, and so what do you want to sell to smart people, by the way?

And here’s the final thing I will tell you. When you compromise your integrity, when you compromise your desires, when you sell what you think is quote unquote right to get a sale, to get, when you’re in get energy and you create an offer from get energy in order for it to be right to get people to magically say yes, you will be deeply frustrated if people don’t buy. If it was not something you really wanted to sell, you are going to be miserable when they don’t buy. You will be so resentful of having to work hard for it. You will be incredulous. You will be confused as to why people are not buying, and you will be very resistant to figuring it out, or you’ll go in that doomsday kind of tunnel, of you’re never going to figure out the right offer, and you’re just going to spin in it.

Versus if you choose what you love, what you would want to buy, what you would be willing to go to bat for to sell, what feels worthy of a fight, of a grind, of working hard, you’re going to be much more likely to do it, to stay with it. Oh, they didn’t buy that yet? Oh, they didn’t get the vision. Let me try again. Oh, this is really hard. Okay, but it’s worth it because I feel really passionately that this is the right offer. Like, you will actually stay more committed to the things you care about if you have that awareness going into it.

That’s why I created the irresistible offer protocol. So many people are making offers from just like what people have told them. “Oh, charge what you’re worth.” I can’t tell you how many coaches have come into my 2k for 2k and told me that someone has told them they should be charging more, they should be charging their worth. People will take them more seriously if they charge more. People won’t take them seriously if they charge less.

Like all of these thoughts that the industry has given them, and none of them are like, What do I want to charge? What am I excited to charge? What feels fun to roll off my tongue? And it’s this much. Who do I think is the best fit for the offer? How long do I want to coach people? How long do I think that they need to be coached? What is the thing that I’m willing to go to bat for?

When you do this, you are going to have more power every day to sell what you want. You will be happier delivering what you want to deliver. You will make more money. You will have more success, and your business will feel so much easier. It will feel so much more fun. And you won’t take the objections as personally. You’ll know that it’s an amazing offer. So if someone doesn’t want to buy it, that’s okay. There are other people who will. Like you will just, I promise you, your whole life will change if you try this on.

And if you want to really master it, we do that in the 200k Mastermind. You start that in 2K, but we really master it in 200k. Like you become a 200k earner that can sell anything to anyone, and you’re in full alignment and integrity with the offer that you really want to be selling, and you have the business model that you want to be selling. That’s the work we do in there. It has a lot to do with your selling self-concept and a lot of being willing to stay in the figuring it out and learning how to sell it, learning PSPR, and all of the things that I set you up for to be successful on this in the 200k Mastermind.

I don’t know when we’re opening again. We’ve been getting lots of emails about that. I’m not quite there yet, but the best place to be if you want to make sure you don’t miss the next opening is going to
 
staceyboehman.com/200kmastermind
. If you scroll to the bottom, it might even be at the top, but there’s a button to join the waitlist, and you want to be on the waitlist. That is where we give all of the information as soon as we have it.

And I also send weekly emails with this kind of stuff. If you’re interested in this conversation and you want to have a more advanced understanding of selling and marketing, and delivering, that’s the email list of mine to be on.
 
staceyboehman.com/200kmastermind
, join the waitlist.

All right, that is lesson number one. I cannot wait. Next week, I will give you another one. See you there. Bye-bye.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2k for 2k program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2Kfor2K. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #361: Uncertainty Tolerance
transcript:
W
elcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2k, $20k, and $200k using her proven formula.

Hi coaches, welcome to episode 361. So excited to be back here with you, podcasting. After 12 weeks, I feel like I have so much to say. I’m really excited.

Today, we’re going to talk about uncertainty tolerance, and I am certain it’s going to change your life. And then I have coming out, a 10 podcast, 10 episode podcast series, a little bit of a tongue twister, for my top, if I could narrow down top 10 lessons for the last 10 years that I’ve been in business. And so we’re going to be airing those coming up, and I’m really excited about them. I think there’s going to be some extraordinary learning and encouragement in those episodes. So I hope that you tune in.

But I feel really compelled to share this message today. I am in The Revenue Challenge. This is something that I do with my 200k Mastermind and my 2 Million Dollar Group every round that I run these Masterminds. So this is a high-level, advanced concept challenge skill set that I teach.

I believe the lesson I’m going to share today is life-changing and business-changing, for lack of just better words from the ground up. Like, if you’ve never made a dollar, this episode is for you. And if you are wanting to create your first 100k launch or your next million-dollar launch, this episode is for you.

I’m going to give some examples of even me and my business recently in the last couple of years throughout this episode. So I can’t stress it enough. No matter where you are in your business, listen to this episode, and what I’m going to share with you, it could be the thing that unlocks for you. So tolerance for uncertainty. Let’s talk about it. 

So when you have a goal, let’s talk about a finite goal. That’s what we’re doing in The Revenue Challenge. So that’s what I consider like a more of an infinite goal, like a year-long goal, like, oh, I want to make 100k in a year. It just feels like such a long amount of time, even though it is a finite period of time. It feels like such a long period of time. It’s really easy to just believe it’s going to happen and then suddenly it doesn’t. And this is what happens with a lot of people.

But when we’re talking about a 30 day period or a one-launch period, when we’re talking about a condensed amount of time, I always say like, That’s when the shit gets real, y’all. When there’s a time frame on it. But I am going to give examples of even a year. But when you have a goal in a period of time, a finite period of time, there will be a large amount of uncertainty that comes up, a large amount of uncertainty present between what you want, the action, and you are taking to get it and the time that you’re putting in to get it, and then the result coming in.

So you desire something, you go after it, and in that going after it, even in the desiring something, the going after it, and then the time between when the results come in, all of that time, think about it. All of that time is uncertainty. I want to start a business. I don’t know if I can. I want to sign my first client. I don’t know if I can. Will I make it in business? Will I be able to make money? Will I be able to replace the income of my job? Will I be able to make 100k this year? Will I be able to do my first launch and sell out my group program? Right? It’s all uncertainty.

And what happens when you are actively going after something in a finite period of time, the closer you get to the finish line, the less your brain is going to want to tolerate all of that uncertainty. Especially if you’re really resistant to the not knowing.

So this tends to be people who really need to know, right? People who would typically go the, get a full time job, corporate route, school route, like certainty, makes me feel safe. There are people, entrepreneurs tend to be people, who have higher risk tolerance, but I think the world is now kind of gravitating towards entrepreneurship. So a lot of people are jumping on board and not really, maybe they don’t have this developed yet, or they don’t realize this is required, but I just see it come up a lot. Even the people that are the most risk-tolerant still experience this. This feeling of, I don’t know what’s going to happen.

And so you have a large amount of this that comes up in your body, that feeling. And if you are resisting it because it doesn’t feel good, because it’s scary, because you don’t have power over it, you feel like you don’t have control, right? You experience the loss of control in uncertainty.

If this feels like a really scary place, if this takes your body into fight or flight, like if you have any, like if there’s not allowance, like anything that isn’t allowance of uncertainty, the closer you get to the finish line, the more tired your brain will get of dealing with the uncertainty and resisting it and not allowing it.

And even when you’re allowing it, I still feel like, from my experiences, like I’ve had years where I’m allowing uncertainty, and it’s a constant bringing my brain back to tolerating it because my brain just doesn’t want to tolerate it. I think all of our brains don’t want to tolerate it.

So as you’re doing this, the closer you get to the finish line, the less your brain is going to want to tolerate the uncertainty. So what it does is it’s going to want to give you a prediction of the end result in order to end the uncertainty. It’s going to want you to go ahead and believe as probability what it’s predicting the outcome will be. Like this is probably what’s going to happen so that you, if you can see it, like, okay, I see the finish line, I see what I think is going to happen, then I can get into certainty and I can have relief.

And it will start organizing proof to show you that it’s right about what it’s certain of. So you’re in this finite period of goal setting and taking action. The result hasn’t come in yet. You’re getting closer and closer to the designated time period you gave yourself. You haven’t seen results yet, or maybe you’ve seen results, but not results that maybe match up what you’re expecting or what you’re trying to create. The uncertainty starts really stacking, like you’re really feeling the heaviness of it. Your brain is not tolerating it, not wanting the uncertainty. So it starts organizing the proof to show you, like, here you go, I’m certain of this thing, this outcome, and here’s all the proof to match what I believe is going to be the outcome.

The problem is, our brain is not set to do that for positive outcomes. So our brain isn’t designed to say, there’s a lot of uncertainty. I don’t know if this is going to happen. I don’t know if this is going to happen. Here’s all the proof that it’s going to happen. I wish our brains did that. I wish our brains when we were in the middle of it, in the thick of it. I wish it was designed to offer us positive feedback.

Look, here’s how we know it’s going to happen. Look at this positive outcome. Did you see this traction you got here? I mean, that was really positive engagement. That seemed to be working. I think you’re going to make it, girlfriend. Let’s go. Keep going. You’ve got this. Here’s all the evidence I have for why it’s going to work out. I wish that our brains did that. Some of you might have brains that do that. My brain does not do this, and the bulk, the majority of the people that I coach on a weekly basis, their brains don’t do this either. 

Their brains do the opposite, right? The proof is always the probable outcome is always that you’re going to fail, right? Probable outcome failure. Here’s all of the evidence that I’m going to show you to prove that’s correct, right? That you aren’t going to create what you want.

And if you haven’t been looking for tangible proof of the opposite, that you will succeed and that you are going to create what you want, like if you haven’t been gathering evidence along the way or creating evidence in your brain, reinforcing that it’s going to happen, if you haven’t been seeing any traction yet, right? If you haven’t been getting feedback that it is happening, you haven’t been having engagement and having people reach out that they’re interested, and having people book consults or having people click on your sales page.

If you haven’t been getting that, you’ll be very inclined to grasp for the certainty of failure to release you from the tension in your brain and your body of holding the uncertainty. You would rather grab the, this is just our brains, grab the certainty of failure than hold the uncertainty of possible success, the closer you get to the finish line, if it looks like or even feels like there could be a remote potential for a missed expectation, a disappointment, or a failure.

So this could look like, I have no consultations on the books, and I’m getting close to my deadline for my goal. I haven’t made any money yet. I’ve been at this for three weeks, and there’s no traction. It’s the final day of my launch, and I’m not even close to my goals. We just started the launch, and the sales are already down from what I expected. So I’m already failing, right?

Your brain would rather grab for the certainty of loss than keep tolerating the uncertainty of potential loss or potential win. It’s wild. The loss feels too heavy to hold, and the possibility to win feels too small to be true. So we just are like, okay, it’s got to be a fail. You give in, you fold, you quit, you grab the certainty that it isn’t happening this time either. I can’t tell you how many people have said, I just, I don’t goal set because every time I try, I always fail.

And I’m always wondering, did you really fail? Like what was the fail? Was the fail, I gave it absolutely everything my all. I stayed in belief the entire time. I evaluated and kept taking more action, kept getting more creative, kept problem-solving at the highest level possible. I saw it all the way through the finish line, extended the finish line, kept going. Like, did you really? Or at what point did you give up? Did you stop putting energy, stop putting value, stop connecting to it, stop believing, stop serving?

Like, it isn’t happening this time either, is more like, I didn’t happen this time either. And then what happens is the cycle of the result not happening is just reinforced again in your brain. Right? Like, see, I can’t do it. It didn’t happen again. So the probability of it ever happening is even smaller and then each attempt after you go in with a higher amount of certainty that you’re going to fail and a higher amount of uncertainty tolerance, like I just can’t handle any more potential like potentialness to fail. I can’t handle the unknown because I believe so deeply the unknown is going to be bad that the unknown feels so terrible, right? I’ve tried this many times and it’s never worked.

Versus, you could say the reality from this moment on could be, I’ve not yet developed the tolerance for this uncertainty. So I keep grabbing for the certainty of failure and then proving it to myself through my thinking, through my actions, through the way I feel while I try to go after this goal.

Which is not the same, right? You grabbing for the certainty of failure so that you don’t have to feel uncertainty, you quitting ahead of time, you reinforcing that it’s not going to happen. That version of you, even if you’re like getting your body to still take action and make offers and send emails and go live and write podcasts, that version of you is not the same version of, of course I’m going to do this. Of course I’m going to win. I’m totally going to create this result. I’m so excited.

Like I always say, when you believe you’re in demand and you believe your offer is in demand and you believe you will create the result, it’s like you’re hosting the best party ever and you’ve got so many RSVPs and you know the party is going to be amazing. The thought that you put into it into creating it and designing it, hosting it, everything is so high because you’re just so excited. That’s not the version that we bring to ourself to our goals most often.

And I know that this might sound crazy, right? That we would rather the known, even if it feels crappy or is unhealthy, we would rather that than the unknown. We would rather, our brain actually create safety in believing we’re going to fail for ourselves. It actually creates more safety there than leaning into belief that you could do it. You will feel more unsafe leaning into positive expectation than you will negative expectation.

It’s wild, and this is how our brain operates. It feels safer with negative expectation. It feels safer with the certainty that you will fail than facing the uncertainty and keeping going, not knowing if you’re going to fail or not.

We tell ourselves subconsciously, I’d rather just know I’m going to fail and be done with it than deal with how the uncertainty feels in my body. And we tell ourselves we’re crazy or impractical to believe in the positive wanted outcomes without proof. Like anytime you say I’m kidding myself, that’s you telling yourself you’re crazy and impractical for believing a positive wanted outcome. That’s what you’re telling yourself.

But most money made for the first time or more money than you’ve ever made before for the first time isn’t going to be known. Entrepreneurship does not have yellow flashing lights pointing you in the right direction. It feels more like you’re blindfolded, stumbling in the dark, hands out, trying not to fall, and believing that whole time that you’re going to find your way, no matter how many things you knock into.

So you have to maintain certainty in the positive wanted outcome through the finish line, beyond the finish line. The moment you give up and you stop trying, you drop your energy, you drop your service, you stop problem-solving, you stop thinking creative, you stop connecting, you release the desire for the outcome because you tell yourself it’s not possible. So why would I desire something that it’s not possible? It’s all gone. Poof.

And anything that you had built up and you had going for you, much of which was probably invisible to you, growing under the surface, all of that stops. It’s like you’re boiling water, and the moment you turn the heat down, the boil stops. But it’s not that the water wasn’t actually boiling. You turn the heat down. Or that you can’t boil water. You turn the heat down, right?

The problem is in entrepreneurship and in making money, we can’t see the boiling point. It happens sometimes quite invisibly. It’s like, nothing’s happening, nothing’s happening, nothing’s happening, nothing’s happening, bam, client shows up out of nowhere.

I actually have a podcast about this, where I had students record their stories of signing clients out of nowhere. No expectation, had no idea someone was following them and paying attention to them, no idea someone was considering coaching with them. Bam, client shows up, reaches out. “I’ve been following you for a long time. I think I’m ready for coaching.” You can go find that episode and listen to it. It’s such proof of this conversation. 

I had a client recently that was failing webinar after webinar after webinar, and then they just got their first five sales on their webinar without doing a consult, on the webinar, five people sending payment notifications coming in, no indication that was going to happen.

So you have to keep going through the finish line with belief, with positive expectation, giving the service, problem-solving the whole way, thinking creatively, connecting, holding the desire, serving the whole time. But in order to do that, the thing you have to develop is the tolerance for uncertainty.

Yes, you might not get the result you want. That’s true. Tell your brain that. You’re right, brain. It’s a lot of uncertainty. I might not get what I want. It is possible. Right? I have a 50/50 chance. But this is what I ask myself, and this is what I ask my clients when we’re in this Challenge.

In The Revenue Challenge specifically, but in general when I’m coaching them, I ask them this question. Who do you want to be in the middle? Who do you want to be in the uncertainty? Like, how do you want to show up to uncertainty in your life? I think this is a question to deeply contemplate. This is something to really take an hour, take 30 minutes, take 20 minutes, it doesn’t even have to take a long time, but start a journal prompt. Go take a walk. It doesn’t even have to be, you don’t have to write it down. Go take a walk. Ponder it in the shower. Who do I want to be in uncertainty?

I always say a true leader and a true coach is someone who can go into any uncertain situation and they bring the certainty. So what does that look like? What’s that look like for you? What’s that look like for all of us?

So what can you be certain of in the uncertainty? Can you be certain of you giving 100% of you through the finish line? Like, I don’t know what’s going to happen with other people. I don’t know if they’re going to buy this offer. I don’t know if they’re going to sign up in as many of them as I anticipated. I don’t know if this is going to land, but what I know is I’m going to go 100% through the finish line. Can you be certain of your ability to tolerate uncertainty?

This is something I know about myself as I’ve developed this a lot recently. Like I have really upped my level of tolerating the uncertainty. And so I know, I’ve told my husband at least three or four times recently, like, can you believe this thing? Like where we were, the tangible result that maybe we’ve had at different times in our lives, and then where we are now and how much uncertainty we faced to get here. Like, I am a master at tolerating uncertainty. I’m like, can you believe your wife did this? Can you believe your wife did that? Pumping myself up all the time. My own cheerleading squad.

Can you be certain of the value you offer? Like if anything else, could you be like, I am certain of how good I am of a coach, or I am certain of how much I fight for my clients. I am certain of the value of coaching. If you don’t have any of these things, start developing it. What am I certain of when it comes to the value of coaching? What am I certain of when it comes to me as someone’s coach? What am I certain of if someone invests in themselves and tries this thing called coaching for them? Like, just start asking yourself, what am I certain of? What am I certain of when it comes to my offer? What am I certain of my level of service?

People think this is crazy, but for a very long time in my business, not anymore, but for a very long time in my business, eight years, nine years-ish, I had money-back guarantees on every single one of my offers. And I sold my 2k for 2k program to so far to date, like over 6,000 people. And I’ve sold my 200k Mastermind to over a thousand people. You don’t create at least $2k, you don’t create at least $25k, I’m going to give you that money back. What? How could you do that? How could you ever make that offer? The level of certainty I have.

I used to think to myself, like, listen, I know they’re going to create $25k, but what I know to be true is even if they don’t, I’m going to get them on calls and I’m going to coach them until they do. I used to create Make Your Money Back calls in the 200k, and we would start them like eight weeks out from the end of the mastermind and I would only invite people on that hadn’t made their money back yet. And I’d be like, okay, we’re coaching all the way through the finish line. And the only people on this call are the same people in the same boat as you and we’re just coaching on the same thing over and over and every single one of you is getting across the finish line.

That was certainty in myself. So I could tolerate offering a program where, at the end, I might have coached someone for six months straight and then given them all of their money back. Like, what? I am certain in that of myself. I am certain in my product. I know that my products are so good, I could put that on them.

The only reason I don’t anymore is because now I’m certain of how I want to feel in my containers and the type of client I want to work with. And I want to work with someone who has risk tolerance because they’re better entrepreneurs and they have more success.

So now I’m certain of my best client, so I don’t need to offer any, I don’t need that guarantee anymore. Because I’m like, my best client doesn’t need it. So I’m certain of myself. Now I’m certain of my best client. So what are you certain of? Are you certain of the connection that you feel to your people? I am certain of that. I am certain that I’m so connected to them that I will always know the thing that I need to say to them. I won’t run out of ideas, and I won’t run out of coaching. Can you feel certain that you will keep problem-solving and won’t quit?

Right? This is even in the uncertainty. So I’m not talking about creating certainty so that you don’t have to feel uncertainty. I am saying when you are in the uncertainty and you don’t have full control over the outcome and you don’t know what’s going to happen yet, can you hold that and tolerate it while also knowing on the other, like in one hand, you’re holding and tolerating uncertainty, and yeah, I might fail, and yeah, this may not end the way I want, yeah, this might suck, yeah, I might feel disappointed, yeah, this is uncomfortable.

And in the other hand, can you be like, and you know what, even though I don’t know any of this stuff, here’s what I do know. I feel certain that I’m going to keep problem-solving and that I’m not going to quit. Can you be certain that you want to enjoy and be proud of your actions, no matter what results they’re creating?

I tell my clients this all the time. I had this powerful realization, like within the last year or so, two years, that I like myself better when I’m in belief. I like myself better when I’m working really hard for something. I like myself more when I’m expanding my capacity. I like myself more when I’m showing up and fighting for what I want, giving it my all, and getting up and going after any fail. I love myself more in my resilience than weakness. I like myself more when I overcome excuses and obstacles versus giving to them. I have a better experience of being me in my body when I live this way, when I have this experience. I love me in my power and in my willingness to tolerate uncertainty. I love me more in that than my intolerance to uncertainty and my mental weakness. I can’t handle this. I’m not capable. I don’t have the capacity. I don’t like that version of myself.

Have you ever stopped and thought about that? Like, do you enjoy the version of yourself that tells yourself I’m not capable, I can’t do this, it’s not possible for me, I don’t have the capacity? Like when you say that out loud, I’ve maxed out my capacity, do you enjoy that version of you?

Because at the end of the day, I was telling my students in The Revenue Challenge, so much of The Revenue Challenge is capacity work, so much of it. How many times in The Revenue Challenge are they telling themselves I can’t do this, I don’t have the time, I don’t have the energy?

I asked them on call one, we’ve done so far at the time of recording, we’ve done two of the seven calls, and on call one I asked them, if you were to quit or back away from this challenge and not go all the way through and disappear and not show up for the coaching and stop engaging with the goal, why would you do it? Like, what would be the thing? Like, let’s go ahead and know it ahead of time, the thing that’s going to try to take you out of this challenge.

The biggest response I got, the most people said, time and energy. I’ll tell myself I don’t have the time, I’ll tell myself I don’t have the energy. Do you enjoy that version of yourself the most? Do you like that version of you? I don’t like that version of me. I know that.

So just for my experience of it all, regardless of whatever I create a result, what I know is I’m going to tolerate the uncertainty because to me, the version of me who doesn’t is the actual intolerable thing. Like our brain is saying, Oh, I can’t tolerate certainty. No, no, no. I can’t tolerate mental weakness inside of me. I can’t tolerate being less of me. I can’t tolerate my excuses and obstacles. I can’t tolerate my bullshit. I can’t tolerate wanting something and then not doing anything about it. Like that’s what I can’t tolerate. I can handle some uncertainty along the way. I can handle that. But I can’t handle the me who doesn’t try. I can’t handle the me who gives up, the me who is out of my power. That’s my truth for me. I think you should explore this for you.

And listen, I can actually tolerate and handle that version of myself, and many of us are, right? Right now, we are tolerating mental weakness inside of ourselves. We are tolerating quitting on ourselves. We’re tolerating less than what we know we’re capable of. We’re tolerating telling ourselves we don’t have the capacity, that we don’t have the time, that we don’t have the energy. We’re tolerating all kinds of less than how we should be living. We’re tolerating making less money than we should be making. We’re tolerating less success than we should have. We’re tolerating less happiness than we should have. We’re tolerating less peace, less balance, less enjoyment of life. We’re tolerating so much, right? We actually can handle it. We have lots of practice in it. We know what it’s about. I just don’t want to anymore.

So the road to your most powerful self, who will coincidentally be the version of you that you probably enjoy the most, is being willing to stand strong in the face of uncertainty. And can you be willing to feel that in your body for a short period of time, for a long period of time, for as long as it takes? A day to start out, a week to start out? What about a year? A whole year of uncertainty.

I was just coaching on this, and so right now I have the public challenge that I’m running where people can join, and even if they’re not my higher-level masterminds, get a taste of what this is, this work is like, and these types of conversations. But then I also have calls in my 200k Mastermind that are just for my 200k students, and I have calls for my 2 Million Dollar Group that are just for them, where they can get coaching on this as well.

And I was in my 2 Million Dollar Group, and we were talking about this level of uncertainty. And I told this story. I said when I restructured, when I restructured my business, like my offers, and then also restructured my entire operation, back-end operations, and my company and my team, everything. Like we basically just said, we’re doing a complete 180 for everything we’re doing, while also millions of dollars of revenue were coming in. It’s a big ask. Like, what I did was a little crazy.

But while I did that, in the year that I did that, we were at break-even for our expenses for 10 months. I dumped $6 million of expenses in one year. Actually, in just a couple of months, I think. There was like a period of time where it was like you could see it in my profit and loss where the expenses were going down every single month, but it did take time for them to go down, and it took time to build back up the structure.

So I was at break even for 10 months as I dumped expenses and built up new offers, sold new things, sold the same offer but different ways. And in the final two months of the year, bam, profitability, a million dollars cash in the bank. Craziness.

I asked my husband this recently because now we’re so far beyond it. I said, Do you think another entrepreneur would have folded six months in? Like I was like, do you realize how like literally how crazy it is what I did? Do you realize how awesome I am?

Like, I have to tell myself this because I don’t realize it all the time. Like I live with me all the time, and you live with you all the time. So, likely you’re not giving yourself credit as well. Like, I’m not even trying to be like annoying, but we just don’t give ourselves credit. So I spend a lot of time trying to recognize the greatness inside of me, and I’ll tell my husband about it, so I can tell myself about it.

But seriously, like, it doesn’t make sense what I was able to do. Most people would have folded three months in, six months in, nine months in for sure. Like mentally collapsed under the uncertainty. They would have stopped creating value, held back, stopped working towards the result, and either folded completely and closed their doors or stayed at break-even.

So many people would have done that. And they would have been like, look, I’ve been at break even now for a year and been telling themselves like it’s never going to happen. I’m never I might as well and then quit. It was a lot of uncertainty the whole year, bringing myself back to I know what I’m creating, I’ve got to tolerate this uncertainty in my body. But I did, I tolerated it in my body. I grew my capacity to experience that emotion. I grew my certainty in myself. I held both of those at the same time. And now no one can take that away from me.

There have been so many people reaching out to me, and they’re like, well, we had someone on The Revenue Challenge that was like, I had a $120,000 business last two years ago, and then I made $8,000 last year. I’m like, I can help you with that. I made $55,000 one year, and I made $5,000 the next year or $15,000 the next year, whatever it was. Yeah, I can help you with that, too.

Like, my certainty is so high, it does not matter what the gap is and how big the hole feels. I’m like, we’ve got this. I know exactly what we have to do. The first thing is you have to develop your tolerance for uncertainty. You’re not going to be certain that you’re going to be able to build it back. You’re not going to be certain that you’re going to be able to build it beyond what it was. You’re not going to be certain. There’s not going to be tangible proof for a large amount of the time. You don’t know yet if you can do it because you haven’t done it yet. So we got to be willing to feel all of that and grow our certainty in ourselves, in our capability, in our capacity, in our time, in our energy, in all of the things. 

And now, this year, what’s so crazy is I refuse to get on tax meetings. It’s not very mature of myself, but I really don’t enjoy doing tax meetings. And so my husband does them as part of his role in the business. And so he got on the tax meeting and he got off, and he was like, Stacey, did you know that you grew your business by a million dollars of revenue? First of all, yes. And our profit is almost at 60%. Yes. And he said, Well, our tax guy wants to know, like, what did you do this year? Like this, he’s like, there aren’t businesses doing this year. Like, what did you do?

And I want to say, like, is it too simple? Is it too simple to say, I tolerated a year of uncertainty, and I grew my certainty in myself, and I kept showing up, and I kept giving value and I believed in what I was creating more than I didn’t believe.

Like, yes, there was strategy, but none of it works if you’re resisting the emotions, your emotions the whole time. Right? You could do all the right things, but if you’re mentally collapsing inside of yourself, if you’re emotionally collapsing inside of yourself, none of it matters. You can do all the right things, and it’s not going to pan out.

So I want you all to take this into if you’re in The Revenue Challenge, take this into The Revenue Challenge, take this into your next launch, take this into your first scale to a million. This is also where I see people really kind of unravel with themselves, is when they try to scale to a million, like they forget how freaking talented they are because they’ve created multiple six-figure businesses, and in the like scale to try to double or triple that, they lose themselves.

They lose themselves in the uncertainty of maybe, maybe I won’t get to a million. Maybe all this energy and effort will be, won’t be worth it. Maybe I’m not good enough. Maybe I don’t want have what it takes. They lose themselves in that. That feeling keeps them up at night. It gives them so much anxiety, they can’t function sometimes.

You know, I remember my first year was, I was a disaster. I had so much anxiety. I’m just being honest about it because I think we have to have the conversation. I had so much anxiety because everybody else in my Million Dollar room, they were all much further along. Like I came in at 300k as the underdog and all of them were at 500k, but also they had systems and structures in their business in place that I didn’t that made them even more prepared to double their revenue. So I was tripling my revenue and had no systems and no processes, and no things skills in place that would have made me ready to scale to a million.

So I had to do way more work, right? Inside of myself, inside of my business, and it was a heavy amount of uncertainty and feeling inadequate and feeling like I didn’t belong. And I met all of that. I faced it. I got intimate with that. Like, yeah, this is a part of me that doesn’t feel like I belong, that doesn’t feel like I can do it, that feels less than everybody else in this room. And I’m willing to feel all of those emotions. And why do I want to scale to a million? Why do I want to do this work? Like what part of me does believe it’s possible? Right? What am I certain of?

I remember when I got kicked out, not invited back to this room. I remember telling my husband, I’m going to fight my way back in this room, but if she doesn’t accept me, I am going to find another coach. I will figure it out. I’m getting to a million. That’s what I knew inside of myself. I’m doing it. And because I had that level of certainty in the uncertainty, I got my way, I asked my way back in, and got in. What I knew I was willing to do is everything it took.

I remember my coach was like, okay, you’ve got to go through Master Coach training. I want you to take this 100k training. You’re also going to be in the Million Dollar training. I’m like, yep, what I’m certain of is I’m willing to work this hard. So are you willing to do that too? And who are you? Who are you lifting the heavy weight of uncertainty? Who are you when you’re tolerating the discomfort and moving forward with purpose and belief of what you are creating? Like, who are you? Who do you want to be? I want you to be so freaking empowered. 

I was telling The Revenue Challenge, this Challenge, so many people think that it’s about being positive for 30 days straight. Nope. It’s about being powerful for 30 days straight. It’s about being powerful through the finish line of your goal. You don’t need to feel positive one freaking second of it.

People who are looking to hire coaches don’t need your positivity; they need empowerment. They need to see you lifting the heavy weights. They need to see you facing uncertainty, tolerating discomfort, moving forward with purpose. That is the coach they want to hire because that’s what’s going to be required of them, too.

If you could just sprinkle some fucking fairy dust on them and some confetti and shoot some rainbows up their ass for them to get the result, great. That would work. If, if, if you could do it, but that’s not what it, that’s not how it works. It’s not just like, like you can’t just give them mantras for their life and suddenly they have results. Like, positivity is not going to fuel them either. Some of it, right? Positive expectation, the certainty will make you feel good. Service makes you feel good. Connection makes you feel good. Like, there are feelings that feel good along the way.

But I don’t, I don’t believe that empowerment feels good. If you really think about it, what feels good is what you get after empowerment. I’ve asked this on an Entrepreneur Series before: What is the actual feeling of empowerment? Like, what’s the vibration in your body? What is creating empowerment feel like? What’s the experience of it? Being empowered in a challenging situation, in an obstacle, in uncertainty, it’s mostly emotions that feel bad.

But people tend to think, Oh, it feels so good to be empowered. No, it feels good after you’ve empowered yourself. The empowerment itself is very difficult because you have to tell yourself you’re wrong about the thing you can’t do and then empower yourself to do it, right? Push power into yourself. That’s what your people need too. So they don’t need your positivity; they need your empowerment. They need you to be able to lift the heavy weights, and they need to see you doing it with integrity, being a product of your product. 

And I want to offer, because I was coaching someone on this in The Revenue Challenge. She was saying, I know I need to be doing more belief work. I feel like it is a bigger thing than I give it, but it tends to be the thing that I do last, or if I run out of time, not at all.

And I want to offer that this, what I’m speaking about here, this work, this skill of tolerating uncertainty, of carrying the heavy weight, of moving forward, going through the finish line, holding uncertainty and tolerating it while also building up your certainty. This isn’t just something. It’s not the extra thing you do at the end of the day. It’s not the thing that you do if you have time, and you don’t do if you don’t have time. It’s not just something, it’s everything. It is the difference between people who make it and people who don’t. People who skyrocket and people who don’t. People who do extraordinary things and people who don’t. People who do the impossible, people who don’t. It’s everything.

All right, I hope you have an amazing week. If you’re in the challenge, I wanted to create this episode really for you to like be a power boost, but also for any future challenges in my 200k Mastermind, my 2 Million Dollar Group, and just anyone that’s a listener of this podcast that needs this juice inside of them this week.

Maybe it’s to just believe that you could start your business. Maybe the uncertainty is keeping you from even going after your first client because there’s so much uncertainty of whether you can do it. This is your first ask. Like, if you really want a client, are you willing to lift the weights of uncertainty to get it?

All right, have a beautiful week. I love you so much. Talk to you next week.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2K for 2K program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2Kfor2K. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #360: Creating Money in 30 Days
transcript:
Welcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2K, $20K, and $200K using her proven formula.

Hello, hello, hello. I’m so excited to be here. So, it was 2018. That is how long I have been running The Revenue Challenge. If my memory is correct, I don’t know that I did one on the first round of 200k Mastermind. The very first one, I don’t think I did this, but the second one, we ran it the first 30 days of the Mastermind. I just remember it very vividly. At the time, the Mastermind was $10,000, and I had a room of 30 beautiful souls sitting in front of me in Chicago, Illinois. And I flipped my chart, and it said $10k in 30 days. And there was a little bit of a gasp in the room. And I said, “This is what we’re going to do.”

Most people will join a mastermind or join a container, and they will wait the entire container to create a return for their investment. I don’t want to do that. Let’s do it in the first 30 days, and let’s make a huge impact. Let’s really do this and get it done so that the rest of the Mastermind, you can profit. And I remember that conversation vividly. And I remember feeling so convicted in this, not just because I wanted them to make their money back in the Mastermind right away, but because of the importance of learning the skill of making money on demand.

We call it in the 200k Mastermind—that’s my higher-level Mastermind—we call it turning the money faucet on and off. There’s a really important aspect of that. And so I really want you to think about it like that. If you had the skill—and I’m going to tell you a couple of my stories that are really why this matters to me—but if you had the skill, like going into your kitchen and just turning the faucet on and the water coming out, if you had that skill and instead of water it was money, and then you could turn it off and be like, “Okay, good. Done. Now I’m going to go walk away from the sink for a little bit.”

And then I’m going to come back and I’m going to turn the water back on. We have no thoughts. Think about this. Unless you didn’t pay your electric bill, you have no thoughts when you go to your sink to turn your faucet on that water isn’t going to come out. But the scariest thing as an entrepreneur is I could go put effort out into the world. I could move the faucet lever, and nothing could happen.

And that realization, that thought is the number one reason people fail when they’re selling and trying to make money. Because the moment you have that thought that I could possibly go move the lever and nothing could happen, that fear, especially when it comes to money, takes over your body. It takes over your energy, it takes over how you show up, it takes over everything. And then you show up ever so slightly differently to everything because of your fear that the money might not come out of the faucet.

So this is the lifeline of really good sales, really confident entrepreneurs, and really healthy businesses, is if you know when I go move that dial, when I go manipulate that lever, there will be something there for me. So if I spend energy doing a consult, going to a networking event, if I spend energy doing a launch, and I put everything that I’ve got into it, I give all of me, and I do that, money’s going to be there.

If you believe that 100% with all of your being and your body and you carry yourself that way through all of your effort, all of your energy, all of your creativity, the likelihood of money being there is very high. But we don’t do that. We either don’t know how to find the thoughts where we’re not really certain that money’s going to come out, or we battle ourselves the entire time.

And this Challenge helps my Mastermind students. We do it every single round, and now there is a process that’s recorded. So many of them do a Challenge every month in the Mastermind. They’re like, “I’m redoing this Challenge,” or, “I’m doing a Challenge to make even more money. I’m doing my next Challenge.” So they have access to be able to do it all the time. They have all the resources, all the support. We coach on it on the calls.

They can—they typically go through the entire process every time they run the Challenge. They’ll watch coaching calls that are Challenge-specific, and they’ll get the support to go out and do it over and over and over. And the more they do the Challenge, the better they get at it, the faster they learn to make money, the more confident they are, the more concrete making money starts to feel.

So here’s why this matters. The other fear that looms over people when they start a business and are running a business is, “Can I make this business work long-term? Can I make it work now? Can I make it work six months from now? Can I make it work a year from now?” I remember when my husband, when I retired him six years ago before we had kids, multiple people at his job said, “Good luck. I hope it lasts.” Something about the money’s going to dry up, and it’s not going to last. Like little comments here and there about how it’s going to dry up. And I never had that fear. Ever. But that fear exists in a lot of people. Will I be able to make it? And if I do, will I be able to replicate it?

And being able to create money on demand is the reason you know you will always be in business. Because—and I’m going to tell you this important story now—because if your business ever got in trouble and it needed money, if your business ever, if you had a big tax bill, if you had an unexpected hire you needed to make, if you had an unexpected refund you had to do.

I remember one time I had to refund someone. They paid in full for a discount. This was maybe my first year of business. She was the best client. Like she did a VIP with me. She ended up buying coaching for someone else, and then she met this guy, and he hated the idea of coaching. And the moment she got engaged, he told her he had to, she had to fire her coach. And instead of being honorable and in integrity and saying, “I already paid this coach and I got a discount and I paid in full, and I know it’s non-refundable,” she really was like, “You must refund me. I’m going to get a lawyer. You have to refund me.” It was a really nasty situation.

And so I just decided to refund her. But at the time, I was investing so heavily in my business, and I had living expenses, right? I’m delivering the coaching. I have living expenses. And so I had spent some of that money. I didn’t have the full refund available.

Like, people don’t realize that when you deliver coaching and it’s your job, you’re living on that money while you’re delivering coaching because it’s your job. It’s just like you go to a corporate office and you get your paycheck, you get to go spend that because you earned it and you made it. And you had expenses to be able to go out and do that, right? You had childcare and you had to buy clothes, and you had to buy lunch and gas that week to get to work. You’re not just holding all of the money all of the time. And so I didn’t have the money.

And I had to refund her in—I just didn’t want to deal with—I didn’t have to refund her, but I decided to refund her because she went from best client to—it was wild. Like screaming at me very, very quickly. And I just, I was so new in business. I didn’t know what to do, and I was like, “I got to refund her.” And so it was $13,000, and I had to put it on a credit card. This is before I knew how to turn the money faucet on and off. So I had to take the credit card out somehow, and I just remember getting credit and paying her $13,000 of a refund on a credit card because I didn’t have the cash. And I’ve also had a $600,000 unexpected tax bill.

And things like this destroy businesses if you don’t know how to handle it. And learning how to create money on demand, knowing how to do that saves you from all of this. If your kid is in school and getting bullied, and you decide to put them in private school, and suddenly you have to pay $7000 a year or $15,000 a year for private school, and you didn’t have the money in the bank.

And you just signed up for a mastermind to grow your business and go to the next level. And suddenly you’re like, “Oh, now I have to—I have to quit the mastermind that I signed a contract for and agreed to do and was really excited to do because I couldn’t come up with the money.” That, that is why this skill matters so much. I’ve never had to compromise my desires, my integrity, my personal safety and health of my finances. I’ve always been able to create the money on demand. And so I feel really passionately about this.

So this is how The Revenue Challenge was created. In 20, I believe it was 2018, I was in a mastermind to make millions of dollars, to learn how to scale to my first million, and then I eventually made eight figures in that mastermind. And one of the things that they would do is we would meet four times a year, and you had to bring your profit and loss statement. So I don’t know if y’all do profit and loss statements. I don’t remember when I started doing them, but at some point in business, you’ll be doing profit and loss statements. And it’s an itemized list of what you, the profits you’ve brought in and then every expense that has gone out and the money that is in the business. And one of the things that they would, the mastermind would ask is certain things on your P&L. So I’m going to give you an example.

So in the mastermind, it wasn’t a requirement, but they taught that for every $100,000 you made, you should have $10,000 in revenue, $10,000 in… we called it working capital, but $10,000 in your account for the business. So if you were making $200,000, you should have $20,000 set aside. If you’re making $600,000, you should have $60,000 set aside so that if you have to do a refund, or you have to hire someone, or you want to pay for run ads or anything that you want to spend in your business, you have that money. It’s your rainy-day fund.

And I had built up, at the time, that year I made $800,000, and so I was around $600,000, and I had $60,000 in my reserve. Actually, I think that’s what we called it. Working capital is more for expenses immediately going out. So it was in my reserve. And I was very prepared, was doing everything that I was supposed to be doing. And then I found the house that I live in now.

My husband and I were living in an apartment at the time because I was investing so heavily in my business. But I just happened to be sent the most amazing, beautiful, ten out of ten house for everything my husband and I ever could imagine wanting in a house. And I didn’t have the money for the down payment, but I did have my reserve, and it was the exact amount that I needed to put on a down payment on my house.

And I know that’s so crazy for so many people, but I just knew that I was going to make that money back. I was growing actively, so I just had a lot of faith. But also, I was willing to get into this house. I was willing to, if I had to make payments on my tax bill for the whole next year, I was willing to do that to get into this house. That’s how bad I wanted it. And so I did.

And every time we went to these quarterly meetings, we didn’t always get asked about our P&L, but this time, they asked. There was an email that went out two or three days—I don’t know, it was very shortly before we were going to arrive at this mastermind that said, “Bring your P&Ls. I want to know… here’s all of this information I want to know,” and one of the things was what’s the amount of money in your reserve.

And I was so embarrassed because I knew that I had made this risky move. I knew that I shouldn’t possibly have used my tax money to buy my house, and I did. And I had already spent the whole year coming up against inadequacy in the room. It felt like, why am I here? Everybody else is so much bigger, so much better. Their businesses are so much further along. They’re so much smarter. They’re Ivy League educated. I don’t belong here. I spent the whole year thinking I didn’t belong anyways. And now I’m going to show up to this meeting, and everyone else is going to have their reserve, and I’m not going to have my reserve.

And I can’t tell you, I was more petrified about that than the $600,000 unexpected tax bill a few years later. Probably some good student complex to begin with. So, I was forced; I was faced with a decision. And I cannot tell you—I’ve coached thousands of coaches in the last ten years, thousands—and I cannot tell you when you’re at this fork in the road, how many people go the other way that I went.

So I’m going to tell you the way that I went. The way that I went is I’m going to come up with $60,000 in the next couple of days. I’m going to solve this problem. I’m going to figure it out. I’m going to make money on demand. I rarely, rarely in my coaching when I see coaches come up against a money issue in their business, whether it’s for their business or their personal life—and typically in my 2k for 2k program and a 200k Mastermind, and in that range below 200k, I would even say all the way to 500k, the people, I would say from 500k and below, the typical thing that happens is they have a personal finance issue. It’s not rarely a business finance issue. Sometimes you might have a refund that you weren’t expecting, but typically your business isn’t big enough yet. And sometimes you might have a bigger tax bill than you expect. But typically, your business isn’t big enough to have big business surprises.

So it’s typically life surprises that happen. And of the thousands and thousands and thousands of coaches—I have 6,000 coaches in my 2k for 2k program. I have probably more than that have actually gone through it. I have over a thousand, maybe 1,200 people who have gone through my 200k Mastermind. So, a lot of coaches in the last ten years. And I would say 90% of the people that I come across who have this issue don’t even ask for coaching on it. They quietly give up on themselves, freak out, and they go the path of, “I’m not able to do this, so I just have to either quit my business, quit my coaching, quit my whatever it is that I had intended to do. I have to stop because this personal finance thing is in the way.” Or, “quit my business and go back to work.”

I don’t have the ability to generate the money to pay for the problem, or pay for the desire, right? If you wanted to go on a trip or something. There’s been so many things that I just—like the house, I just desired. And I was like, “All right, I’m going to take the money from my business, but then I still have to come up with the money to replace the money for the business,” right? That was a desire thing. So they never, ever go this way, which is, “I can create the money. I can make money on demand. I’ll just get creative. I’ll make an offer. I’ll go do it. I’ll sign a new client.” I’ve done this so many times. 

And so I really see it as a big thought error in coaches who are entrepreneurs. I see it as the biggest obstacle that coaches face, and I see it as the biggest barrier to having a healthy, solid business that you can keep going and that you can invest in and that you can grow consistently over and over and over.

Because I also find if you’re not growing constantly over and over and over, you, you get stale, it becomes harder to grow. The longer you go without growing, it just becomes a little bit harder to get off the ground. So there’s just infinite reasons why this matters.

So I need to come up with $60,000, and I had literally maybe a week. I made it in two days. And here’s the thing that’s really important. If people do decide, “I’m going to solve this problem. I’m going to create an offer. I’m going to make—I’m going to figure out how to make this money,” typically, they do it with hustle. They do it with offering something they don’t really want to offer, offering something that isn’t maybe their core offer that they’re offering. They try to throw something out there and see what sticks.

And every time I’ve done this, I’ve been able to—I’ve had since I started scaling to a million three core offers: 2k for 2k, 200k Mastermind, 2 Million Dollar Group. And I’ve been able to do this, staying within my core offers without hustling. But I do it very strategically.

So for that specific instance, I made an offer to my current Mastermind students. I said—we had enrollment coming up maybe a week before—and I said, “For those of you who sign up in the next 48 hours in early enrollment and pay in full, I’m taking you to Miami for two days for the most amazing VIP with me. We’re going to be at One Hotel South Beach. We’re going to be in the pool all day coaching. We’re going to go to Little Havana. We’re going to do—we did a fancy, private dinner on the dock at the Strand Hotel, I believe it was called the Strand. Like, really fancy.” I probably spent $20,000 on this VIP for two days, but I didn’t make just $60,000. I made $120,000 in two days.

My students were like, “Oh my God.” I still have the photos from that VIP. One of the, two of the best days of my entire career. The most fun. So there was nothing stressful, there was nothing crazy over the top. I wasn’t working long hours and busting my ass. I just made a really great offer, and people took it. People took me up on it. Sorry, my hand’s getting tired.

And this has happened over and over and over and over in my business. So recently, while on maternity leave, I went into my 2k for 2k program, and I had a special offer just for them that I was going to make before I went on maternity leave, but then I had my baby ten days early and didn’t make it. And I felt really strongly that they should have this offer right away, and I didn’t want them to wait because I knew everything I was going to be selling after, and there just wasn’t time to fit it in. And so I told my team, “I’m going to sell it on maternity leave.”

And I sold it out in two hours from one live stream. Sold out, made $100,000 in two hours from the same principles that I teach in The Revenue Challenge, learning how to make money on demand. Except for that one, everyone’s been asking, like, “We’ve got to reverse engineer.” They’ve been telling me they’ve watched the live stream over and over and over to figure out what I did. And I actually, that made me think, “What did I do there? How did I do that?”

And I figured this is specifically what I did there that is repeatable for my students, that I can teach my students, that will be really useful. It was actually very, very, very simple things that are very profound. And so I’m going to teach that in this next Revenue Challenge.

So after I created the $60,000 in, or the $120,000 in two days and I went to my meeting and I was like, “Yes, here, I have my $60,000 reserve,” and I created the money for my house that I wanted in two days. And from that moment on, I have felt the importance of this skill set, of being able to make money on demand when you need it, when you want it. It’s everything. I’ve done it for 2.5 million dollars in 30 days just for fun.

I remember running this a few years ago with my 200k Mastermind, and I knew I was going to ask them to do it. And the number one thing that happens when The Revenue Challenge comes up is people are like, “I’m not prepared. I haven’t prepared to put this energy and effort into it. I haven’t prepared for making money. I can’t possibly do it.”

And I didn’t have 2.5 million dollars on my revenue schedule at the time. And I thought, “You know what? Okay, I get the feeling of not being prepared.” I even challenged myself to do 2.5 million because that would be like—I went to the place in my brain where they feel, at the time it was $25,000 in 30 days. And I’m like, how do they feel with $25,000 in 30 days with where they are? How that must feel for them. What dollar amount would that take for me to feel that way? And it was 2.5 million. And so I was like, “Okay, let’s get to work. 2.5 million in 30 days, I am walking in integrity with these students who are about to go through this Challenge.”

I ended up making three million dollars. Now, it wasn’t in cash. So typically, we go for cash in The Revenue Challenge. However, I always tell people, if you generate money through payment plans that is not yet cash received, you’re not going to be mad. You still get the money. And so I made three million dollars that I received over the next six months, and I had the most amazing time, and my students were so freaking happy.

That time, I offered them—I don’t always offer a live in-person thing. I just happened to be using those two examples, but I offered them to come and do a live recording of a course for me in 200k Mastermind. So it was a one-day thing, and they just got to watch me record a new course and ask questions and be live coached, and hang out with each other, and they freaking loved it. And we had the best time.

So that was one of the other times I’ve done it. But I also had a $600,000 unexpected tax bill that came up one year. This was many years ago. And I’ve had things like that come up here and there, everywhere, all the time. Sometimes it’s just like I want to make a certain amount of money in a certain time frame. And I have the ability to do it. So being able to turn the money faucet on and believe that money is coming out is everything because it has me and the people who know how to do this going with all of their heart, 100% of their energy, putting everything into every sales opportunity that they do.

And when you are not holding yourself back, there’s a very different you that shows up. When you are fully confident, there’s a very different you that shows up. And that you makes a lot more money than the you that you make now. Makes a lot more money than you now. So that is why this skill matters. I think it matters for longevity in business. I think it matters for confidence. I think it matters for fun in sales. I think it matters for literally everything.

And the last thing I want to share with you that I also think I have not taught this ever before in The Revenue Challenge, and then I’m going to give you the link if you want to join me and tell you how it’s set up. But I’ve been on maternity leave, and I’ve known that I’m going to be doing The Revenue Challenge.

I chose it very specifically to do it right when I came back because I wanted to go from being out of business, being out of my business and not working, to level 100 right away. I don’t want there to be any building up. I was like, let’s just go. I wanted to bring the energy up for myself. I wanted to bring the energy up for my clients. I wanted to just be 100% immersed very, very quickly. I think that is the key for me. I don’t—I’m not a slow-dip kind of gal. I got to jump in the water.

So I’ve had a lot of time to think about The Revenue Challenge, and I’ve had a lot of time to think about what haven’t I said and what feels the most relevant to me now that I want to share with the people who join the Challenge. This is going to be my—I’m doing the Challenge for my 200k Mastermind students, my 2 Million Dollar Group, and then those of you who sign up to join us from this offering.

So you’ll get to join. This is a very rare opportunity. I have only done the Challenge outside of my 200k Mastermind and my 2 Million Dollar Group one time, and that was last August, I believe, or last October, something like that.

And this may be the last time I do it publicly because I do it in my Mastermind. We do it every round and it’s a lot of energy and I like to just, a lot of times I do it just for the Mastermind. But I’ve been thinking about it a lot, a lot, a lot, a lot. And this is the other thing that I’m going to be teaching inside this room. This is the other transformation that you have the possibility of walking away with. I’m going to be the example of what’s possible when it comes to selling and delivering.

So what a lot of business owners, coaches, entrepreneurs tend to think is they need a long runway of value, time, and energy in order to make money. So if you thought about making $1000 in the next 30 days, $5000 in the next 30 days, $20,000 in the next 30 days, typically your brain is going to go to, “I haven’t prepared. I need time. I didn’t create enough value. I didn’t nurture people long enough. I don’t have an audience. I don’t know who I would sell this to or how I would sell it.”

And that poses a problem too at a lot of levels in business. I again, I would say from nothing, zero, I’ve made no money, all the way up to your first million dollars, especially in the like $200k to a million dollar range. I see people cancel launches all the time because they’re like, “I just couldn’t get it done. I couldn’t get my launch materials prepared. I don’t have time to execute it. I don’t have time to put what needs to go into it in order for it to sell.”

But I was on maternity leave and made $100,000 in two hours. And that’s all I did. It was a live stream, and we sent I think one email out. A live stream and one email. It actually does not require a runway. It’s a thought error that we have that we are required to give lots of value ahead of time, required to nurture people for long periods of time, required to have been thinking about it for a really long time, required to have been putting—written a ton of emails and a ton of social posts and all the things. We’re required to do all this pre-work in order to be worthy of the money coming in or to have the audience that will bring the money in, whatever the thought is, there’s a lot of them, they’re errors. They’re not actually true.

You don’t actually have to have a huge runway. So I’m going to be the example of what’s possible for that. I have no runway. I come back in one week. And I’m just doing it. So I’ve been thinking about this. It’s like what we think when it comes to a launch or making money in business is I have to be one of those, if you live in the United States or if you live in Europe, you know those big planes that are going to go over the ocean or they’re going to fly to Asia? Like, they’re a really long flight and they’re humongous. And they need a really long runway to take off. That’s the way we think about making money. We’re like, “I need that really long runway and the really big plane.”

And the way that I think of The Revenue Challenge is it teaches you how to be one of those military planes that’s on a Navy ship in the middle of the ocean and has to take off with the tiniest runway. And it needs a specialized pilot. I teach the specialized pilot version for coaches.

How can you take off with no runway? How can you make money with nothing planned? No runway, no—I don’t have a stack of emails written. I don’t have a stack of social posted. I don’t have tons of time to do it. How can that happen as well? And I know that might seem like, “Oh, she’s just selling me get-rich-quick,” but I haven’t had that experience. It’s a thought process. It’s the way you use your brain.

And I think it is a worthy skill set if it takes, no matter how long it takes you to develop it. I think it’s one of the most worthy things to develop. Because again, if you get that tax bill, if you get an unexpected opportunity to work with someone, if you want to put your kids in a private school, if you want to invest in the stock market, if you want to pay off your house, if your husband loses their job.

I’ve had that happen so many times with entrepreneurs. I remember one entrepreneur that I was coaching was in my, I believe my 2 Million Dollar Group. She might have been in 200k, I don’t remember. She was in both, but it was in a kind of a transition period. And she was like, “Oh my God, my husband lost his job.” And she was at this growth period, and I said, “Well, it looks like you just retired him.”

And her brain wanted to be like, “Oh, I have to sacrifice. I have to suffer now because my husband lost his job, and so I have to pay the bills, and because I have to pay the bills, it’s going to stress my business, and so all of these things, right? I have to get smaller.” Instead of, “I’m going to get bigger. I’ve got this.” And I was like, “No, no, no, you’ve got this. You’re just going to make more money. You’re just going to replace this income. It’s not a problem.” What? What if you thought that? What if that was the empowered way that you thought, that you trained your brain to think that way?

It starts in The Revenue Challenge. It’s 30 days at a time. It’s your first Challenge, your second Challenge, your third Challenge, your fourth Challenge. I want to invite people, those of you, if you did the first Revenue Challenge that I offered publicly in last October, if you did that one, I want to invite you back. Let’s do it better this time. If you used to be in 200k Mastermind and you’re not in 200k Mastermind anymore, and you love the Challenge, I want to invite you in. If you’ve never done the Challenge, I want to invite you in.

This is going to be a room full of very serious people working on a very serious skill set, a skill set that can literally keep you in business, save your business, build your business back up. It is the lifeline for your business. There is no revenue requirement for this, but I do tell people that it’s rated R for revenue, meaning if you have a really bad goal aversion, you’re going to be confronted with that.

My entire 200k Mastermind and my 2 Million Dollar Group will be in this room. So there’s going to be people making 50k, 100k, 200k, 500k, a million, three million, five million. There’s going to be people making a lot of money in this room. You’re going to be seeing people having a lot of success. I remember one student last year at the very end of the Challenge made $40,000 in a day. That’s not typical. Results not typical. But you are going to see people making money. You’re going to see people celebrating.

And some people will have a hard time. It will be a challenge. This is one of the things I teach in the process is it’s called a challenge. It is a challenge. That’s in the name. It’s supposed to be a challenge. It is challenging. And I have a lot of material to help you through that challenge.

So people always tell me, “Well, I just have really strong goal aversion.” And I say, “Well, how long do you want to keep that? How long do you want to keep having goal aversion running a business?” I promise you if you were trying to be an entrepreneur and you have goal aversion, if you hate setting goals and you have a really strong physical response or emotional response or mental response to setting a goal, if it causes you massive anxiety, if you’re waking up in the middle of the night—people think something’s gone wrong when this happens. I woke up in the middle of the night with anxiety a hundred times the year I was scaling to a million dollars.

I never wake up in the middle of the night now. You got to face it. You got to face it head-on. If it gives you the sweats, if it gives you panic in your body, if you get a headache, yeah, that’s stress manifesting physically in the body. How long do you want to keep that if you’re going to call yourself an entrepreneur and be an entrepreneur?

Not long, or it will be miserable. I promise you. You’ve got to learn how to have a good relationship with setting revenue goals and achieving them if you want to have a really healthy business and have fun.

And so I want to invite everyone in, but just know it is an advanced course. It’s an advanced room. We’re talking advanced things, and it is going to be a challenge. It is challenging to learn this skill set. And it’s the most rewarding skill set that you’ll ever develop.

So if you want the link—and then I’ll give you all the details—just comment revenue. And for those of you that are spelling challenge like myself, I believe it is R E V E N U E. Revenue. Someone post it. I looked at it the other day, and it looked weird. I was like, “Wait, is that spelled right?” And then I’m like, “I should probably not have my mini chat set up with a word that feels challenging to spell.” It just looked weird. Have you ever had that happen where you look at a word and you’re like, “Is that the way it’s spelled?” I don’t know.

So, comment revenue, and we will send you the link automatically set up with a mini chat. It’s not me, it’s just a link. It’ll send you the page to sign up. So last time I did this Challenge, I gave one week’s notice. You’re getting a little bit more notice now. The very first Challenge call is November 6th. So you have some time. You have like, I don’t even know, 12 days, 13 days.
