You’re helping them make new decisions, different decisions than they’ve made before.

 

And typically, you will have people, like even if you’ve paid attention to your own self-coaching and your own implementation of things, there are times where you will get coaching and you will hear it and it will feel valid and it will feel true and like I should probably do this, but you will be on the fence of actually doing it. Or there could be a moment, I always describe this in my, I remember when I did relationship coaching 10 years ago.

The very first thing I hired someone for, really, it was life coaching, but the big chronic pain was my relationship. And one of the things I was constantly on the fence about was the moment where I would be ready to explode at my partner. Something would happen, and you know that moment where you’re ready to just pounce, and I would have to catch myself and pull myself back from that experience. And sometimes I would be on the fence of like, am I going to jump in and start yelling or am I going to calm myself down, get to neutral, drop into my vulnerability, look at what I’m actually feeling, and learn how to communicate that properly. So there’s so many times that we’re on the fence of things.

But what on the fence is, the way that I think about it for every situation, is its indecisiveness. And that is really important to know. It’s actually the opposite of decisiveness. And that again, is what we teach our clients. I think it’s the number one thing we help people do. Like, if you were like, what does a help a life coach do? I help you become decisive in your life. Decisive about the things you want, decisive to take action towards them.

I help you get out of the land of indecisiveness. What do I want? I don’t know what I want. I don’t know what the future looks like. I don’t know how to get there. All the “I don’t know,” I help you rid yourself of that. That’s what we teach our clients. If you really start thinking about it and that’s what coaching is every day, taking action, being decisive in how you’re going to think, how you’re going to feel, how you’re going to respond, what you’re going to do, what results you’re going to create, decisiveness, decisiveness.

No one created anything big in their lives, any major changes ever, by being wishy-washy, not knowing, or being on the fence. So we have to be expert fence-hopper-offers. Experts at hopping off the fence the moment we find ourselves on it. Which means anytime, for any reason, for any topic that we catch ourselves sitting on the fence, we have to know that what we are actually sitting on is indecisiveness. And then we have to immediately turn that into decisiveness.

And in order to do that, you’re going to want to have an inner process for that. And hopefully, that inner process, whatever you work out for yourself, is rooted in the same things you would teach your clients if they are making decisions. We want their decisions rooted in sufficiency. We want their decisions rooted in intention towards what they want to accomplish. It’s the only way you accomplish something is you take action decisively towards what you want. We want them to take action with self-confidence and self-belief. Right? Most humans are right in the world right now are taking action from lack of self-belief, lack of self-confidence, and that’s why they don’t like their results. So we have to build that confidence, build that belief by taking action every day as if you would if you had that.

We also want to make decisions that come from your future self and your future desired results. Again, it’s the only way you get there, and they have to be decisive. You don’t take the action the same way if you’re indecisive, but you know what the action is, and you take it, but you didn’t get your brain on board. Decisive is when your brain is on board, your emotions are on board, and then you go for it. That’s true decisiveness. And we also want that inner process for being decisive to be grounded and calm.

Like, I bet you could find a lot more as well, but those are the things that came to mind. Like when I am being decisive, I want to be sufficient. I want it to be intentional towards what I want, rooted in self-confidence and self-belief, rooted in my future self and my future desires, and from a grounded, calm place.

I don’t want the decisiveness to be rooted in fear. Sometimes we do that. We’re very decisive. Oh, I don’t want that. Now, it’s okay if you’re like, I don’t want to ride this amusement park ride, or I don’t want to go, you know, take a walk at night down this street, or I don’t, you know, want to go fly right now. Whatever it is, it’s like sometimes your fear and steering you away from a decision is good, but not when it’s creating the life that you want. Any decision made from fear is not going to give you the outcome you want. So we don’t want decisiveness rooted in that. And we also don’t want decisions that are coming from you being stuck in where you are now and not seeing a future path forward.

Because a lot of people that you get on consults with, that’s where they’re coming to you from. They are stuck in exactly where they are now and where they’ve been, and they have no clue how to move forward. And if they try to make a decision with you to say yes to you and your coaching, and they are stuck there, they will not be able to get past that.

Which is why if you’re in 2k, we talk about creating a vision for them on the consult and making that very tangible and showing them what’s on the other side so that they’re very motivated to leave where they are now because they have to overcome a lot of fear in order to leave where they are now. But most people, if they just can’t imagine another reality other than where they are now, then they’re going to have the desire for something new, and then they’re going to be stuck where they are, and that’s what creates the indecisiveness and sitting on the fence.

Sitting on the fence is “I have the desire, and I don’t have the belief.” I have the desire, and I’m stuck looking at my situation now and not seeing an alternative to get out of it. So the desire feels more like a wish or a hope or a dream. It doesn’t feel tangible. And then we also don’t want the decision rooted in urgency or lack. Like I have to take action urgently, or else something terrible is going to happen. I have to take it because I’m lacking, and I have to make up for that. Because believe it or not, that’s also not the right energy, right? To go create your future life, to go do the thing, to go accomplish what you want to accomplish. Unworthiness, unbelong, like not belonging, smallness. These are all other factors that come into sitting on the fence.

And so I think your biggest thing that you want to be thinking about right now is for anything that you’re on the fence with in your life, you want to pay close attention to why you’re on the fence. What has you there? What has you with the desire and then firmly planted on the fence, stuck in where you are now and not really believing a true future different than where you are now or being stuck there because you think the circumstances that you’re in right now are so big that they prevent you from getting off the fence.

Because your clients will think that, too. They’re going to hear all of your best-laid offer of how you’re going to help them. They’re going to hear all the value you would bring them, all the solutions you’re going to give them, how you’re going to help them become someone new. And then they’re going to be like, “this sounds amazing, however…” and “I’ve got a lot of money going out this month and you know, I’m waiting on some clients to pay me and I’ve got this going on and I’ve got that going on.”

And really, what they’re going to be telling you is my circumstances are so big that I have to sit on the fence right now with my desire and just watch because my circumstances prevent me from hopping off. And if you are not an expert in hopping off the fence, you will not be able to walk other people. It does not matter how many amazing questions you ask or what you say to them or it doesn’t matter, you will not be able to get them off the fence either.

This is why this matters. The more decisive you are, the more decisive people you will attract in your marketing. It’s just an energetic thing. I always tell my clients, your future people who want to coach are thinking about a certain type of coach. Like they’re thinking of who that person is and who they aren’t, and what the coach possesses that they need. And they’re looking for the person who models that, who lives that, who just is that. And if you aren’t that, they will not reach out to you and ask you to help them.

You can’t, if you are energetically on the fence, especially a lot of times, but really in anything big, then you’re not an energetic match. You’re not being the person, being the coach that they want to hire, because they want to get off the fence. That’s why they’re asking for help. So you’ve got to become a master at not being on the fence ever. So you want to know “why am I on the fence” the moment you recognize being on the fence.

What are the actual thoughts keeping you from making a decision? You have to be very clear what they are. Again, it will be impossible to help someone figure out what their thoughts are that are keeping them on the fence, the real thoughts, and the real feelings if you don’t have a practice rooted in this. It doesn’t matter what I teach you in 2k, 200k, 2 Million Dollar Group, doesn’t matter. This will, it will be a mental block from you.

And sometimes when you are figuring out why you’re on the fence, when you’re asking yourself, why am I on the fence? Like if I catch myself on the fence for anything, I’m exploring immediately. And sometimes our feelings reveal our thoughts. Like we are like, oh, I’m on the fence, I’m feeling uncertain, why? Here’s the thought that I’m thinking.

Or sometimes our thoughts reveal our feelings. I’m on the fence because I’m afraid this won’t be any different than all the other times. And then you’re like, okay, how is that, what feeling is that inside my body? And then do I do I think that is my best intentional feeling for creating the results I want to create and the person I want to become? For me, it’s whichever is easiest to find; I’m going to explore it. Whether it’s a feeling or a thought or a thought or a feeling, I’m going to explore that.

Now, here’s the key. This should not take more than a few minutes. Not days, not hours, minutes. Decisive people are very quick to figure out what is keeping them undecided. Decisive coaches are good at exploring their thoughts and their feelings to figure that out. You want to become that person very quickly. So not hours, not days, not weeks, not months, not years, minutes.

Now, it could, if it’s something really big, way beyond your normal decision-making processes, then it could be days. And it could maybe be a few weeks. I think that’s still extraordinary. But it could take a couple of days. I’ve considered a $100,000 investment before in my company, like $100,000 paid in full up front. I’ve considered that investment, and it took me a few days to unwind my indecisiveness and figure out exactly what it is and all, and coach myself on all the thoughts that were coming up, and like really make a clean, clear decision. It took me a couple of days, but not weeks, days.

And that was like the top of I think what I would call like my tolerance for decisiveness, right? Like my tolerance for decisiveness is very, very high. And $100,000 might have been at the time the top for me. I’d never made a $100,000 investment before in one thing. And I had already, that was the year I invested $233,000 just in coaching. I’m not talking about ads, I’m not talking about team, I’m not talking about any of that, just coaching on my brain. And so it was a lot. It took a couple of days.

But then I had decided, and I had a very clear reason. And I also want to tell you that specific reason was I just, I had some colleagues tell me, like, Stacey, you could do this on your own and save $100K. I was in the shower and I had an epiphany of I could, I don’t want to. I want to feel supported in this. It would feel amazing. The way I imagine myself feeling when I feel supported through this learning this thing, and coaching on this, I really do think it would make the difference of my energy levels, my capacity to, you know, be there for my students, sell, deliver content, create new things. I just felt like I’m willing to pay that much money for support to feel supported, to have someone holding my hand through something, to have someone teaching me, and me not having to figure it out through trial and error.

And that ended up ultimately being my decision. I could have where I am now in my business; I could have figured it out, and I just didn’t want to do it on my own. And so that, like having access to that’s my reason and I love that reason, now I’m on, I’m off the fence, and I’m decisive.

But my tolerance being that high is from a thousand little moments or 100,000 little moments along the way. It’s exercising it every day. Why am I on the fence for this thing or that thing? Doesn’t matter what it is, but for sure investments. Because I’m always thinking like, how do I help you be more of a product of your product, more in integrity with what you’re selling, so that you easily overcome objections for people who genuinely want to be yeses?

You have to think about it, being on the fence literally means I’m indecisive because I have this desire, and then there’s something in the way. I’m either not believing that I could go beyond where I am now, or it feels like my circumstances are too big to overcome, or my past is too big to overcome, my shame is too big, something is there that’s too big for me to overcome, but I also have this desire, so I’m just sitting on the fence. I’m not on the other side to be a no, but I’m also not on the side to be a yes.

Remember that’s what that means. So we’ve got to be experts in doing that. And I want to say the best way that you could start becoming an expert in this, if you’re like, well, what’s an inner process? Like, what should I do? This one’s the simplest. And if you ever are on the fence, you guys are going to laugh. It’s really simple. But if anyone, if I’m ever selling, and this happens a lot with my entrepreneur series or my 200k Mastermind, I will have because I have such a huge community in my 2k for 2k program, that people will post and they’ll either tell other students who joined or they’ll tell me “I’m on the fence.” And they won’t always say that they’re on the fence, but I know they’re on the fence.

And so they’ll say, “I’m thinking about doing this, but here’s my reservations.” And then they’ll list out all the reasons why they wouldn’t do it. And all the reasons why it would be hard. And every time I ask them one question, and when they do this question, every single time they end up signing up. Every single time, they end up moving forward. Are you ready? It’s not rocket science. I always tell them, “Okay, so you’ve given me a great argument, you know, and all the reasons why you wouldn’t do it. Tell me why you would.” That’s it. Tell me why you would do it. You could ask your people this, too. You can steal it.

But here’s why this is such a simple yet profound question and process. Because our brains are so used to giving us the argument for why we wouldn’t do something, why something is impossible, why it won’t work, why we’re not enough to do it, all the nots. This is why I wouldn’t do it. This is what’s in the way. It’s going to give you all of that all day long. And we’ve trained ourselves to only listen to that. So, post after post, customer service, email after customer service email is entire paragraphs of all the reasons why someone wouldn’t do something with one sentence of I’m thinking of doing this, but here are six paragraphs as to why I wouldn’t.

And so they’ve just never thought, they’ve never considered the desire part. Why do I desire this so much so that it has me on the fence? Because I could equally just be like, look at these five paragraphs, it’s very evidently a no. But the desire is there, nagging. It wants to be seen, it wants to be heard, it wants to be included in the conversation. And I find that the more you include desire, the more easily you start taking action in your life towards what you want, and the more you create a life that you truly desire.

I’ve been talking about desire a lot because I just, I don’t have anything on my calendar anymore that I don’t desire. Team meetings, podcasts, classes, emails, like anything. There’s nothing on my calendar that I don’t desire. So I never have to use self-discipline. So when I take action from desire, then I’m not working against myself. I’m not using willpower. I’m not using discipline. I’m not disciplining myself.

And when I make decisions and I move towards my desires decisively, then I create a life that I truly, unbelievably desire. I get all the things I want. And that’s I know what you want, and that’s what I know your clients want. So the secret sauce is just paying attention, giving the desire the same amount of voice that you give the lack of desire or the stuckness, or the no’s, or the this is why I wouldn’t. Just give it 50% airtime. It will change your life. You’ll be absolutely shocked at what will happen when you start listing out why you would do something.

Go to why you would go to the networking event, why you would join the course, why you would, whatever it is, say yes to the coaching that you’ve been given and do the thing, why you would start the podcast, why you would, you know, market this thing that you’ve had an idea to market forever. That’s another thing when I’m in 200k, I’m coaching a lot of people, and they’re like, I’ve been thinking about doing this forever, but here are all the reasons why I wouldn’t. And I’m like, okay, let’s talk about all the reasons why you would. And I get people off the fence so fast with that question for everything.

Try it on. Just this week, everything you’re on the fence with, list out your desires, see what happens. And then like, tell me about it. I would love to know. It’s a powerful exploration. But we’ve got to get you off the fence. You can’t have any of that energy and be selling coaching at the same time because you won’t be able to help people off the fence for themselves, but also you won’t be in your full coach energy because coaches get people off the fence. It’s what we do.

All right, have an amazing week. I am so excited to be talking to you. I have a lot of amazing podcasts planned out coming up that I think are going to be so valuable. So I’m so excited to get back in the recording studio and be knocking these out for you all. I will see you next week. Have a beautiful one. Bye-bye.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2k for 2k program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2Kfor2K. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #341: Am I Fooling Myself?
transcript:
Welcome to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2k, $20K, and $200K using her proven formula.

Hey coaches, welcome to episode 341. Today we’re going to talk about the answer to the question, am I fooling myself? So I’m going to give you a little background. I just finished call two, technically call three. So call three, but lesson two of my newest entrepreneur series, ROI, Return on Investment. And one of the things about that you have to know about the entrepreneur series is this is a place for me to come and express my creativity and have no rules or regulations for myself and immerse myself in teaching and coaching on a topic.

And we even have this on the sales page. The calls are 90 minutes, but sometimes we go over. And I just did a two-hour and 10-minute call. I was actually surprised when I looked at the time. I was like, oh, shit. I went a little over. But it was so amazing. I taught for the first 90 minutes, and then I coached for another hour and 10 minutes. And I got through several people. It was so amazing, and each person brought something that added to the conversation that wasn’t planned or that was a reinforcement of the conversation or a different angle of the conversation. And so I really love to include that.

And so on the very final person who raised their hand, the question came up. Actually, this happened in two of the coachings. So two of the people mentioned, am I fooling myself when it comes to my business and when it comes to investments? So am I fooling myself that I could be as successful as I imagine myself to be? I have this version of myself that I see that could be really successful, but am I fooling myself to believe I’m capable of that? Or am I fooling myself when I sign up for this thing that I could actually accomplish this result?

And I think this is really important to talk about. And so I want to share some of the things that I shared with this student at the end of the call because I want to share it for the students who are in ROI because maybe you won’t get that far into the call and you might miss it. But for those of you that aren’t in it, I also still want to bring you along. Even if you aren’t in it, I want you to experience some of the wisdom from it. And I do think that as entrepreneurs, I think we do run into this. I think that especially in the beginning, when you have a dream, any dream, any vision of a bigger life for yourself, it’s very common to ask, am I fooling myself with this?

And then especially when you start pouring money into it, and especially if you aren’t immediately creating returns, and then other people might also question if you’re fooling yourself. And so I think this is a really important topic, and I’m going to cover it in four different angles or with four different angles. So the first thing I told my, or one of the things that I told my student, is there is a difference between – I think it’s a framing, right? I don’t think it’s the right question. So am I fooling myself is one question that has a bunch of possible answers, but I think the better question is, am I finding what I’m capable of with no regrets?

Because I actually think that’s what we’re doing when we go for a dream. If we have a dream and we want to accomplish something or become someone that’s very different than who we are, you could be, quote unquote, fooling yourself to what you’re capable of, and that could feel really scary and terrible and like you don’t have a grasp on reality. Like I think that’s what the question creates for us, is a belief that we don’t have a real grasp on reality. And the moment, I don’t know about you, but the moment that I think I don’t have a grasp on reality, I feel very scared.

This is why I can’t do any sort of, I don’t smoke pot, I don’t do any of the things that would ever take, I don’t even like to be drunk. I don’t do anything that takes me out of my brain because the moment I think I’m like, reality is distorted, there’s something about it that creates a lot of anxiety for me. It’s like the opposite of what it’s supposed to do for maybe for those of you that do engage in gummies or smoking pot of some sort. It’s like the opposite. That does not, it’s not what happens for me. I’ve experienced, that’s not what it is.

So for me, I like to be very rooted in reality. And I think that it can feel very scary to think that there’s a version, like there’s a possibility in the world that you could be looking at a skewed version of reality and then acting into that skewed version, and then investing into that skewed version, and it’s a place that you could easily spiral and that other people could also easily pull you into and make you really question what’s real and what’s not.

And so I think that the framing of the question or the framing of the statement matters because one is rooted in, I’m not sure if I’m understanding reality correctly, and the other is rooted in the more accurate statement, which is if I’m going for a dream, if I’m going for a bigger vision of myself, if I am wanting to have a much bigger reality in life and achieve a dream, then where I’m at now, the only way to get there is to find out if I’m capable.

And I personally, I was telling another client on this call, for me, when I first started investing in my business, I had a very big dream for myself, a very different reality. And it would have been easy to say that I was fooling myself from where I was with the circumstances I started out with, right?
 

I didn’t have lots of money. I didn’t have a house. I was living in an apartment and living kind of paycheck to paycheck and a terrible relationship. There was nothing that said I was going to become a multi-millionaire in this lifetime. And yet, I’d had a dream my whole life to become a multi-millionaire and I’d had a dream since I was in high school to become an entrepreneur. I started my first business when I was 17 years old, when I was still in high school. Isn’t that crazy?

And so I was telling them that I had no money really to invest. And so investing, when you have no money to invest is like, I have no money, and now I’m going to the bottom of the barrel of having no money. And what that looks like is I’m selling all of my things in order to invest in my business, and I’m cashing out the $5,000 IRA that I, it took me like six years to build or seven years to build $5,000 in an IRA, and I’m cashing that out and taking a $1,200 penalty in order to use some of that money to invest in myself. So now I have no furniture and I’ve sold my clothes and I’ve cashed out my IRA and I’ve worked extra hours. That’s like bottom of the barrel broke, right?

And so it would have been really easy for me to think I’m recklessly spending all this money, fooling myself that this version of my life and dreams is possible. But what I told myself instead is, I don’t want to live with regret. I don’t want to get to the end of my life and think that maybe I could have done something different and didn’t. And I’m willing to risk all of this money to find out, to find out what I’m capable of, to see if I could really do it.

I coached a student earlier before this moment where I said, if you take all the action and you actually implement in your business and you actually use the investments that you invest, because she’d invested a lot of money and not used the investments. And so I said, if you actually used them, and the reason she didn’t use them is because she was afraid I might, I might actually get to the end of the using and find out I’m not capable, that I’ve been fooling myself. And I said, okay, so how would that feel? And she’s like, “Terrible, awful. So horrible.” And she’s crying and telling me that she feels terrible and awful and horrible now.

And I said, okay, so the only difference is, if you’re truly not capable, which I don’t agree with, but if you truly weren’t capable, the only difference is right now, you’re feeling terrible and awful and you have regrets. But at the end, you’ll feel terrible and awful and you’ll have no regrets. And I actually think that’s a better way to live. It’s a better way to live to say I really tried for this and I didn’t make it happen.
 

This is the way I think about Olympic athletes or, you know, people who want to be in the Hall of Fame, but they don’t quite make it. If they’re, you know, playing at this highest level, like if it’s a golfer but they never win a major tournament or, you know, you want to become an Olympic athlete but you never make the team, if you, like things like that where it’s like, you spend your whole life trying for something, there will be times where you don’t actually achieve the thing. Like not everyone’s going to make $100 million.

I was telling them like, since I’ve become a mom, I’m like, am I really going to make a, create a $20 million business in one year? Like am I going to build it to be $20 million? Maybe after they go to school. I don’t know. Like I’ve been thinking about that. Like what it would take. Like I don’t want regrets with my family. I’d rather have regrets with my business than my family. And but I’m also willing to work really hard and see if I’m capable of doing both and getting to $20 million. But the thing that feels the most painful is actually the regrets, not the no regrets. So I’d rather find out and have no regrets that I couldn’t do it than to not find out and have regrets and wonder if I could have. I think one feels so much worse.

So I was telling her, I think she’s capable. I think everyone’s capable of creating a business. Will we all do it? No. Will we all get over the hardships and the frictions and the obstacles? Will we all grow the emotional resilience and the mental stamina to be able to do it? Maybe not. Will we all invest enough to make it happen? Will we all make choices that make it happen? Maybe not. But you have to make a decision. It’s not, am I fooling myself? There is a reality in which you could fool yourself. It’s just, am I finding what I’m capable of with no regrets? Like do I want to find out if I could actually do it and then not live with regrets? That’s the more accurate statement.

But then, the second thing that I told my students is it’s not that you either have capability or not. Like you either inherently have it or you don’t. It’s either you have it or you develop it or you choose not to develop it. That’s it. That’s the actual neutral truth of the matter. I either have the capability or I don’t, and then I either develop it or I choose not to. Like I have the capability currently or I don’t. Most of us start a business without the capability right now to have a business. If we had the capability, we’d have the business. So we don’t have the capability.

So then it becomes, do I develop it or do I not develop it? That’s the only question. Again, it’s not I’m fooling myself to believe I’m capable or not. It’s I’m choosing to develop it or not. And I’m going to need to tell myself the truth of if I’m willing to feel the hard to develop it or not.

My final client that I coached, she said, “Stacy, when I got into this business 10 years ago, everybody was just saying how easy it is.” And she’s like, “Where have you been?” And I said, “Where was this message?” I said, “Listen, I’ve been saying that it’s hard for the last 10 years.” I feel like I’ve been that coach that has talked about the hard stuff and helped my clients be willing to do the hard things, right?
 

Maybe she didn’t find me 10 years ago, but I feel like I’ve been saying it for 10 years. It’s not that we’re capable or not. It’s just am I willing to feel the hardness to develop the capability or not? Am I willing to feel the discomfort to develop the capability or not? Am I willing to keep going until I develop the capability or not?

And for me, it’s like the time is going to pass anyways, so I might as well try. And for me, the fun thing is like, with my big goals, like $20 million for example, the thing is, how can I stretch my brain to maintain my family priorities and develop my skill sets to be so that I could actually have a $20 million business and maintain my priorities? I feel like that’s just a skill set. And so I am willing, like if I’m going to pass the time anyways. I’m going to be working anyway, so why don’t I try for the thing? Again, I’m willing to get to the end and find out that I didn’t do it or that I couldn’t do it for whatever reason and have no regrets.

But I don’t think they couldn’t do it is inherent. I think it’s like, will I find out that I just don’t want it? Once you decide to create a dream, then you find out what the dream costs, and then you have to decide if you still want it from there.
 

And I do think that a lot of entrepreneurs go through this, which is why they quit, because they decide to become entrepreneurs, maybe they even make some money in entrepreneurship, but then they find out how hard it is to maintain entrepreneurship or to create money in entrepreneurship, and they decide, I don’t want to do the thing that it costs. Like I don’t want the cost of this. And that’s an honest conversation. You’re either willing to pay the cost or you’re not. You’re willing to go through the hard thing and develop it or not.

Now, I want to also say for some of you that might be like, maybe I’m just not willing. I would question that. I would question it a lot because I think it’s actually harder to not go through the hard stuff and develop competence and capability. I think it’s actually harder to not do that than to do it. It feels unfamiliar and uncomfortable, but it’s an easier life to operate with 100% capability than it is to operate life feeling not capable of the things that you want.
 

The experience of your life is much different when you tell yourself you’re not capable and you can’t do something that you really deeply want to do. It’s like there’s a dream inside of you and you are snuffing it out. And that experience daily, I think is much harder than just doing the thing and getting over the hardship of the thing.

So the third thing that I told my client, because one of the examples she gave is that she’s invested a lot of money. She lives in a different country than the US and what she believes a specific way to build a business in the country that she lives in. And she’s been sold that theory a lot. And one of the theories is that you have to be on Instagram and you have to be doing all the tactics correctly, and you have to be implementing exactly to get the visibility, and you have to have a beautiful website and ads and funnels and all the technological things.

And so she was talking about, I have this potential to make this investment with a coach that I really respect, and he says that I could go global if I implement this strategy. And she said, “But I’m wondering if I’m fooling myself because I know that what I’m still struggling with is local. Like if I can’t make it work local, how am I going to make it work global? Am I fooling myself?” And I said, “This is because we’re having a conversation about investing and creating radical returns, one of the things that I do think is really important when you’re thinking of making an investment is, do I believe I can do this thing?”

There’s a difference between I don’t believe that I can do this thing at all, but this person believes so much in me that I trust that they’re going to make it happen for me. Like their belief and what their process is, they’re going to do the work for me, so I don’t need to believe in me because I’m not doing the work, they’re doing the work.
 

One of my students, I think she asked at the very end, how do you know if something’s a bad risk or a good risk? Like if entrepreneurship is risky, how do you know if it’s a good risk or a bad risk? And I told her, I think it’s a bad risk when you have no belief that you could do the thing, and then someone sells you their grand vision because – not from a negative place, but because they believe anybody could do it, but you have no belief in yourself and you think that the thing is going to happen because they’re going to do it for you.

It’s like they’re going to create the grand vision. I’m not going to have to do it. And I think that’s where we make mistakes in investing versus do I lean towards this investment because I recognize that there is some version of belief in me that thinks I could do this thing? That’s like sometimes you do it when, you know, that might be like a scarier investment, maybe your first investment.
 

I know for sure, for me, when I made my first investment, I was very scared. Like can I do this thing? But there was also a version of me that believed I could do this thing. And then as I got more experience and made bigger and bigger investments, it became, I do believe I can do something with this investment and this is what I’m going to do with this investment.

And if you are thinking about a $10,000 investment, a $20,000 investment, a $50,000 investment, whatever amount of money is a really big amount of money for you, you have to have some belief that you are going to be the one doing the work and that you are going to create it for yourself. And if you don’t have any of that belief, I wouldn’t do it. And I would work on developing that belief first, however you can, with their free content, with their smaller paid offers, anything that you can do to develop that belief in yourself.

I also asked her, is there something smaller and more tangible that you could believe instead? Like if there’s a business strategy you’re looking for, instead of shooting for the moon, which is what gives her the feeling of she’s fooling herself. I told her, I was like, a lot of the coaches come into the industry and what we think is the way that you need to market your business from the very beginning is ads and funnels and all of these complicated systems because it’s the only thing you see marketed to you. But that’s because it’s actually the top 1%, 5% of coaches that are making multiple millions of dollars, that’s because that’s how they market. They’re paying to push that advertising out to you. So that’s what you’re seeing the most of.

But it’s not actually the reality of how most coaches make their money, which is not spending hundreds of thousands of dollars on ads. So I call that the 1% marketing funnel because the 1% or the top 5% are the ones that are doing that marketing funnel, and the 95% of other coaches have figured out other ways to market themselves that are less grand. They’re smaller, they’re more tangible, like organic marketing, meeting people, telling them you’re a life coach, offering to help them, right? Like that, there’s 95% of the coaches are making money doing that.

So when you’re thinking about I’m going to invest in my business in a strategy, does that strategy feel tangible to me? Does it feel like it’s something attainable that I could do? Do I believe I could meet people, tell them I’m a life coach, and offer to help them? And if I, if I can’t believe that, then I need to join Stacey’s entrepreneur series to develop that belief, and maybe that’s where I start with a smaller investment.
 

But if I have no belief whatsoever that I’m going to be able to put an ad together and put a funnel together and go sell it online, then I probably shouldn’t spend $20,000 from a coach telling me that I could and me thinking they’re going to do the work for me because they won’t be doing the work. You will be doing the work.

So I asked her, how can she meet herself where she’s currently at with her current capability to take small tangible actions to then grow into maybe that grander vision? But it can’t just be I’m making this decision solely 100% based on someone else’s belief in me. Am I, am I fooling myself? That part could be, am I being honest with myself that I don’t believe this at all? Or the fourth part of this is, am I listening to myself?

Because I told her, I was like, you know, we all have very innate wisdom inside of us. And her wisdom said, if I can’t do it locally, what makes me think I can do it globally? And I was like, I think that’s actually a really smart statement to recognize that if I’m struggling to do it on the small scale, I probably am not going to just magically do it on the grand scale. And so I’m fooling myself. She was like, “He’s fooling me.” And she’s like, “No, no, no, I’m fooling myself.” And I’m like, that’s the more responsible place to be. That’s the place where you own your decisions around investments, is I’m letting myself be fooled. I’m fooling myself by attaching to this grand vision because I believe somehow the grander vision will be easier than the smaller vision.

Like I have people tell me all the time that they’re like, 100%, I can make 100K. I totally believe that. And I’m like, “Could you make 2K today?” “Absolutely not.” Well, if you can’t believe you can make 2K today, you’re not going to actually do what it takes to make 100K. This is one of the biggest things that we turn people away for with my 200K Mastermind. They’re in my 200K, or they’re in my 2K for 2K, and they’re working to believe that they could make 20K, but they’re not there yet. They’re at 5K or 10K or 8K. And they’re like, but I know I’m capable of so much more. Well, if that’s true, let’s make that money in 2K for 2K. And then 200K Mastermind becomes a natural fit.

But sometimes people think 200K Mastermind is going to be the answer. It’s going to help, it’s going to give me something that I’m not getting now. It’s going to do the work for me. It’s going to be the miracle or the magic. It’s the grander thing. It’s more exciting. It seems more fun, all of the things. The grand thing is always going to feel more fun than the tangible thing, always.
 

But the tangible thing is what keeps us moving forward and growing our capability. The grander the vision becomes, the grander the actions have to become, and then you actually lose your belief more because you can’t find a tangible thing to start, right? If you’re like, I’m going to go from zero to 100K, well, how the hell do I do that?

The steps are so big. I’m going to have to create a funnel. I’m going to have to start running ads. I’m going to have to spend money. I’m going to have to have the perfect messaging. I’m going to have to know my client avatar. Oh, wait, I don’t know any of these things. Or I could just go online or get out of my house and meet someone and introduce myself and start a conversation and tell them I’m a life coach and pique curiosity for people until someone says, I might be able to use you. And then you say, for sure, I can help you. That’s tangible. That’s smaller. You could imagine yourself doing it.

So then it becomes less about I’m fooling myself and more about am I just going to do that or not? Am I willing to do that uncomfortable thing in order to create the results that I want in order to live without regrets? Am I willing to do that or not? That’s it. That’s the whole thing. So we can root ourselves in reality and not fear that we’re getting sucked into some alternate version of reality and not getting sucked into believing something that’s not possible for you. Is instead just reframing it to, I’m finding what I’m capable of because I don’t want to live with regrets. And if I’m starting out, I probably don’t have the capability yet, but I’m deciding to develop it.

And I’m going to stick with that failure after failure, time after time, and how I know I’m not fooling myself is by evaluating and extracting value and failure gold from each failed attempt, tracking my progress, seeing myself change little by little by little, paying attention to that so that I see I actually am more capable today than I was yesterday, seeing my emotional muscle grow, seeing things that used to freak me out no longer freak me out, seeing things I used to do terribly, now I’m actually having positive reactions from it. I’m actually gaining traction here. That’s how we do it. One little moment at a time.

I hope this was helpful. I know it can be really scary to feel like maybe you are not rooted in reality. But the other alternative is, are you fooling yourself that this is all you’re capable of? Are you fooling yourself that this is the life you’re meant to live? Are you fooling yourself that you’re not stronger, that you’re not more capable, that you can’t do bigger things? Maybe that’s the fooling yourself. How do we know? We really want to go down a rabbit hole. I’d rather just decide I’m moving forward and I’m figuring out how to be capable so that I never have to live with regrets. And even if I don’t get the ultimate goal that I want, I will still have the experience of no regrets. For me, that is everything.

All right, I hope you have an amazing week. I hope this was super helpful. If you’re in ROI, I will see you on Monday. And if not, maybe I’ll be dropping some more nuggets like this as we go. I love you all. I will talk to you soon. Bye-bye.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2k for 2k program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2kfor2k. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #340: How to Empower Clients to Invest in Coaching
transcript:
Welcome 
to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2k, $20K, and $200K using her proven formula.

Hello, hello! I am so excited to chat with everyone today, my Facebook audience. I love you all so much. I didn’t even for the longest time do live streams and engage with my Facebook business page audience, and it’s been so fun to do that. In the last six or eight months, I’ve been live streaming a lot more than ever before and to be able to give messages and share things that I’m thinking about with you all and to commune in this way.

So, if you are just finding me, my name is Stacey Boehman. I am a Master Certified Life Coach, and I help coaches make money. And today, we’re going to actually talk about women, specifically, making money and being in their power when it comes to business.

I help coaches make their first $2000 and then $20,000. And then I have a 200k Mastermind where I help them make their first $200,000, and then I have a 2 Million Dollar Group where I help them make the first two million dollars. Y’all see how I love the twos?

And then I also have a brand new series called the Entrepreneur Series, and that is, this is my tenth year in business. And this series has been dedicated to the wisdom that I have collected and accumulated in my brain over the last ten years and selling $40 million of coaching, more than $40 million of coaching at this point. And so there’s a lot of wisdom.

So we have done courses on, and really the other piece of the Entrepreneur Series is I found that coaches come into the industry and they have this beautiful coach heart and they want to serve people, and they have no idea how to be an entrepreneur, and no one’s really taught them. And so the Entrepreneur Series is my collection of wisdom after ten years combined with helping my coaches become better entrepreneurs.

And so we’ve done one on staying in service energy even when you’re trying to make specific amounts of money. And we’ve done one on, I called it “Alive,” and it was really about triumphing over every challenge that comes your way in entrepreneurship. And we did one on capacity work and increasing your intellectual, your emotional, and your physical capacity. And now the next Entrepreneur Series course is ROI, creating a return on investments that you make for your coaching business.

No one’s ever taught this before. Have you guys ever thought, have you thought about this, why? It’s so crazy to me. Why is there no teaching on creating returns for your investments? This has blown my mind since I started the industry. Every time I would join containers, no one was talking about making your money back. And I created that as my core, one of the core philosophies in my containers when you come into my programs, the first thing we do is make your money back.

You join 2k for 2k, we do that in the first thirty days. If you join 200k Mastermind, I have a 25k in 30 Day Challenge, and you do the challenge at any revenue, but at least $10k. That’s what the investment is or typically has been. And we work on that return right away. All of my programs, it’s like, have you made your money back? That language is throughout my programs because I noticed that no one was ever holding people, not accountable, but having the standard of that.

And so it’s really easy to invest a lot of money in the coaching industry specifically, not talking about stock markets, I’m not talking about real estate. It’s really easy to invest a lot of money in the coaching industry and not be aware of how much you’re putting in and aware of how much you’re getting back, or specifically work towards creating returns every single time. And I was forced to do this because I joined the industry and I had no money.

So I couldn’t just frivolously put $2k here and $10k here and $20k there and $25k there and I couldn’t do that, $6k there. I couldn’t do that because every dollar I was spending was money I should be paying bills with, basically, in the beginning. And so I had to be, I’m signing up for this, and then I’m creating money in this way. This is how I’m paying for it. This is how I’m creating a return. And I just noticed no one was ever talking about it.

And even for me, I’ve been talking about it a lot in my ten years and in all of my containers, but I’ve never actually taught a course to my students on how to create returns. I have seen people do a hundred consults, and they’re amazing coaches, and the people say, “This was so valuable,” and they still don’t buy. And there’s just something about, it’s an intangible thing that if you don’t have the experience of having paid money for coaching and invested in yourself time and time again because you see the value of coaching over and over and over, then it becomes very difficult to sell it to other people because you’re just not a product of your product. You’re like, “I have lots of experience, but I’ve never been coached. I don’t coach. I’m not looking to spend money on coaching.” Then you’re not going to find people looking to spend money on coaching either. It’s just an energetic match that doesn’t happen.

“Even if I spend $12k on a program and never cracked it open.” So if you spent $12k on a program and never cracked it open, that is disempowerment around investing, and we will fix it. We will talk about it. There’s been one time where I did not do a program and I left, and it actually created such a transformation that I immediately did a $100,000 launch, but it was very intentional and I was very empowered around the decision. But if you spend $12k on a program and you don’t do it and you’re disempowered, then that starts bleeding into everything you’re selling from that moment on.

Stephanie, “Is this best for beginner coaches or how would this benefit established coaches who are regularly investing in their business?” I think it’s for everyone that’s spending money in their business. If you’re not creating ridiculous returns that blow your mind every single time, you want to be in this program. And if you’re not good at helping other people do it, you want to be in this program. So the two things that have made my career what it has been and created $40 million is how the returns that I get for myself and then the returns that I’ve helped my clients get.

Like we, my 200k Mastermind has been running since 2019, and last year we did a data study on 650 students that came through that room. It was a self-reported data study. So they would apply and on their application tell us how much money they had made in the last six months, in the last twelve months, and then we track their revenue as part of our program every month to see, again, because I believe so much in creating returns, I’m always paying attention to my students’ returns and having them pay attention to their returns. And we collected all that data over a six-year period and created an algorithm to produce a study on that data. And one of the things that we found is my students, on average, were growing beyond hypergrowth.

So they consider hypergrowth in the business world 40% growth, and that’s over a year period. My students were coming in and growing at a median growth rate of 48% in a six-month period, which is almost 100% annualized, which is really unheard of. And so there’s something about when you understand how to create massive returns for yourself, not just returns, returns that would make you keep investing.

This is how you know. If you’re an experienced investor and you’ve invested and you constantly make investments, how empowered do you feel? How amazing do you feel? And do you have such big returns that you are always lining up the next investment? And there would never be a time where you were taking a break or not investing in yourself.

I’m going on maternity leave. I still am paying my business coach because I am a CEO who will still be running a business on maternity leave, and I pay $11,000 for every single call that I do, for a ninety-minute call, $11,000 every time. But I turn that $11,000 into hundreds of thousands of dollars every single time. I can track it. I can see the return from each and every conversation and how it shows up in my selling, my delivering, my managing of my business. I see it everywhere. So this isn’t just if you’ve never created a return, it really is like my ultimate goal for all of you would be that you are so good at creating returns that you would always be investing in your business, always be massively growing, and hitting more higher and higher levels of success. Don’t we all want that? That’s what I want for you. That’s my goal.

Teresa, “Investing in myself is simply a necessary part of owning a business.” Yeah, and aggressively investing. Now, I’m not going to sell you aggressive investments. It’s not about that. So it’s not going to be like, “Come to this real estate conference and then give me $250,000.” Someone was just telling me about that recently. My, one of my doctors had that experience recently.

But whatever you do want to invest in the future, I want you to feel so empowered with it, whether it’s with me in one of my programs or someone else. I really have a genuine belief that the more coaches invest in themselves and create returns from coaching, the more value you get from coaching, the more you then help other people say yes to themselves to get coaching, the higher that then the more your people get results and value from coaching, the more they tell other people about their results and their experience and how amazing it was, and then the more their people who hear about it decide to get coached.

And suddenly, now the value of the reputation of the entire coaching industry increases, and then the buyer pool of people interested in coaching and feeling safe to buy coaching, that also increases. And so I think it’s for you, it’s for your clients, but it’s also for the entire industry. And our, the value of our industry, the reputation of our industry, and then increasing the buyer pool of our industry by people getting high returns, both coaches and clients. That is the goal.

And then if you think about that, if every client and every coach is getting massive returns for everything that they do and more people are getting coached, it’s like the world really does start changing. I know that’s a big vision for some people to grasp onto in the beginning, but I’ve been doing this for ten years, and this is some of the things I think about. It matters to me. I think that’s how we change the world, is one person getting coached at a time.

All right, I got to jump off here. I love you all so much. I will see you all on Monday.

Hey, if you’re ready to make money as a life coach, I want to invite you to join my 2K for 2K program; where you’re going to make your first $2,000 the hardest part using my simple five-step formula for getting consults and closing new clients. Just head over to StaceyBoehman.com/2Kfor2K. We’ll see you inside.

title: Ep #339: ROI
transcript:
Welcome 
to the 
Make Money as a Life Coach
®
 
podcast
 
where sales expert and Master Coach Stacey Boehman teaches you how to make your first $2K, $20K, and $200K using her proven formula.

Hello, hello. It is time to reveal the new Entrepreneur Series coming to you. I have been dreaming of this next course that I’m going to be releasing as part of the Entrepreneur Series. I have been feeling in my soul the importance of this work and how badly coaches need this work. And it has never been done before, ever. At least that I’m aware of. I do not know that there’s a single course or program or anywhere that you could go to learn what I’m going to teach in this next Entrepreneur Series course.

So, if you are live, before I dive in, I would just love to know and hear if you have done any of my Entrepreneur Series courses. Like, are you finding me for the first time? And so I need to back up a little bit? Are you, you know, in my world, and you were in Served or you were in Capacity Work? I would love for you to comment below and tell me which one you joined in on, or if you’ve done them all, maybe you’ve done them all. This one is going to be very unique and different than all of the Entrepreneur Series before.

And I will explain why, but I am just curious for those of you that are on, what your familiarity is, and I might start there. This one is needed. It’s just needed. And I don’t typically sell things that are like needed, but this one is needed. And I also think it will be highly desired, but I also think it’s really risky, and there is a reason no one has tackled this topic before. And I also don’t think that the reasons why, I’ve explored why I think that there isn’t more education, knowledge, coaching on this topic. I’ve explored why I think that is, and I’m going to tell you a little bit about it. And it just doesn’t feel like a good reason for me to not do this one.

These are all limited courses. You right now, as of now, you can’t go back, like you can’t just purchase them anytime. They’re only available when I do them live for a very limited time. And so we open access, we do the live training, there’s a little bit extra access at the end to catch up on replays, and then we close it completely. It’s the only way I can make the series at the price points that I have them, and make them so available to everyone and so accessible is because they’re so limited. And they’re not like in, I don’t know what the word is, chronological order, I don’t think is the right word, but maybe it is. Like, if you do them all, the more you do them, I do think it compounds your mindset.

And so I do have students that will tell me what I learned in Served, or what I learned in Alive, or what I learned in Capacity Work. But they’re all very just different subjects. So, let me just start with this, and I’ll be brief. But the Entrepreneur Series, I created it because I realized, I’ve been coaching for the last 10 years, and for the last 8, 7, 8, since 2017, 2018, I’ve been coach, 2018. Since 2018, I have been coaching exclusively coaches making money. And so all of my containers have been, and this is going to matter for this conversation too, they have all been, I did something that when I decided to help coaches make money, I decided to do something that no one had ever really done in the industry, not at the way that I did it, where I took all of my programs, my three core offers, and I made them specific to revenue.

And the reason I did that is because I was in a lot of coaching containers. And one of the things, I always get what I came for, but one of the things that I noticed is that there was a lot of people that were able to kind of hang out in containers and there was no like pressure or, not even pressure is not the right word, but no standard to make money. There was no standard for income. So I would go to, you know, very expensive retreats looking to mingle with other millionaires, and there would be people who had never made a dollar. And I would go to events where we would, they would be very business-focused, and it would be the same people every event, but they were never actually building their business.

And when you’re making a lot of money, like you want to be in a room where other people are making lots of money. And when you’re, like you just want to be around people who are making money, and the more people who are building a hobby business or what I found was like people were wanting to have businesses, but because there was no standard or accountability to make money, it was really easy to keep investing and spending money and be in containers to have the dream of one day having a business without the difficulty, the pain, the growth of actually having to build the business, right? So you could be in containers endlessly and feel really great about coaching and really great about the community and really happy to be there and feel like you’re getting a lot, but never actually create any sort of movement.

And I wanted to create movement, and I felt like the only way to create movement was to have containers that had set amount of revenues where that was the focus, where we created money. So my first program, 2k for 2k, was all about new coaches coming in and making their first $2k. And then making $10k, and then $20k. And then I created a 200k Mastermind. Yes, it’s a girls’ trip. Yes, that is how it felt. I never wanted my containers to feel like a girls’ trip, which means they don’t always feel like rainbows and daisies and fucking butterflies, but also my people get results.

So I wanted that container where people could come in and learn to make their money. And then I created the 200k Mastermind. And then there was a revenue requirement for that, where we didn’t let people in until they had made at least $25,000 of revenue. And we went all the way up to $200k earners. And then I created the 2 Million Dollar Group, and you had to have made at least $200,000 of revenue to be in that room. And then each room had a focus on creating money.

Like we talk every day in my 2k for 2k program about making $2k. We talk every day in my 200k Mastermind about making $200k. We actually revenue track. So every month people post what their revenue is and we actually attack the thoughts. Like we do thought work on how much money they’ve made. Like, we really do focus on doing the thing and creating the thing.

And so that was really important to me because I just didn’t see it being done anywhere and being done well. People would, you know, even if there was a container to help make six figures, if someone didn’t get results, they would just let them keep enrolling time and time and time again. Whereas if you come into one of my, like my 200k Masterminds, and you don’t create the minimum revenue by the end of the round, I don’t let you return. And not because I don’t love my people or because I don’t want to support them, but because I don’t want them to overinvest. I don’t want them to keep doing something that isn’t working, whether it’s for them or in the room or whatever the reason, it can be so nuanced as to the reason, but like I just don’t let people keep investing without actually doing the work to produce the revenue.

And that was sort of revolutionary for the industry. People hadn’t been doing that. No one had been accountable to creating money. No one had held their students in a standard for getting returns on investment. Like no one had been doing that. And it felt really important to me, not just for the community space and for the way people interact together, but for the students and for the coach, like let’s actually do this thing instead of having a girls’ weekend or instead of dreaming about doing the thing, like let’s actually do it.

And then after 8 years of being in containers, where we’re very focused on creating money, one of the things I realized is that my students were starting to lack mindset and things that made making money a lot easier. I give them the strategy of marketing and selling, and delivering, and I give them the mindset of that, but we don’t really go into the what I realized is there is a specific mindset you have with being an entrepreneur that isn’t taught anywhere, really. And I find that a lot of people who are coaches who come into the industry are not, maybe not natural entrepreneurs.

People who are wanting to be coaches, maybe they’re natural healers, maybe they’re natural wisdom seekers and wisdom providers, sages, like just like really people who work in the emotional realms. They’re intuitive, they’re interested in serving people, and they have this coach heart that’s so beautiful. And they just want to help people get results.

And so there’s, we decide to become coaches, and we want to help people, and that’s the thing that gets us into the coaching industry, is we want to help people. And then we’re suddenly entrepreneurs without realizing it. And entrepreneurship is a really hard game. It requires a very like steel mindset to survive in entrepreneurship. There’s a reason most businesses don’t survive past the first 5 years. If you look at brick and mortar businesses, just all businesses, because it’s a grind. It’s hard. It’s the highest level of mindset and skill set required. If everybody could do it, everybody would be doing it.

And I’ve had a lot of success helping coaches become great entrepreneurs in my core containers. But I wanted to have some containers where I could look at some pieces of the entrepreneur mindset that maybe people were missing. And so that’s where Served came, and then that’s where Capacity Work came, and Alive, and we did a revenue challenge, which was more of an advanced Entrepreneur Series course. And so this series is really filling the gaps that I think people are missing to help them integrate all of entrepreneurship at a deeper level and have more success with it.

And so when I started out, I was thinking about, like what are we missing when it comes to entrepreneurship? What is the mindset required aside from coaching and aside from making money? What is that’s missing? And this question has, every answer has been a course. So this answer that came for me very early on, actually. I’ve had this answer for a long time, but I knew that I wanted to do some other ones first, but this one feels like a really big one, is when I think about what’s missing for people in the mindset of an entrepreneur, one of the biggest gaps is the mindset of being an investor, of knowing how to be a really good investor.

When you decide to become a coach, whether you realize it or not, unless you decide to get hired by someone else and work for them, which is still going to work for someone else. If you want to work for yourself, you are inevitably an entrepreneur. And then the moment you become an entrepreneur, you inevitably become an investor. So, whether you realize it or not, the moment you decide I want to become a life coach, I want to get paid, and I want to work for myself, you’re becoming a coach, you’re becoming an entrepreneur. You’re also becoming a leader, but you’re also becoming an investor.

And this is the one area where coaches struggle the most, the investment piece. It’s different than anything, it’s not the same as spending money. Investing money is not the same as spending money. But investing in coaching or things for your business are also not the same as investing in the stock market or real estate. It’s a very specific mindset that makes someone really good at investing in coaching. And what makes someone really good at investing in coaching is the returns they get from the money they spend.

So to date, it’s almost impossible to come up with an actual, like specific, like this is the number, because I’ve been investing for so many years. But from the investments that I can remember, I’ve invested over $500,000 of my own personal cash into coaching, being coached. All kinds of coaching, mostly business coaching, but also my coach certification for my life coaching, all of the coaching, I’ve invested over $500,000 in the last 10 years. But I have turned that $500,000 into $40 million of sales. So I want you to think about my rate of return, $500,000 in, $40 million out. It’s a really big return.

And I have created this return, I believe with a very specific way that I approach the investments I make, how many I make, how often I make them, and what I do before I make them, and what I do immediately after I make them, and what I do the entire time that I’m in a coaching container, how I approach it, the way that I think. And what I know to be true is that the way that I think is very contrary to what the world, how the world thinks, especially when you think about consumerism. And if you think like a consumer and buy coaching like a consumer, it will not go well. It will not be great. It will not produce the type of returns that I have been getting and that I’ve been helping my clients get.

So it’s not just me that has created an insane return for the money that I’ve put in. But I’ve also done a data study on my 200k Mastermind students over the last, since 2019. That’s when I opened the doors of my 200k Mastermind. We did a data study. We had all of our students give us their current 12- and 6-month revenue as they applied, and then we tracked their revenue growth for every month that they were inside of our containers until they were not. And you can listen to the podcast. I have a podcast about it on the Make Money as a Life Coach podcast. They don’t do numbers, podcast numbers anymore for iTunes, but it’s called Proven Results and the 200k Mastermind Data Study.

But I reveal a lot of really incredible growth, proof of growth that happened in my room. And students getting a 48% return as the typical median result in their first round, which is more than hypergrowth. Students coming in at my $25k range of income, creating 248% growth in one round, 6 months. Insane results. The amount of, we’ve created over, I can’t remember the exact number, but 300 and something, six and multiple six figure earners from their investments.

So it’s not just that I have adopted a mindset that has created a huge return for me, but I subtly teach things here and there in my containers, in my 2k for 2k, in my 200k Mastermind, in all of my containers that help my students create returns as well. I focus on what I can control. I teach them on what they can control, but I also teach them how to think when they’re in containers to get the most out of the container. And a container is just what I mean, like a coaching, you know, whether it’s a mastermind or a one-on-one, like that’s a container, right? And so I’m always teaching them how to get the most out of it.

And so I’ve started compiling over the last many months all of the things that I know about investing, my processes, my mindset, the way that I handle when investments don’t go well, how I recover, how I, and in fact, I actually haven’t had, because of the way that I create value in my investments, I haven’t ever had one that I have a bad emotion, like that I have a negative emotion around or a bad experience around.

Like I know so many coaches have had really bad experiences putting money into coaching in this industry, and I don’t have any that I can report. But I do have a lot of value that I’ve taken from every container I’ve been in, and I really want to share this wisdom with my people because I want you to be able to have this as well.

One of the things that I, that has helped me grow the fastest, and people are always asking me, how did you grow so fast? How did you, like my first full year I made $150,000, my second year I made $325,000, and then my third year $860,000, and then I was in millions by my fourth year. And people are always asking, like how did you grow so fast?

And the answer is in the investment, the aggressive investing that I’ve done, and the aggressive returns that I’ve created. And I’m not afraid to invest, but because I have a really strong mindset and process around doing it. So I’m never like hemming and hawing about it. I’m never uncertain of myself about doing it. I don’t have to be worried about getting sold something and then not being good. I don’t have any of those thoughts. But I do have a very set of specific thinking that has really served me that I want to teach my people.

But when I first started marketing this, when I, the first couple of emails, I said that this was going to be a very risky course. And I want to tell you why I believe it’s going to be risky, and not for you, for me. It’s going to be risky for me. And this is why I think no one has ever done a course on how to invest in coaching and how to create returns of investments in coaching. The reason I believe no one has ever done this is because, there’s a few reasons. Number one, when you get to the level that I’m at, it’s very easy to diminish what I have to say about it by saying, yes, it must be nice though, you have millions of dollars. Of course, you can think that way.

Have you ever thought that? Have you ever had a thought like that? Oh, it’s really easy for them to think this. It’s really easy for them to make that investment. It’s really easy for them to do that. They have millions of dollars. The truth is, I’ve been investing like this since the very beginning.

And in this course, I’m going to break down some of my earliest investments and some of the trickiest things I had to navigate within those investments, and how I responded that created such big returns. So I have been thinking this way since the very first coach that I ever hired. I have had the thoughts that I’m going to share in the room. And I’m going to share my original stories because I think it’s so, I’m going to share some current ones too, but I think the original ones are the most impactful because I had two spoons when I first started the coaching industry.

I had no furniture. I had a tiny apartment. I had very little money to my name. I was a, basically a nomad selling mops in Walmart. And I had no business, according to anyone I knew, becoming a life coach, and definitely no business putting money into coaching over and over. So I think that my earliest stories and the things I learned from them are really the most powerful. But there is risk there because it could be so easy to diminish what I have to say just because of where I am now, not realizing that the mindset of investing is how I got here.

So that’s the first risk on me, not on you. But the second risk, which I think is even riskier, is that I sell coaching, and specifically, I sell business coaching. So I think it’s also really easy if someone’s selling coaching and selling business coaching to think, well, of course you think that. You sell this, right? Of course that you think people should do this. Of course, you think that this is the mindset. Of course, you approach it that way. Or you’re like in the industry. Have you heard that? Like, oh, they, she’s already drank the Kool-Aid. She’s in the industry.

And so I think it could be really easy if you had a really negative lens on investing in yourself and investing in coaching, it could be really easy to diminish or excuse away or find what I’m going to be teaching manipulative. And so I do think that is one of the reasons that there’s never been a course like this before. I’ve also spent a lot of time over the last few years talking to my millionaire colleagues in my masterminds and bringing up some of these things. I’ll bring up my mindset around things, and people will say, well, of course you have that. That’s why you make millions. Other people don’t think that way. That’s why they don’t make millions. 

And I’m like, yeah, but don’t you think we should teach people the conversations we’re having in these millionaire rooms? Don’t you think that this is the kind of conversation we should be having with people? And people always tell me, well, they’re not ready to hear it. People aren’t ready to hear it. I don’t believe that.

I have tested that with all of my Entrepreneur Series courses. In Capacity Work, I really taught some very confronting things for people to help them step in their power. And I found that people, everyone in the container, whether they’d not made any money or they’d made a ton of money, I found that they were all incredibly responsive and ready and hungry for the information and the conversation. They wanted it really bad. I have not found that yet for my people.

So I am hoping that we can have this conversation in the same way. I am hoping that we’re at a place and a time and a point where people are hungry to figure out how to make this less risky, how to be more empowered, how to put all of the power in the investor’s hands, how to create immense value and not ever have investor shame or regret or doubt and know that everything you do is in total alignment for who you are and the business you want to have and where you’re headed. I believe we want that.

What it’s going to take is a really hard conversation. I’m going to share some things that could potentially be very confronting. Because if you have past negative experiences with investing and you’re holding on to it as shame and anger at yourself or shame and anger at someone else, in order to become a powerful investor, you’re going to have to let that go. We’re going to have to work on that. We’re going to have to move through that. And in order to do that, you’re going to have to be wrong about the way that you think about things. You’re going to have to be wrong about a lot of the things that have been taught by society, and some of the things that you have maybe picked up along the way that are keeping you in consumerism instead of in being a great investor.

And so I think that this could be a confronting course. And I think every single coach should not spend another dollar on big investments in this industry or even smaller couple-thousand-dollar ones until you’ve taken this course. I think it will save you, I don’t even think I could put a number on it. The amount of money that you would save and the amount of money that you could make learning what I’m going to teach is going to be profound. There will be a before this course and an after this course with the empowerment that you feel in your business.

But the other most important thing is I also know, because my 2k for 2k program is very highly focused on getting consults and closing them. And the number one reason people don’t close them is they can’t overcome objections. The number one reason people can’t overcome objections is because they don’t have the investor mindset for coaching, and they can’t pass it on to other people. And so when other people are in consumerism, and when other people are not embodying their most highly resourced, powerful selves, resourceful selves, if you are not in that place as well, it will be really hard to speak to them about making investments in this way when they’ve never made an investment in coaching before.

And if you have fear about making investments in coaching that you could make a wrong one, if you have shame around investments that you’ve made in the past, and you have someone who is on the phone with you, afraid to make an investment, it does not matter what you say to them. The energetics of it will not have this person signing with you.

The reason I’m able to overcome objections so easily, and the reason I’m able to sell so much coaching is because my energetics around investing in coaching and what I believe about I put money in and this is what I get out.
